he realizes accordingly with wisdom that all phenomena enter into one and one enters into the manifold variety; he realizes accordingly with vast wisdom the entire dharma-realm;
he realizes accordingly with ultimate wisdom the entire realm of space; he realizes accordingly with wisdom that all worlds enter into the past; [and] one...
He attains the wisdom that realizes the entry of all worlds into the future; he attains the wisdom that realizes the entry of all worlds into the present;
and he attains the wisdom that realizes how the infinite practices and vows of all Tathāgatas are fully perfected within a single wisdom.
All Buddhas of the three periods of time are identical in their single practice, through which they attain liberation and follow the awakening of wisdom; this is the tenth.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will obtain the light of mastery over all dharmas, and all their vows will be fulfilled.
In a single moment of thought, they are able to fully comprehend all Buddha-dharmas and achieve equal and perfect enlightenment. O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva...
Bodhisattvas have ten kinds of realized knowledge. What are these ten? They are: knowing that all phenomena have a single characteristic; knowing that all phenomena have immeasurable characteristics;
knowing that all phenomena exist within a single thought-moment; knowing the mental activities of all sentient beings without obstruction;
knowing that the faculties of all sentient beings are equal; and knowing the afflictions and habitual tendencies of all sentient beings.
They practice. They know the mental activities of all sentient beings. They know the wholesome and unwholesome actions of all sentient beings.
They know the sovereign abiding and transformations of the vows and practices of all bodhisattvas.
They know that all Tathāgatas are endowed with the ten powers and have attained perfect enlightenment. These are the ten. If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain all dharmas.

Skillful Means. O Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of powers possessed by Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten? They are: the power of entering into the intrinsic nature of all phenomena;
the power of entering into all phenomena as being like a magical creation; the power of entering into all phenomena as being like an illusion;
the power of entering into all phenomena as being entirely the Buddha-dharma; the power of being without attachment to any phenomenon; and [the power] regarding...
The power of profound and clear understanding of all phenomena; the power of a mind that never abandons or fails to respect any spiritual friend;
the power that causes all roots of goodness to flow toward the sovereignty of unsurpassed wisdom; the power of deep faith in all Buddha-dharmas without disparagement;
and the power of skillfulness that prevents the mind of omniscience from ever regressing—these are the ten. If bodhisattvas...
Abiding in this Dharma, one possesses the unsurpassed powers of a Tathāgata. O Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of equality for Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
What are these ten? They are: equality toward all sentient beings; equality toward all dharmas; equality toward all lands;
equality toward all profound intentions; equality toward all roots of goodness; [and so forth]. One...
The equality of all bodhisattvas; the equality of all vows; the equality of all pāramitās; the equality of all practices;
and the equality of all buddhas—these are the ten. If bodhisattvas abide securely in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed dharma of equality of all buddhas.
Son of the Buddha, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of buddhas.
The phrases concerning the true meaning of phenomena (*dharmārtha-pada*). What are the ten? They are as follows: all phenomena are merely names; all phenomena are like illusions;
all phenomena are like reflections; all phenomena are merely dependent origination; all phenomena are pure in their karma.
All phenomena are merely the products of words; all phenomena are the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); all phenomena are signless (*animitta*); all phenomena are the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*);
all phenomena are the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*). These are the ten. If bodhisattvas abide securely in these dharmas, [they shall attain liberation].
Thus, one skillfully enters the supreme, true meaning of the knowledge of all-knowledge. O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva teaches ten kinds of dharmas.
What are these ten? They are: teaching the profound dharma; teaching the vast dharma; teaching various dharmas; teaching the dharma of omniscience;
teaching the dharmas that accord with the pāramitās; and teaching the dharmas that give rise to the powers of the Tathāgata.
He taught the dharmas associated with the three periods of time; he taught the dharmas that cause bodhisattvas not to regress; he taught the dharmas that praise the merits of the Buddhas;
and he taught the dharmas associated with the training of all bodhisattvas, the equality of all Buddhas, and the realm of all Tathāgatas.
These are the ten. If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed skill in preaching the Dharma.
O Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of upholding for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
What are the ten? They are: upholding all accumulated roots of merit and virtue; upholding all the teachings spoken by all Tathāgatas; upholding all parables; upholding...
The gateway to the principles of all dharmas; the dhāraṇī gateway that sustains all that arises; the sustainer of all dharmas that eliminate doubt and confusion;
the sustainer of the accomplishment of all bodhisattva dharmas; the sustainer of the gateway to the samādhi of equality taught by all Tathāgatas;
the sustainer of the gateway to the illumination of all dharmas; and the sustainer of the power of the divine play of the supernatural faculties of all Buddhas. This is...
There are ten. If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the sustaining power of the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed great wisdom.
O Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of eloquence for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are the ten? They are: eloquence that is non-conceptual regarding all dharmas;
eloquence that is without activity regarding all dharmas; regarding all [dharmas]...
The eloquence of non-attachment to phenomena; the eloquence of thorough realization of the emptiness of all phenomena;

the eloquence of being free from doubt and darkness regarding all phenomena; the eloquence of the Buddha’s empowerment regarding all phenomena; the eloquence of self-awakening regarding all phenomena;
the eloquence of skill in the differentiation of words and phrases regarding all phenomena; and the eloquence of the reality of all phenomena.
He speaks with eloquence; he possesses the eloquence that gladdens the minds of all sentient beings according to their inclinations. These are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed and skillful eloquence.
O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of mastery. What are the ten? They are as follows: namely, the mastery of teaching and taming all sentient beings...
Mastery over birth; mastery over universally illuminating all phenomena; mastery over practicing all roots of goodness; mastery over vast wisdom;
mastery over precepts that are without dependence; mastery over dedicating all roots of goodness toward enlightenment;
mastery over diligence that is non-regressive; mastery over using wisdom to destroy all demons; and mastery according to one's aspirations.

They attain mastery in causing the arousal of the bodhicitta; they attain mastery in manifesting the attainment of perfect enlightenment according to those who are to be transformed. These are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will obtain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed mastery of great wisdom. O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of non-attachment. What are the ten? They are: non-attachment toward all worlds;
non-attachment toward all sentient beings; non-attachment toward all phenomena; non-attachment toward all activities;
non-attachment toward all roots of goodness; non-attachment toward all places of rebirth; [non-attachment toward] one...
I vow to be without attachment: to all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*), to all bodhisattvas, and to all buddhas—this constitutes the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will be able to swiftly transform all perceptions (*saṃjñā*) and attain unsurpassed, pure wisdom.
O Son of the Buddha, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of equanimity (*samatā*).
The impartial mind. What are the ten? They are: the impartial mind that accumulates all merits; the impartial mind that gives rise to all distinct vows;
the impartial mind toward the bodies of all sentient beings; the impartial mind toward the karmic retributions of all sentient beings;
the impartial mind toward all phenomena; and the impartial mind toward all pure and impure lands.
The mind of equanimity: the mind of equanimity that understands all sentient beings as equal;
the mind of equanimity that makes no distinctions among all practices; the mind of equanimity regarding the powers and fearlessnesses of all Buddhas;
the mind of equanimity regarding the wisdom of all Tathāgatas—these are the ten. If Bodhisattvas abide in these, they shall attain the unsurpassed [wisdom] of the Tathāgata.
The Mind of Equanimity. Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of wisdom that arise for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
What are these ten? They are: the wisdom that arises from knowing the understandings of all sentient beings; the wisdom that arises from knowing the various distinctions among all buddha-fields;
the wisdom that arises from knowing the boundaries of the network of the ten directions; and the wisdom that arises from knowing [the worlds] that are inverted, upright, and so forth.
The wisdom that gives birth to all worlds; the wisdom that gives birth to the vast dwelling in the knowledge of the single nature and manifold natures of all phenomena;

the wisdom that gives birth to the knowledge of all various bodies; the wisdom that gives birth to the knowledge of being entirely unattached to the inverted delusions of all worlds; and the wisdom that knows all phenomena ultimately consist of a single [nature].
The path of renunciation gives rise to wisdom; knowing the Tathāgata’s spiritual power to enter all dharma realms gives rise to wisdom;
knowing that the Buddha-seed of all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time is never severed gives rise to wisdom. These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will have no lack of thorough understanding regarding all phenomena.
Sons of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of transformations of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are the ten? They are as follows: the transformation of all sentient beings;...
The transformation of all bodies; the transformation of all lands; the transformation of all offerings; the transformation of all sounds;
the transformation of all practices and vows; the transformation of teaching and taming all sentient beings;
the transformation of attaining perfect enlightenment; the transformation of preaching the Dharma; and the transformation of all empowerments—these are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the full perfection of all supreme methods of transformation.
This second major section, "The Arising of the Mind of Samantabhadra," consists of twenty gates that answer the preceding twenty questions, clarifying the practices for the ten stages of dwelling.
The first stage has four gates; the second stage has two gates; the third stage has two gates; and the fourth stage...
The first stage has one gate. The fifth stage has one gate. The sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, and tenth stages each have two gates.
Within the four gates of the first stage, the first—arousing the mind of Samantabhadra—clarifies the general characteristics of the stage of the initial arousal of the bodhicitta.

The "mind of Samantabhadra" is precisely the *bodhicitta*; it refers to the characteristic of arousing the mind by taking the fruition-awakening (*phala-bodhi*) as its entirety and foundation. The preceding ten...

While abiding in the stage of practice, one arouses the mind by taking the ten powers of the Buddha as an object; this is the arousal of a vast mind based upon the realm of the Buddha, and thus it is aroused through dependence on another.
Now, in terms of the fruition-awakening, it is aroused from its own essence; this is precisely what reveals the meaning of the interpenetration of the sequential and the perfect.
Furthermore, when one first generates the bodhicitta for the first time, the four great vows are generated instantaneously in a single thought-moment.

Because this generation of the mind contemplates the principle and accords with the true *dharmadhātu*, it is called the "universal generation of the mind. These four gates collectively clarify the meaning of generating the bodhicitta.

Second, regarding the stage of "Purifying the Ground" (*bhūmi-viśodhana*), there are two gates that clarify how the generation of the bodhicitta must necessarily rely upon a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*).

Thus, one attains accomplishment. Third is the stage of practice and abiding (*caryā-vihāra*), which consists of fully practicing the ten perfections (*daśa-pāramitā*); because these are essential, they must necessarily be practiced.

Fourth is the stage of realization and knowledge (*praveśa-vihāra*), which clarifies the dwelling of noble birth. Because one has previously cultivated the ten perfections and thereby comprehended all Buddha-dharmas and attained equal and perfect enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*), and because of this thorough understanding, one is able to realize and know [the truth]. Through such realization, one is born into the holy teaching (*ārya-śāsana*).
Therefore, it is called "Born Noble. This is the fifty-fold power, the first gate, clarifying the dwelling in practice through the perfection of skillful means.

In the previous ten dwellings, it was stated that all cultivated practices are for the sake of sentient beings, yet it was not specified which practices; therefore, this clarifies the practices to be cultivated.
Because of the thorough comprehension of the preceding stages, one is able to skillfully enter into all phenomena, possessing great power and function. Thus [it is so named].
One is able to fulfill skillful means, which is to say, the rescue and protection of all sentient beings. Sixth, there are two gates that clarify the practice of the stage of right mind.
In the first gate, there are ten kinds of equality. Because one has previously entered well into all phenomena, one is thus equal toward all phenomena;
therefore, it is called the single equality of the true dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*). Having realized that there are no dual characteristics, [one perceives] the Buddha and...

The mind, objects, phenomena, principles, and so forth, are each thoroughly integrated and permeated, becoming identical in a single flavor; therefore, it is called the "Right Mind. As for why they are equal:

because one realizes that the *parikalpita* (imagined) nature is without reality, the *paratantra* (dependent) nature is empty, and there is only the pure, singular *pariniṣpanna* (perfected) nature, they are thus equal.
Therefore, this is established by means of the second gate: the true meaning of the Buddha-dharma. Section Seven has two gates explaining non-retrogression.

The dwelling and practice. Because one thoroughly realizes the equality of all phenomena and dwells securely in *tathatā* (suchness), the mind does not regress, and one is able to speak of the Dharma realized by oneself, expounding it according to one's capacity.

This is accomplished through the subsequent gate, which consists of two sections clarifying the dwelling and practice of the stage of the youthful truth (*kumārabhūta*). By dwelling in the equality of all phenomena...
...and so forth. Because they realize the true meaning, they attain skillful eloquence and great mastery (*vaśitā*).
Ninth, there are two gates that clarify the conduct of the prince while dwelling therein: because of the aforementioned unimpeded mastery over the Dharma, they attain non-attachment;

because of non-attachment, they penetrate deeply into the limit of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), and thus they attain the equality of the Buddhas. The former [section] was the realization of the equality of phenomena; this—
Thus, one abides in equanimity; therefore, this is the training for the station of the Dharma King.
*The Compendium of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Fascicle 53; *The Compendium of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Fascicle 54.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Śikṣānanda of the Kingdom of Khotan;
commentary on the meaning by the Śramaṇa Chengguan of Qingliangshan Dàhuá yán Temple;
and edited and summarized by the Śramaṇa Hanshan Deqing of Fāyún Temple on Kuāngshān, Ming Dynasty.
The above response concludes the explanation of the practices for the ten stages of practice (*daśabhūmi*) in answer to the preceding twenty questions.
Below are thirty sections answering the thirty questions regarding the ten practices.
*Lokottara-parivarta*, Chapter Thirty-Eight, Part Two.
O Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of sustaining powers of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten? They are:

the sustaining power of the Buddhas, the sustaining power of the Dharma, the sustaining power of sentient beings, the sustaining power of karma, the sustaining power of practice, the sustaining power of vows, the sustaining power of spheres of experience, the sustaining power of time, the sustaining power of goodness, and the sustaining power of wisdom. These are the ten. If Bodhisattvas abide in these...
Dharma. Thus, regarding all phenomena, one attains the supreme power of mastery and sustenance.
Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of great consolation for Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten? They are as follows: Bodhisattvas give rise to this thought:
"Throughout the entirety of the future world, for all Buddhas who appear in the world, I shall follow and serve them all."
He gives rise to joy. Reflecting thus, his heart is filled with great consolation. He further thinks:
"When those Tathāgatas appear in the world, I shall honor and make offerings to them all with unsurpassed requisites.
Reflecting thus, his heart is filled with great consolation. He further thinks: "When I present offerings to those Buddhas, those Tathāgatas..."
He will surely instruct me in the Dharma; I shall listen to and receive it all with a profound mind of reverence, and practice according to his teaching.
Regarding the stages of a bodhisattva, I shall certainly attain birth in the past, birth in the present, and birth in the future. Thinking thus, my heart was filled with great joy and consolation.
Furthermore, I made this reflection: "I shall practice the conduct of a bodhisattva for unspeakably unspeakable eons, always together with all [beings]."
One comes to dwell together with all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; contemplating this, one’s heart feels great joy and consolation. Furthermore, one reflects:

"In the past, before I had resolved upon the unsurpassed, great mind of enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi-citta), I was subject to various fears—namely, the fear of lacking a livelihood, the fear of ill repute, the fear of death, the fear of falling into the evil realms, and the fear of the majesty of the great assembly. But from the moment I first resolved my mind [upon enlightenment], all of these have been entirely [dispelled]."
They remain far removed from all [distractions], neither startled nor terrified, neither fearful nor apprehensive, neither timid nor afraid;
they cannot be defeated by any demons or non-Buddhist outsiders. Contemplating thus, their hearts are filled with great joy and consolation. They further form this thought:
"I shall cause all sentient beings to attain unexcelled bodhi. Once they have attained bodhi, I shall, before those Buddhas..."
Throughout their entire lives, they cultivate the bodhisattva practices. With great faith, they provide all necessary offerings for the Buddhas to whom they should make offerings.
Furthermore, after the Buddhas have entered parinirvāṇa, they each erect immeasurable stupas to honor the relics and uphold and protect all the remaining teachings.
Contemplating in this way, their hearts are filled with great joy and consolation. Moreover, they form this thought:

I shall adorn all worlds throughout the ten directions with unsurpassed adornments, causing them all to be fully endowed with various wonders, equal and pure; furthermore, by means of various great supernormal powers, I shall...
The earth shook and quaked, and its radiance shone forth, pervading everywhere. Reflecting thus, his heart was filled with great joy and consolation.
He further thought: "I shall sever the doubts and delusions of all sentient beings and purify the aspirations and inclinations of all sentient beings."
It awakens the minds and intentions of all sentient beings; it extinguishes the afflictions of all sentient beings; it closes the gates to the evil realms for all sentient beings;
it opens the gates to the auspicious destinies for all sentient beings; it shatters the darkness of all sentient beings; it bestows light upon all sentient beings;
it causes all sentient beings to be free from the works of Māra; and it leads all sentient beings to peace.
In private, he reflects in this way and his heart is filled with great joy and comfort. The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva further thinks:
"The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are as difficult to encounter as the Udumbara flower; in immeasurable kalpas, one may not see even a single one.
Yet, in a future age, whenever I wish to see a Tathāgata, I shall immediately be able to see them; the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, never abandon me."
I shall always dwell in my own abode so that I may behold [the Buddhas]. They shall preach the Dharma for me without interruption. Having heard the Dharma, my mind and intentions will become pure;
free from flattery and crookedness, I shall be upright and without guile. In every thought-moment, I shall constantly see all the Buddhas.
Reflecting thus, his heart was filled with great joy and consolation. He further thought: "In the future, I shall attain Buddhahood.

By the spiritual power of a Buddha, I shall manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment individually for all sentient beings throughout all worlds, uttering the pure and fearless Great Lion’s Roar.
Through my original great vows that pervade the entire Dharma-realm, I shall strike the great [drum of the Dharma]."
The Dharma drum beats; it rains down the great rain of Dharma and performs the great gift of Dharma. Throughout immeasurable eons, it constantly expounds the True Dharma.
Sustained by great compassion, its physical, verbal, and mental actions are never weary or exhausted. Reflecting thus, his heart is filled with great joy and consolation. O Son of the Buddha!

These are the ten kinds of great consolation for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas. If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the great consolation of the wisdom of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas have ten ways of deeply entering the Buddha-dharma. What are the ten? They are: entering all worlds of the past; [entering all worlds of the future]; [entering all worlds of the present];

[entering all realms of sentient beings]; [entering all realms of phenomena]; [entering all realms of space]; [entering all realms of time]; [entering all realms of liberation]; [entering all realms of skillful means]; and [entering all realms of the Buddhas]. These are the ten ways of deeply entering the Buddha-dharma. Regarding the first, it is said: entering all worlds of the past.
They enter all worlds of the future; they enter the enumeration of worlds, the activities of worlds, the descriptions of worlds, and the purification of worlds in the present age.
They enter the various natures of all worlds; they enter the various karmic retributions of all sentient beings;
they enter the various practices of all bodhisattvas; they know the succession of all past buddhas; they know the [future... of the unborn.

They come to know the succession of all Buddhas; they know all the Buddha-lands and assemblies throughout the ten directions, equal to the void and the dharma-realm, and how these Buddhas preach the Dharma to subdue beings. They know the worldly dharmas, the dharmas of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and Tathāgatas.
Although they know that all dharmas are without discrimination, they expound various teachings, all of which enter into the Dharma.
Because the realms have no point of entry, as the Dharma teaches, there is no grasping or attachment; this is the tenth.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain entry into the profound nature of the great wisdom of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of reliance; by relying on these, Bodhisattvas practice.
The Bodhisattva practice. What are the ten? They are: practicing the bodhisattva path by relying on making offerings to all Buddhas;
practicing the bodhisattva path by relying on taming all sentient beings; practicing the bodhisattva path by relying on attending upon all virtuous friends;
practicing the bodhisattva path by relying on accumulating all roots of goodness; practicing the bodhisattva path by relying on adornment... [text continues]
They practice the bodhisattva conduct by purifying all buddha-fields; they practice the bodhisattva conduct by relying on never abandoning any sentient beings;
they practice the bodhisattva conduct by relying on deeply entering all perfections; they practice the bodhisattva conduct by relying on fulfilling all bodhisattva vows;
they practice the bodhisattva conduct by relying on the immeasurable mind of enlightenment; they rely on...
To practice all the bodhi-conduct and bodhisattva conduct of all Buddhas—this is the tenth. It is by relying on these that Bodhisattvas practice the bodhisattva conduct.

O Son of the Buddha, there are ten ways in which Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give rise to a mind of fearlessness. What are these ten? They are: giving rise to a mind of fearlessness by extinguishing all obstructive karma;
giving rise to a mind of fearlessness after the parinirvāṇa of a Buddha by protecting and upholding the True Dharma; [and so forth].
The fearless mind that subdues all Māras; the fearless mind that disregards body and life;
the fearless mind that crushes all the heterodox arguments of external paths; the fearless mind that causes all sentient beings to rejoice;
the fearless mind that causes all assemblies to be entirely joyful; and the fearless mind that tames all devas.
Nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas give rise to a mind of fearlessness;
they give rise to a mind of fearlessness by departing from the stages of the two vehicles and entering the profound Dharma;
they give rise to a mind of fearlessness by practicing the bodhisattva conduct for unspeakably unspeakable eons with a mind free from weariness—these are the ten. If all...
When Bodhisattvas dwell securely in these dharmas, they attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed great wisdom and a mind free from fear.
O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give rise to ten kinds of minds free from doubt, such that their minds have no uncertainty regarding any of the Buddha-dharmas.
What are these ten? They are as follows: the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to this thought: "I shall gather in all sentient beings through giving;
I shall gather in all sentient beings through ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.
When he gives rise to this thought, it is certain and without doubt; that he should give rise to a doubting mind is impossible. This is...
This constitutes the first arousal of a mind free from doubt. Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva reflects:
"When all future Buddhas appear in the world, I shall serve and make offerings to them all. When he arouses this thought, it is certain and without doubt.
If one were to give rise to doubt, it would be impossible; this is the second generation of the mind free from doubt.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects: "I shall universally adorn all worlds with various wondrous nets of light.
When generating this mind, he is resolute and without doubt; if one were to give rise to doubt, it would be impossible. This is...
This constitutes the third generation of the mind free from doubt. Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva reflects thus:

"I shall cultivate the bodhisattva practices throughout all future kalpas—practices that are innumerable, immeasurable, boundless, incomparable, incalculable, ineffable, inconceivable, unfathomable, unspeakable, and beyond the reach of speech; they transcend all calculation and reach the ultimate limit."
"Throughout the entire realm of phenomena and the realm of empty space, for all sentient beings, I shall bring them to maturity by means of the supreme methods of teaching and discipline.
When one gives rise to this thought, it is certain and without doubt; it is impossible for a mind of doubt to arise.
This is the fourth arousal of the mind of non-doubt. Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects thus: "I shall..."
Having cultivated the bodhisattva practices and fulfilled the great vows, one abides within the possession of all-knowledge.
When this mind is generated, it is certain and without doubt; for it is impossible for a mind of doubt to arise. This is the fifth generation of the mind of non-doubt.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva reflects thus: "I shall universally practice the bodhisattva conduct for the sake of all worlds;
I shall become the pure radiance of all dharmas, illuminating all the Buddha-dharmas that exist.
When he gives rise to this mind, it is resolute and without doubt; it is impossible for a mind of doubt to arise. This is the sixth generation of the resolve free from doubt.
The Mind. Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva forms this thought: "I shall know that all dharmas are the Buddha-dharma.
According to the minds of sentient beings, I will expound them for their sake so that they may all attain awakening. When he gives rise to this mind, he is resolute and free from doubt.
It is impossible for doubt to arise; this is the seventh generation of the mind free from doubt.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva reflects: "I shall attain the gate of non-obstruction regarding all phenomena, because I know that all obstructions are unfindable.
With such a mind, free from hesitation, he abides in true reality until [enlightenment] is achieved.
Regarding *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, when one gives rise to this mind, it is certain and without doubt;
it is impossible for a doubting mind to arise. This is the eighth [resolve]: giving rise to a mind free from doubt. Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects:
"I shall know all dharmas such that there are none that are not supramundane dharmas," and he remains far removed from [the notion of] a single [self].
All deluded thoughts and inversions are adorned with a single adornment, yet there is nothing to be adorned.
One realizes this for oneself without awakening through another; when this mind is generated, it is certain and without doubt.
It is impossible for a mind of doubt to arise. This is the ninth generation of the mind free from doubt. Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects thus: "I..."
One shall attain supreme perfect enlightenment regarding all phenomena, because of being free from all conceptual constructions and inversions;
because of attaining the wisdom of instantaneous correspondence; because neither unity nor difference can be apprehended; because of being free from all numerical reckonings;
because of being ultimately unconditioned; because of being free from all verbal expression; and because of abiding at the limit of the ineffable realm—at the moment this mind is generated.
This is certain and beyond doubt; it is impossible for a mind of doubt to arise. This is the tenth arousal of the mind free from doubt.
If Bodhisattvas abide in this dharma, their minds will have no doubts regarding any of the Buddha-dharmas. O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of inconceivabilities. What are these ten? They are:
the inconceivability of all roots of goodness; the inconceivability of all vows; the inconceivability of knowing that all phenomena are like illusions;
and the inconceivability of not losing roots of goodness while cultivating bodhisattva practices after having resolved upon bodhicitta, being without any discrimination.
It is inconceivable. Although they have deeply penetrated all phenomena, they do not take up parinirvāṇa, for it is inconceivable that all their vows have not yet been fully accomplished.

While practicing the bodhisattva path, they manifest descending from heaven, entering the womb, being born, renouncing the world, practicing austerities, proceeding to the site of enlightenment, subduing the hosts of Māra, attaining supreme perfect enlightenment, and turning the wheel of the true Dharma.
They enter parinirvāṇa; their mastery over spiritual transformations is unceasing, and they inconceivably rescue and protect sentient beings without abandoning their compassionate vows.

Although they can manifest the ten powers of a Tathāgata and mastery over spiritual transformations, they also do not abandon the mind that is equal to the dharma-realm, inconceivably teaching and transforming sentient beings. They know that all phenomena are signless, yet this is their very characteristic.
Marks are markless; non-discrimination is discrimination, and discrimination is non-discrimination. That which is not existent is existent, and that which is existent is non-existent.
Non-action is action, and action is non-action. That which is not speech is speech, and that which is speech is non-speech—this is inconceivable.
One knows that the mind and bodhi are equal; one knows that bodhi and the mind are equal. Mind and bodhi...
They are equal to all sentient beings. Furthermore, they do not give rise to mental inversion, conceptual inversion, or view-inversion, nor to anything inconceivable.
In every moment of thought, they enter the meditative absorption of cessation (*nirodha-samāpatti*). They exhaust all outflows (*āsrava*) yet do not realize the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).

Nor do they exhaust their roots of goodness associated with outflows. Although they know that all phenomena are without outflows, they also know the exhaustion of outflows and the cessation of outflows. Although...
To know that the Buddha-dharma is itself the worldly dharma, and the worldly dharma is itself the Buddha-dharma;
yet not to differentiate the worldly dharma within the Buddha-dharma, nor to differentiate the Buddha-dharma within the worldly dharma;
for all dharmas enter the Dharma-realm because there is nothing to enter; and to know that all dharmas are non-dual because they are without change—this is the [first]... (or: this is the second).
Ten Inconceivables. O Son of the Buddha, these are the ten kinds of inconceivability of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
If Bodhisattvas abide in them, they will attain all the unsurpassed, inconceivable dharmas of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of skillful secret speech (*saṃdhā-bhāṣita*). What are the ten? They are as follows:
The skillful secret language regarding all Buddha-sūtras; the skillful secret language regarding all places of rebirth;

the skillful secret language regarding the manifestation of all bodhisattva supernormal powers and the attainment of perfect enlightenment; the skillful secret language regarding the karmic retribution of all sentient beings;
the skillful secret language regarding the defilement and purification arising in all sentient beings; and [the skillful secret language] regarding all phenomena.
This is the skillful esoteric language of the ultimate gate of non-obstruction:
that within every single location throughout all realms of space, there are worlds either forming or decaying, with no intervening empty space; this is the skillful esoteric language.
That throughout the entire dharma-realm and in all ten directions, even down to the most minute points, the Tathāgata manifests his initial birth and continues until his attainment of Buddhahood.
The skillful secret language [is that which] enters parinirvāṇa and fills the dharma-realm, yet discerns and perceives all things;
it perceives the equality of the nirvāṇa of all sentient beings as being immutable, and thus does not abandon the great vow;

it is the skillful secret language [that acts] so that the vows of omniscience, though not yet perfected, may be brought to fulfillment; and although one knows all dharmas through realization independent of others, yet...
They abandon all unwholesome spiritual friends and increase their reverence for the Tathāgata;
they are in harmonious union with spiritual friends without duality; they cultivate, plant, dedicate, and abide in all roots of goodness;
they share the same activities, the same essential nature, the same renunciation, and the same accomplishment of skillful secret speech—these are the ten. If bodhisattvas...

Abiding therein, one attains the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed skillful and subtle secret speech. O Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of skillful analytical wisdom possessed by Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
What are these ten? They are: the skillful analytical wisdom that enters all lands;
the skillful analytical wisdom that enters the abodes of all sentient beings; and the skillful analytical wisdom that enters the mental activities of all sentient beings.

The wisdom of skillful discernment; the wisdom of skillful discernment that enters into the faculties of all sentient beings; the wisdom of skillful discernment that enters into the karmic retributions of all sentient beings;
the wisdom of skillful discernment that enters into the practices of all śrāvakas; the wisdom of skillful discernment that enters into the practices of all pratyekabuddhas;
the wisdom of skillful discernment that enters into the practices of all bodhisattvas; and the wisdom of skillful discernment that enters into all worlds.
Skillful analytical knowledge of phenomena; skillful analytical knowledge that enters all Buddha-dharmas—these are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide therein, they will attain the supreme, skillful analytical knowledge of all dharmas possessed by all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of entry into samādhi for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
What are these ten? They are: entering samādhi in all worlds; entering samādhi in the bodies of all sentient beings; entering samādhi in all phenomena;
entering samādhi upon seeing all Buddhas; entering samādhi while abiding through all kalpas; [and] from samādhi...
They manifest inconceivable bodies and enter samādhi; they enter samādhi within the bodies of all Buddhas;
they awaken to the equality of all sentient beings and enter samādhi; and within a single thought-moment, they enter the samādhi of the wisdom of all bodhisattvas.
Within a single thought-moment, by means of unimpeded wisdom, they accomplish all the practices and vows of all bodhisattvas without exception.
Resting in meditative absorption (*samādhi*). These are the ten. If bodhisattvas abide therein, they will attain the unsurpassed skillful methods of the *samādhi* of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of universal entry for Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten? They are:
universal entry into sentient beings, universal entry into lands, and the various characteristics of worlds.
Pervasive entry; pervasive entry into the calamity of fire; pervasive entry into the calamity of water; pervasive entry into the Buddha; pervasive entry into adornments;
pervasive entry into the Tathāgata’s body of boundless merit; pervasive entry into all various forms of teaching the Dharma;
pervasive entry into all various offerings made to the Tathāgatas. These are the ten. If Bodhisattvas abide therein, they then attain the Tathāgata’s [unimpeded wisdom].
The Great Wisdom that Pervasively Enters All Dharmas. O Son of the Buddha, there are ten gates of liberation for Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
What are these ten? They are: the gate of liberation in which a single body pervades all worlds;
the gate of liberation in which one manifests infinite varieties of physical forms within all worlds; the gate of liberation in which all worlds enter into a single Buddha...
The liberation door of the buddha-fields; the liberation door of universally empowering all realms of sentient beings;
the liberation door of filling all worlds with bodies adorned by all Buddhas; the liberation door of perceiving all worlds within one's own body;
the liberation door of abiding in all worlds within a single thought-moment; and the manifestation [of these] in all ages.
The liberation door of all Tathāgatas appearing in the world; the liberation door of a single body filling the entire Dharma-realm;
the liberation door of manifesting all the playful supernatural powers of the Buddhas within a single thought-moment—these are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide therein, they will attain the unsurpassed liberation door of the Tathāgata. O Son of the Buddha, these are the [liberation doors] of the Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Bodhisattvas have ten kinds of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*). What are the ten? They are: the supernormal power of the wisdom of skillful means for recollecting past lives;

the supernormal power of the wisdom of skillful means for the unimpeded divine ear; the supernormal power of the wisdom of skillful means for knowing the inconceivable mental activities of other sentient beings;
the supernormal power of the wisdom of skillful means for observing with the divine eye without obstruction; and [the supernormal power] of manifesting according to the minds of sentient beings...
The skillful wisdom-penetration of inconceivable great supernormal powers; the skillful wisdom-penetration of universally manifesting a single body throughout immeasurable worlds;
the skillful wisdom-penetration of entering, in a single thought-moment, unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds;
the skillful wisdom-penetration of producing immeasurable ornaments to adorn inconceivable worlds; and the manifestation of the unspeakable...
The supernormal power of skillful means of the transformation body (*nirmāṇakāya*), which, according to the inconceivable minds of sentient beings,
manifests the attainment of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in unspeakable worlds through the supernormal power of skillful means—
this is the tenth. If bodhisattvas abide in these, they will attain the Tathāgata’s supreme and great skillful supernormal powers as one.
They manifest in various ways for all sentient beings, causing them to practice and learn. O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of clear knowledge (*vidyā*).
What are these ten? They are: the clear knowledge of skillful wisdom that knows the karmic retributions of all sentient beings;

the clear knowledge of skillful wisdom that knows the realm of all sentient beings is quiescent, pure, and free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*); the clear knowledge that knows one... [text continues]
The various objects of perception of all sentient beings are but a single characteristic, none of which can be apprehended;

all phenomena are like adamant, through the illumination of skillful wisdom. With immeasurable and subtle sounds, this illumination of skillful wisdom is heard throughout all worlds in the ten directions;
it universally destroys all mental attachments through the illumination of skillful wisdom. It is able to...

The light of skillful wisdom that manifests through skillful means the appearance of taking birth or not taking birth; the light of skillful wisdom that abandons all objective spheres of perception and sensation;

the light of skillful wisdom that knows all phenomena to be neither existent nor non-existent, characterized by a single nature and the absence of intrinsic nature, yet being free from conceptual differentiation while still being able to comprehend the various phenomena and explain them through analysis over immeasurable eons.
Abiding in the *dharmadhātu*, they possess the skillful wisdom and illumination that brings about *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva knows that all sentient beings are fundamentally non-arisen from the very beginning, because they thoroughly understand that birth cannot be apprehended;
yet they know causes, know conditions, know phenomena, know objects, know conduct, know arising, know cessation, and know verbal expression.
He knows delusion and knows freedom from delusion; he knows perversion and knows freedom from perversion;
he knows affliction and knows purification; he knows birth-and-death and knows nirvana; he knows the attainable and knows the unattainable; he knows attachment and knows non-attachment.

He knows when to remain still and when to move; he knows how to go and how to return; he knows how to arise and how not to arise; he knows ruin and knows transcendence; he knows maturation and knows the faculties;
he knows how to discipline them, providing various kinds of instruction according to what is appropriate for each, never forgetting the conduct of a bodhisattva.
Why is this? Because a bodhisattva sets out for the sake of benefiting sentient beings alone.

They have no other purpose than to give rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. For this reason, Bodhisattvas constantly transform sentient beings with bodies free from weariness, never contravening what is done in all worlds;
this is called the luminous wisdom of skillfulness regarding dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*).
A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva does not give rise to a mind of attachment toward the Buddha, nor does he give rise to a mind of attachment toward the Dharma.
They are unattached to buddha-fields and do not give rise to a mind of attachment toward them; they are unattached to sentient beings and do not give rise to a mind of attachment toward them.

They do not perceive the existence of sentient beings while practicing teaching, taming, and preaching the Dharma; yet they do not abandon the various practices of a bodhisattva, their great compassion, or their great vows.
Seeing the Buddhas and hearing the Dharma, they practice in accordance with them, planting all roots of goodness based upon the Tathāgata, and they pay respectful homage.
They make offerings without ceasing. By means of their supernormal powers, they can shake immeasurable worlds throughout the ten directions, for their minds are vast and equal to the dharma-realm.
They know the various ways of teaching the Dharma; they know the number of sentient beings; and they know the distinctions among sentient beings.
He knows the arising of suffering; he knows the cessation of suffering; he knows that all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) are like reflections.

He practices the bodhisattva conduct to forever sever the root of all rebirth. Yet, for the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings, he practices the bodhisattva conduct without anything being practiced.
He accords with the lineage of all Buddhas and gives rise to a mind like the king of great mountains, knowing all things to be empty.
Free from delusion and perversion, one enters the gateway to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*). With vast wisdom that cannot be shaken, one shall attain perfect enlightenment.
Possessing skillful wisdom and clarity, one impartially delivers all sentient beings across the ocean of birth and death. These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide therein, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed, great skillful wisdom-illumination.
O Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of liberation for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are the ten? They are: liberation from afflictions;
liberation from false views; liberation from all grasping; liberation from the aggregates, sense bases, and elements; liberation that transcends the two vehicles; liberation from [the absence of]...
The liberation of the patience regarding the arising of phenomena; the liberation of being free from attachment to all worlds, all lands, all sentient beings, and all phenomena;
the liberation of infinite abiding; the liberation of initiating all bodhisattva practices and entering the Tathāgata’s stage of non-conceptuality;
and the liberation of being able to fully comprehend all three periods of time within a single thought-moment. This is...
There are ten. If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they are able to perform the unsurpassed work of a Buddha, teaching and bringing all sentient beings to maturity.
Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of groves. What are the ten? They are as follows:
Birth-and-death (*saṃsāra*) is the Bodhisattva’s grove, because they never grow weary of or abandon it; teaching and transforming sentient beings is...
The garden of the bodhisattva is the absence of weariness. Abiding through all kalpas is the garden of the bodhisattva because it encompasses all great practices.
Pure worlds are the garden of the bodhisattva because they are where one dwells. All palaces of Māra are the garden of the bodhisattva because they are for the purpose of subduing those hosts.
Contemplating the Dharma as it has been heard is the garden of the bodhisattva.

It is because he observes with the clarity of a forest; because the six perfections, the four means of attraction, and the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment are the Bodhisattva’s grove, as they continue the realm of his compassionate father;
and because the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the eighteen unique qualities, and even all Buddha-dharmas are the Bodhisattva’s grove, as he does not dwell upon other dharmas. Thus it is shown.

The sovereign supernormal powers and majestic might of all bodhisattvas constitute their grove, for they turn the wheel of the true Dharma with great spiritual power to subdue sentient beings without ceasing.
In a single thought-moment, they manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment in all places for the sake of all sentient beings;
this constitutes their grove, as the Dharma-body pervades everywhere throughout the entirety of space.
Because it is the world. These are the ten. If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed, sorrowless, and great blissful practice of the Tathāgata.
O Son of the Buddha, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of palaces. What are the ten? They are as follows:
the mind of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*) is the palace of the bodhisattva, because it is never forgotten. The ten wholesome [actions]...
The paths of action, merit, and wisdom are the palace of the bodhisattva, for the purpose of teaching and transforming sentient beings in the desire realm.
The four divine abodes and meditative concentrations are the palace of the bodhisattva, for the purpose of teaching and transforming sentient beings in the form realm.
Rebirth in the Pure Abode heavens is the palace of the bodhisattva, because they are untainted by any afflictions. Rebirth in the formless realm is the palace of the bodhisattva.
To cause all sentient beings to leave behind places of hardship, the birth in a world of defilement is a palace of the bodhisattva;
to cause all sentient beings to sever their afflictions, dwelling within the inner palace with wife, children, and retinue is a palace of the bodhisattva;

to manifest as a wheel-turning monarch, a guardian of the world, Śakra, or Brahmā is a palace of the bodhisattva, for the purpose of bringing to maturity those sentient beings who shared his past practices.

This palace is for the sake of taming sentient beings who possess sovereign minds; it is where one dwells having attained mastery over all bodhisattva practices and the play of supernatural powers (*ṛddhi-vikrīḍita*);
it is the palace of the bodhisattva through skillful play in various dhyānas, liberations (*vimokṣa*), samādhis, and wisdom;

and it is that which receives from all Buddhas the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) and prediction (*vyākaraṇa*) as the King of Omniscience (*sarvajñatā-rāja*), possessing unsurpassed sovereignty. This is the palace of the bodhisattva...
The palace of the Tathāgata. By dwelling therein, one attains the sovereign mastery of all dharmas as a Dharma King, adorned with the ten powers. These are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide within them, they receive the Dharma-consecration and attain sovereign power through spiritual might over all worlds.
O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of delight. What are these ten? They are as follows:
They delight in right mindfulness, because the mind is not distracted. They delight in wisdom, because they discern all phenomena.
They delight in visiting the abodes of all Buddhas, because they never tire of hearing the Dharma. They delight in the Buddhas, because they fill the ten directions without limit.
They delight in the sovereignty of Bodhisattvas, because they manifest their bodies through immeasurable gateways for the sake of all sentient beings. They delight in the various samādhis.

They delight in the gateways of samādhi, because by entering a single gateway of samādhi, they enter all gateways of samādhi. They delight in dhāraṇīs, because they uphold the Dharma without forgetting it and transmit it to sentient beings.
They delight in unimpeded eloquence (*anāvaraṇa-pratibhāna*), because they can analyze and expound upon a single word or phrase of a sūtra for unspeakable eons without end.
They delight in attaining perfect enlightenment, because for the sake of all sentient beings, with no [regard for themselves]...

Because they manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment within their own bodies through the gate of measure; because they delight in turning the wheel of Dharma to destroy all heterodox teachings—these are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed dharma-bliss of all Buddhas, Tathāgatas.
Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of adornments. What are they?
Tenth: the adornment of power, because it is indestructible; the adornment of fearlessness, because it cannot be overcome;

the adornment of meaning, because the inexhaustible explanation of the ineffable meaning is unending; the adornment of Dharma, because the eighty-four thousand aggregates of Dharma are observed, expounded, and never forgotten;
and the adornment of vows, because the great aspirations undertaken by all bodhisattvas never regress.

Because they transform; because they practice the conduct of Samantabhadra as an adornment of conduct and thereby achieve liberation; because they adorn the buddha-fields by making all fields into a single field;
and because they adorn with universal sound by raining down the rain of Dharma throughout all worlds of the Buddhas.
The adornment of power, because one practices countless deeds throughout all kalpas without interruption;

the adornment of transformation, because one manifests within the body of a single sentient being as many bodies as there are sentient beings, causing all sentient beings to know and see them, and because one seeks omniscience without ever turning back. These are the ten. If Bodhisattvas abide in these...
By this dharma, one attains all the unsurpassed dharmas of the Tathāgata’s adornment. Sons of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of immovable minds that a bodhisattva mahāsattva generates.
What are the ten? They are: the immovable mind that is able to relinquish all possessions;
the immovable mind that contemplates and examines all buddha-dharmas; the immovable mind that recollects and makes offerings to a single...
The immovable mind that honors all Buddhas; the immovable mind that vows never to harm or afflict any sentient being;
the immovable mind that universally gathers in all sentient beings without discriminating between enemies and kin; the immovable mind that seeks all Buddha-dharmas without ceasing;
and the non-arising [mind] that practices the bodhisattva conduct for as many unspeakably unspeakable eons as there are sentient beings.
They possess a mind that is free from weariness, non-retrogressive, and immovable;

they have accomplished faith with roots, unclouded faith, pure faith, utterly pure faith, stainless faith, lucid faith, faith that reverently makes offerings to all Buddhas, non-retrogressive faith, inexhaustible faith, indestructible faith, and a mind of great joy and exultation that is immovable. They have achieved...
The unshakable mind that gives rise to the path of skillful means for attaining all-knowledge;
and the unshakable mind that hears all the dharmas of the bodhisattva practices, accepts them with faith, and does not slander them—these are the ten.

If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed, unshakable mind of all-knowledge. O Son of the Buddha, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of non-abandonment of the profound...
The Great Mind. What are the ten? They are: the great mind of never abandoning the fulfillment of all the profound and great aspirations of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
the great mind of never abandoning the teaching and taming of all sentient beings; the great mind of never abandoning the uninterrupted lineage of all Buddhas;
the great mind of never abandoning the close attendance upon all spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*); and never abandoning...
The profound and great resolve to make offerings to all Buddhas; the profound and great resolve never to abandon the single-minded pursuit of all Mahāyāna qualities and dharmas;
the profound and great resolve never to abandon the practice of pure conduct and the maintenance of pure precepts in the presence of all Buddhas;
the profound and great resolve never to abandon the close attendance upon all Bodhisattvas; the profound and great resolve never to abandon the seeking of the methods for all Buddha-dharmas.

One then protects and upholds the profound and great mind—the profound and great mind that does not abandon the fulfillment of all bodhisattva practices and vows, and that gathers all the qualities of a Buddha. These are the ten. If bodhisattvas abide in these, they will be able to never abandon any of the Buddha-dharmas.
Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of wisdom-observation for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are they?
Tenth: that is to say, the wisdom-observation of skillfully analyzing and explaining all phenomena; the wisdom-observation of knowing all roots of goodness throughout the three periods of time;
the wisdom-observation of knowing the sovereign transformations of all bodhisattva practices;
the wisdom-observation of knowing all gateways to the meaning of all phenomena; and the wisdom-observation of knowing all... [the text continues].
The wisdom-observation of the Buddha’s majestic power; the wisdom-observation that thoroughly knows all dharani-doors;
the wisdom-observation that universally proclaims the True Dharma in all worlds; the wisdom-observation that enters the entire realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu);
the wisdom-observation that knows the inconceivable [realms] of all ten directions; and the wisdom that knows all Buddha-dharmas.
The light of wisdom is unimpeded, and one observes with wisdom; this is the tenth.
If Bodhisattvas abide therein, they will attain the Tathāgata’s supreme great wisdom of observation.
O Son of the Buddha, there are ten ways in which Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas expound the Dharma. What are these ten? They are: expounding that all phenomena arise from conditions; expounding...
All phenomena are entirely like illusions. It is said that all phenomena are without conflict or contention.
It is said that all phenomena have no limits or boundaries. It is said that all phenomena have no basis for reliance. It is said that all phenomena are like vajra.
It is said that all phenomena are entirely suchness (tathatā). It is said that all phenomena are entirely quiescent. It is said that all phenomena are...
They are all liberated. It is taught that all dharmas abide in a single meaning, perfected in their fundamental nature. These are the ten.
If bodhisattvas dwell therein, they will be able to skillfully expound all dharmas. O Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of purity for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
What are the ten? They are: purity of the profound mind; purity of severing doubt; [and so forth].
Purity of freedom from views; purity of the objective sphere; purity of seeking all-knowledge; purity of eloquence; purity of fearlessness;
purity of abiding in the wisdom of all bodhisattvas; purity of receiving the vows of all bodhisattvas;
and the complete accomplishment of the thirty-two marks of a supreme Buddha, which are the pure dharmas of a hundredfold merit and all that is wholesome.
The purity of the faculties—these are the ten. If bodhisattvas abide in them, they will attain the unsurpassed, pure Dharma of all Tathāgatas.
O Son of the Buddha, there are ten seals of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?

What is meant by a bodhisattva-mahāsattva knowing the suffering of suffering, the suffering of change, and the suffering of conditioned existence; seeking the Buddha-dharma with single-minded devotion without giving rise to indolence;
practicing the bodhisattva conduct without weariness or laxity; being without alarm, fear, dread, or terror; not abandoning the great vow;
seeking all-knowledge with firm resolve and without retreating; and ultimately attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

"Ti. This is the first seal. When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva sees sentient beings who are foolish and deranged, who may insult and humiliate one another with coarse, vile, and evil speech, or who may inflict harm with swords, staves, tiles, or stones, they never abandon the bodhicitta because of such circumstances.
Rather, they practice patience and gentleness, single-mindedly cultivating the Buddha-dharma, and abide in the supreme..."
Entering the state of separation from birth by means of the supreme path is the second seal.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas hear the profound Buddha-dharma associated with omniscience being taught, they are able, by means of their own wisdom, to have deep faith, to accept it with patience, to comprehend it, and to enter into it.
This is the third seal. Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects thus: "I have resolved with a profound mind to seek all-knowledge.
I shall attain Buddhahood and realize Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. All sentient beings wander through the five destinies, undergoing immeasurable suffering;
I shall likewise cause them to resolve upon Bodhicitta, to have deep faith, and to rejoice."
To cultivate diligence with steadfastness and without regression—this is the fourth seal. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas know that the wisdom of the Tathāgata is without limit;

they do not attempt to fathom the wisdom of the Tathāgata through fixed measures. Because these bodhisattvas have previously heard from immeasurable Buddhas that the wisdom of the Tathāgata is without limit, they are thus able not to measure it by means of fixed limits. All [bodhisattvas].
All that is expressed by the words of the world has its limits; none can fully know the wisdom of the Tathāgata.

This is the fifth seal. Regarding unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*), the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva attains the most supreme desire, the profound desire, the vast desire, the great desire, the manifold desire, the unconquerable desire, the unsurpassed desire, and the firm desire.
He firmly desires that all Māras and non-Buddhists, together with their retinues, shall be unable to destroy his aspiration;
he desires the unretrogressive pursuit of omniscience. When a bodhisattva dwells in such aspirations as these, he ultimately never retreats from unsurpassed enlightenment.
This is the sixth seal. When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva path, disregarding body and life, nothing can obstruct or destroy him.
Because they have resolved their minds toward omniscience; because the nature of omniscience is constantly manifest before them;
and because they have attained the light of the wisdom of all Buddhas, they never abandon the enlightenment of the Buddhas and never abandon spiritual friends.
This is the seventh seal. If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva sees a son of good family or a daughter of good family who has set out upon the Great Vehicle...
It causes them to increase their aspiration for the Buddha-dharma; it causes them to abide securely in all roots of goodness;
it causes them to embrace the mind of omniscience; and it causes them not to regress from unsurpassed enlightenment. This is the eighth seal.
By causing all sentient beings to attain a mind of equanimity and exhorting them to diligently cultivate the path to omniscience, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva...
They preach the Dharma with a heart of great compassion, causing [beings] to never regress from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
This is the ninth seal. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas share the same roots of goodness as all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
they do not sever the lineage of all Buddhas and ultimately attain the knowledge of all-knowledge (sarvajñajñāna). This is the tenth... [seal].
Ten Seals. O Son of the Buddha, these are the ten seals of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
By means of these, the Bodhisattva swiftly accomplishes *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and becomes fully endowed with the supreme seal of wisdom regarding all the dharmas of the Tathāgata.
O Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of illumination of wisdom for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten? They are:
the illumination of wisdom that knows one will certainly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; the illumination of wisdom that sees all Buddhas;
the illumination of wisdom that sees all sentient beings dying here and being born there; and the illumination of wisdom that understands all sūtras.
The light of wisdom that illuminates the Dharma-gates; the light of wisdom that arises from relying on spiritual friends to generate the bodhicitta and accumulate all roots of goodness;
the light of wisdom that manifests the presence of all Buddhas; the light of wisdom that teaches and transforms all sentient beings, causing them to dwell securely in the stage of the Tathāgata;
and the light of wisdom that expounds inconceivable and vast Dharma-gates with skillful means.
The illumination of the wisdom-light of the supernatural powers and majestic might of all Buddhas; and the illumination of the wisdom-light that fulfills all *pāramitās*.
These are the ten. If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the illumination of the supreme wisdom-light of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of peerless abodes. First:
Among all sentient beings, including śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, there is none who is equal to them. What are these ten? They are as follows:
although a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), they do not realize it, because all their vows have not yet been fully accomplished.
This is the first incomparable dwelling. A bodhisattva mahāsattva plants all roots of goodness equal to the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), yet...
In this state, there is a slight attachment; this is the second peerless dwelling (*asama-sthiti*).

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva path, knowing that all things are like illusions because all phenomena are utterly quiescent, yet does not give rise to doubt regarding the Buddha-dharma, this is the third peerless dwelling.
Although the bodhisattva mahāsattva is detached from everything belonging to the world...

This is a false conceptualization. Nevertheless, he is able to apply his attention to practicing the bodhisattva path for unspeakable eons, fulfilling his great vows without ever giving rise to a mind of weariness or fatigue in the interim; this is the fourth peerless dwelling.
The bodhisattva mahāsattva does not grasp at or cling to any phenomena, yet because the nature of all phenomena is quiescent, he does not realize nirvāṇa.
Why is this? Because the path of omniscience has not yet been fully perfected. This is the fifth peerless abiding.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva knows that all eons are in fact no eons, yet he truthfully speaks of the enumeration of all eons.
This is the sixth peerless abiding. The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva knows that all phenomena are entirely without action, yet...
Not abandoning the practice of the path while seeking all Buddha-dharmas—this is the seventh peerless dwelling.

The Bodhisattva-mahāsattva knows that the three realms are mind-only and that the three periods of time are mind-only, yet he thoroughly understands that this mind is immeasurable and boundless—this is the eighth peerless dwelling.
The Bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices for the sake of a single sentient being throughout unspeakable eons.

The Bodhisattva practice: desiring to cause [beings] to dwell securely on the stage of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-bhūmi*), he acts for all sentient beings exactly as he would for a single sentient being, without ever giving rise to weariness or fatigue. This is the ninth peerless dwelling (*anuttara-vihāra*).
Although the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices with perfection, he does not realize *bodhi*. Why is this? Because the Bodhisattva acts in this way...

He reflects: "That which I have undertaken was originally for the sake of sentient beings. Therefore, I should remain for a long time within birth-and-death (*saṃsāra*) through skillful means to benefit them, causing all to dwell securely in the unsurpassed path of the Buddha. This is the tenth peerless dwelling.
O Son of the Buddha, these are the ten kinds of peerless dwellings of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. If Bodhisattvas abide within them, they then attain...
The unsurpassed great wisdom, the peerless abiding in all Buddha-dharmas. O Son of the Buddha!
A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives rise to ten kinds of non-inferior minds. What are these ten? O Son of the Buddha! A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva forms this thought:
"I shall subdue all celestial Māras and their retinues; this is the first mind free from inferiority. Again, he forms this thought:
"I shall utterly destroy all non-Buddhists and their false teachings; this is the second mind free from inferiority.
Again, he forms this thought: "I shall use kind words to instruct and enlighten all sentient beings..."
To cause them to rejoice—this is the third mind free from inferiority. Furthermore, one forms this thought:
"I shall fully accomplish all practices of the pāramitās throughout the entire dharma-realm"—this is the fourth mind free from inferiority. Furthermore, one forms this thought:
"I shall accumulate the treasury of all merit. This is the fifth mind free from inferiority. Furthermore, one reflects:
"Unsurpassed enlightenment is vast and difficult to achieve; I shall practice so as to bring it entirely to fulfillment.
This is the sixth mind free from inferiority. Furthermore, one reflects: "I shall teach the unsurpassed and discipline the unsurpassed."
To teach and transform all sentient beings so as to bring them under control—this is the seventh mind free from inferiority.
Furthermore, one reflects: "The various worlds are all different; I shall, with infinite bodies, attain equal and perfect enlightenment.
This is the eighth mind free from inferiority. Furthermore, one reflects: "While I am practicing the bodhisattva path, if there should be any sentient beings..."

If someone comes to me to beg for my hands, feet, ears, nose, blood, flesh, marrow, bones, wife, children, elephants, horses, or even my royal throne, I am able to relinquish all such things without giving rise to a single thought of regret or sorrow.
This is solely for the benefit of all sentient beings, seeking no karmic reward; with great compassion as the foremost principle and great loving-kindness as the ultimate goal—this is the [first]...
Ninth, he possesses a mind free from inferiority. Furthermore, he reflects thus:

"All Buddhas of the three periods of time, all Buddha-dharmas, all sentient beings, all lands, all worlds, all that belongs to the three periods of time, the entire realm of empty space, the entire realm of dharmas, the entire realm of linguistic designations, and the entire realm of quiescent nirvana."
All such various phenomena, I shall fully know and fully awaken to with wisdom corresponding to a single thought-moment;
I shall fully see, fully realize, fully cultivate, and fully abandon them. Yet, within this, there is no conceptualization and freedom from conceptualization;
no manifold distinctions, no skillful artifice, and no objective sphere; it is neither existent nor non-existent, neither one nor two, by means of non-duality.
Wisdom knows all dualities: by means of signless wisdom it knows all signs; by means of non-conceptualizing wisdom it knows all conceptualizations;
by means of non-differentiating wisdom it knows all differences; by means of non-distinctive wisdom it knows all distinctions;
by means of non-worldly wisdom it knows all worlds; and by means of non-temporal wisdom it knows all times.
With the wisdom of no sentient beings, they know all sentient beings; with the wisdom of non-attachment, they know all attachments;
with the wisdom of no dwelling place, they know all dwelling places; with the wisdom of no defilement, they know all defilements;
with the wisdom of inexhaustibility, they know all that is exhausted; and with the wisdom of the ultimate realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), they manifest throughout all worlds.
With a body that demonstrates ineffable sounds through wisdom free from verbal expression; through the wisdom of a single self-nature, entering into the absence of self-nature;
through the wisdom of a single objective field, manifesting manifold objective fields; knowing all phenomena to be ineffable yet manifesting great sovereign speech;
and having realized the stage of omniscience, he acts for the purpose of teaching and disciplining all sentient beings.
Therefore, they manifest great supernormal powers and transformations throughout all worlds; this is the tenth mind that is not inferior.
O Son of the Buddha, these are the ten kinds of minds that are not inferior which a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva generates.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these minds, they will attain all the supreme, non-inferior Buddha-dharmas. O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva...
Mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of mountain-like superior resolve regarding *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. What are these ten?
O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva constantly applies the mind to diligently cultivate all dharmas of omniscience, this is the first mountain-like superior resolve.
They constantly contemplate that the intrinsic nature of all dharmas is empty and non-existent...
This is the second mountain-like superior mind. May I practice the bodhisattva conduct for immeasurable eons, cultivating all pure and white dharmas.
Because of abiding in all pure and white dharmas, may I know and see the immeasurable wisdom of the Tathāgata;
this is the third mountain-like superior mind. For the sake of seeking all Buddha-dharmas, may I maintain a mind of equanimity and reverence.
He serves all spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) without seeking anything else in return, without a mind that steals the Dharma, but giving rise only to a sense of respect and unprecedented devotion.
He is able to relinquish everything he possesses; this is the fourth mountain-like superior mind.
Even if sentient beings should revile, insult, or slander him, or strike, beat, slaughter, or dismember him, causing pain to his physical form, even unto the taking of his life—thus [he remains].
They are able to endure all such matters; they never, because of these, give rise to a disturbed mind or a mind of anger and malice.
Furthermore, they do not retreat from or abandon their great compassion and vast vows, but cause them to increase further without ceasing. Why is this?
Because the Bodhisattva has achieved the renunciation of all phenomena as they truly are and has attained the patience of all the Tathāgatas’ teachings.
Because it is supple, humble, harmonious, and autonomous, this is the fifth mountain-like superior mind.
The bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes superior great merit, namely: the superior merit of devas and the superior merit of humans.
The excellence of physical form, the excellence of power, the excellence of retinue,
the excellence of desire, the excellence of sovereignty, the excellence of mastery, the excellence of merit, and the excellence of wisdom—
though he has accomplished such excellences as these, he ultimately does not give rise to attachment toward them.
He is "clad," meaning he is not attached to flavors, not attached to sensual desires, not attached to wealth, and not attached to retinues; rather, he deeply delights in the Dharma.
He follows the Dharma, dwells in accordance with the Dharma, proceeds toward the Dharma, and reaches the ultimate consummation in the Dharma.

He takes the Dharma as his reliance, the Dharma as his refuge, the Dharma as his destination, and the Dharma as his shelter. He guards the Dharma, loves and delights in the Dharma, and yearns for the Dharma.
Contemplating the Dharma: O Son of the Buddha, although Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas fully experience various kinds of Dharma-joy, they always remain far removed from the realms of Māra.
Why is this? Because in past lives, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have given rise to such a mind:
"I shall cause all sentient beings to forever leave the realms of Māra and abide in the realm of the Buddha."

Therefore, this is the sixth mountain-like superior mind. For the sake of seeking anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, the bodhisattva mahāsattva has already practiced the bodhisattva path with diligent and tireless effort for immeasurable asaṃkhyeya kalpas;
yet he still thinks, "I have only now first resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi" and practices the bodhi-path.
They do not tremble, they are not terrified, and they have no fear regarding the practice of the bodhisattva path.

Although they are capable of attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in a single thought-moment, for the sake of sentient beings, they practice the bodhisattva path for immeasurable eons without ceasing.
This is the seventh mountain-like superior mind. The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva knows all...
Sentient beings are by nature discordant and unwholesome; they are difficult to discipline and difficult to transform. They are unable to recognize kindness and unable to repay it.
