He further manifested all kinds of flowers, perfumes, music, and young maidens, and said to Sudhana, "You may take these."
The cultivation of various merits and the giving to all sentient beings comprise nine and a half lines of scripture; these are all the functional applications of the Dharma-gates.

The reason they are manifested through giving is to signify that the Bodhisattva uses the illusory-like Dharma-gate and the four means of integration (*saṃgrahavastu*) to teach and transform sentient beings.
Thus, by being free from bondage and attachment, one transcends obstacles and reaches the state of non-obstruction.
This indicates that teaching the Dharma and benefiting sentient beings in this stage are all manifested according to what is shown. Later, he humbles himself, saying:
"I know only this liberation door of the Cloud-Net; as for the various wondrous practices of the Bodhisattvas, they are not within my knowledge.
He then extols the superior, saying: "In this Jambudvīpa, at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), there is a presiding earth goddess named Anala..."
"Stay! You may go and inquire; she will explain it for you. Then Sudhana gazed up at her, took his leave, and departed.
At that time, the youth Sudhana traveled by stages until he reached the presence of the goddess Ananyagāminī within the Bodhimaṇḍa in the kingdom of Magadha.
There were one million earth-deities dwelling together therein, who said to one another: "This youth who has come here is..."
This is the Buddha-treasury. It shall surely serve as a place of reliance for all sentient beings;
it shall surely shatter the eggshell of ignorance of all sentient beings. This person has already been born into the lineage of the Dharma King;
his head shall be crowned with the stainless, unimpeded silk-bands of the Dharma, and he shall open the great treasury of the jewels of wisdom, subduing all that is false.
Discourse on the Different Paths. At that time, ten million earth-deities, such as Anvaya and others, emitted great radiance that illuminated the trichiliocosm.
They caused the entire earth to tremble and roar simultaneously, adorning every place with various precious objects.
Their reflections were pure and their light flowed forth, mutually reflecting and penetrating one another. All tree leaves grew at once, and all flowering trees [blossomed]...
All [the trees] blossomed together; every fruit tree ripened its fruit. All rivers flowed into one another, and all ponds were completely filled.
A fine, fragrant rain fell, sprinkling the entire ground, while the wind blew, scattering flowers everywhere upon it.
Countless musical instruments played simultaneously, and the celestial ornaments all produced beautiful sounds. The oxen...
The elephant kings, lion kings, and others all gave rise to joy, leaping and roaring like the sound produced when great mountains strike one another.
At that time, a hundred-thousandfold treasuries spontaneously surged forth. Then, the earth goddess Anālayā addressed Sudhana, saying:
"Welcome, young man. You have planted roots of goodness in this very place, and thus she has appeared before you. Do you wish to see her?
At that time, Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the Earth Goddess, circumambulated her countless times, and stood with palms joined, saying, "Noble One," he said.

"Indeed, I wish to see them. At that time, the earth goddess Anvaya pressed her foot upon the ground, and hundreds of thousands of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* treasuries of jewels spontaneously welled up.
She addressed him, saying: "O son of good family, these treasuries of jewels now follow you;
they are the fruit and retribution of your past roots of goodness, and are sustained by the power of your merit. You should enjoy them according to your will and with mastery."
"Enjoyment. Good son, I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called the 'Indestructible Treasury of Wisdom.

I constantly use this dharma to bring sentient beings to maturity. Good son, I recall that since the time of Dīpaṃkara Buddha, I have always followed the Bodhisattva, reverently protecting him and observing all his mental activities, wisdom, and spheres of experience. All my vows..."
May all pure practices, all samādhis, vast and great supernormal powers, and the power of great sovereignty—
dharmas that cannot be destroyed— pervade all buddha-fields. May they universally receive the predictions of all Tathāgatas,
turn the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas, extensively expound the gateways of all sūtras, and cause the great light of the Dharma to shine everywhere.
...the radiance that teaches and tames all sentient beings and manifests the supernatural transformations of all Buddhas;

I am able to receive and retain them all in my memory. Good son, in the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru, there was an eon named Adorned and a world named Moon Banner. The Buddha there was named Wondrous Eye. Under that Buddha, I attained...

"Good son, regarding this Dharma-door, I have practiced and cultivated it through both entering and emerging from it, and thus I have constantly seen all Buddhas without ever being separated from them.

From the time I first attained it until the Bhadrakalpa, during that interval, I encountered Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields; I have met with them all."
I served, honored, and made offerings to them; I also saw those Buddhas approach the seat of enlightenment and manifest great supernormal powers.
I also saw all the roots of goodness and merits belonging to those Buddhas. Noble son, I know only this Dharma-door of the indestructible treasury of wisdom.
As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who constantly follow all Buddhas and are able to uphold everything—[I do not know their ways].
As taught by all Buddhas, they enter the profound wisdom of all Buddhas; in every thought-moment, they pervade the entire Dharma-realm;
they are equal to the bodies of Tathāgatas, give birth to the minds of all Buddhas, possess all Buddha-dharmas, and perform the works of all Buddhas.
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct? Good son, in this Jambudvīpa, in the kingdom of Magadha, at [the city of] Kāśi...
In the city of Vīra is a night goddess named Vāsantī. Go to her and ask:

"How should a bodhisattva learn the conduct of a bodhisattva and cultivate the path of a bodhisattva? Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the earth goddess, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with deep reverence, and took his leave to depart.

The tenth is the Earth Goddess Anvaya-vyūhā (Abiding in the Ground). She is entrusted with the immeasurable dedications of the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), meaning that she dedicates roots of goodness equal to the Dharma-realm back into the Dharma-realm.
The name of this spiritual friend, the Earth Goddess Anvaya-vyūhā, is derived from the fact that the earth is the support for all phenomena;
it is thus the Dharma-realm into which one enters. "Abiding" (*anvaya*) has the sense of "entering. As for "being at the site of enlightenment" (*bodhimaṇḍa*), *bodhi*...

This is the fundamental source (*mūla*). Previously, it was indicated that there is something "to the south" of the source; however, from the perspective of the source, one now subsumes the derivative (*mala*) back into the fundamental dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), and thus it is not called "south.

Furthermore, the realization of *tathatā* (suchness) on the stages (*bhūmi*) is likewise identical to this source. Since the final stage of dedication (*pariṇāmanā*) has now been reached, everything is subsumed and returned to this [source];

such is the meaning of this commentary. Generally speaking, regarding the long path, it concerns the Universal Worthy (*Samantabhadra*) practices cultivated by the preceding three levels of the stage of worthies (*śaikṣa*).

All practices are established based upon the *tathatā-dharmadhātu*. Now that the stage of dedication (*pariṇāmanā*) is fulfilled, the causes of the three levels of worthiness (*tri-śaikṣa*) reach their conclusion;
these preceding practices are subsumed and unified within a single mind as the supreme progress for entering the stages (*bhūmi*).
Since they originally flowed forth from the *dharmadhātu* and now finally return to the *dharmadhātu*, taking the stages as the fundamental *dharmadhātu*, one therefore abides therein.
The Earth Deity entrusts this dedication here; thus, the presence of one million Earth Deities within it signifies that the earth is the destination to which all myriad practices return.
Furthermore, their mutual praise of Sudhana indicates that Sudhana follows his cultivation and realization into the stage of True Suchness (*tathatā-bhūmi*).
At that time, the one million Earth Deities all emit great radiance and manifest various seeds.

Regarding the manifestation of auspicious signs: it means that upon realizing this *tathatā* (suchness), inconceivable functions arise spontaneously; therefore, without waiting for a question, they are immediately manifested.
Thus, when the earth goddess Anantaprabhā pressed the ground with her foot, ten thousand *asaṃkhyeya* treasuries of jewels spontaneously surged forth.
This precisely reveals that the *dharmadhātu* of *tathatā* is the great treasury of the jewels of merit and Dharma.
Having realized this within oneself, it is said that one may "enjoy it according to one's will. Next, he declared:
"I have attained the bodhisattva liberation named the 'Incorruptible Treasury of Wisdom. As for 'incorruptible,' that which is corruptible is ignorance."
That which is indestructible is *tathatā* (suchness) and the *tathāgatagarbha* (womb of the Tathāgata); it is also termed "wisdom. This correctly demonstrates the *dharmadhātu* (dharma-realm).
First, the name, essence, and function are indicated. The commentary states: "When the wisdom of a single thought-moment merges with the *dharmadhātu*, it is indestructible."

In this context, there is nothing that is not produced; therefore, it is called a "treasury" (*garbha*). Since the stage of the virtuous ones (*śuklavidarśanābhūmi*) has been fulfilled, the three stages of the virtuous ones are collectively integrated as the cause for entering the [first] ground (*bhūmi*).
Thus, the merit of Sudhana is revealed: his wisdom, which constantly follows the earth-deities (*bhūmidevatā*), is indestructible.

This means that the former causes are not lost, and he is thus able to enter into realization. Next, from the passage "I recall... onwards, the specific functions [of this treasury] are individually revealed.
Next, the passage beginning with "In the distant past" reveals the time and place where the Dharma was attained. Next, the section beginning with "I, at...
summarizes the exclusive heat (*ūṣmagata*). Then, he humbles himself, saying: "I know only this Dharma-gate of the indestructible treasury of wisdom;
as for the superior practices such as those bodhisattvas who enter the profound wisdom of all Buddhas, they are not within my knowledge. Thus...
Pushyadeva said, "In this Jambudvīpa, there is a night goddess named Vāsantī. You should go and ask her; she will explain it for you.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the earth goddess, gazed up at her with reverence, took his leave, and departed.
This concludes the ten stages of Dedication (*pariṇāmanā*); hereafter follow the ten stages (*bhūmi*).
At that time, the youth Sudhana, with single-minded contemplation, dwelt in the divine teaching.

He recollected the Bodhisattva’s liberation of the indestructible treasury of wisdom; he cultivated its samādhi, studied its regulations, observed its playful manifestations, entered its subtlety, attained its wisdom, realized its equality, knew its boundlessness, and fathomed its profound depth, proceeding gradually.
Traveling on, he arrived at that city. Having entered through the eastern gate and stood there for no long time, he saw the sun set.

In his mind, he followed the instructions of all the Bodhisattvas; thirsting with longing to see that Night Goddess, he conceived the thought of the Tathāgata toward the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra).
He further reflected: "Through the spiritual friend, one obtains the universal eye, which can clearly perceive all ten directions."
Regarding the spheres of experience: through spiritual friends, one attains vast understanding and is able to universally comprehend all objects of focus.
Through spiritual friends, one attains the eye of samādhi and is able to universally observe all dharma-gates.

Through spiritual friends, one attains the eye of wisdom and is able to universally and clearly illuminate the ocean of lands in the ten directions. While he was reflecting thus, he saw that night goddess in the void.
In the midst of the sky, he sat upon a lion throne within a precious pavilion, adorned with fragrant lotuses. His body was the color of pure gold;
his eyes and hair were deep azure. His physical form was upright and majestic, bringing joy to all who beheld him.

He was adorned with necklaces and ornaments made of various jewels, wearing crimson robes and a Brahma-crown upon his head. All the constellations shone vividly upon his body, and upon each part of his person...

From every pore, there appeared the manifestation of the deliverance of immeasurable and innumerable sentient beings of the evil realms, showing them images of their liberation from perilous hardships.

These sentient beings were either born among humans, or born in the heavens, or were directed toward the enlightenment of the two vehicles, or were practicing the path to omniscience. Furthermore, within each and every one of those pores, he manifested:
Through various skillful means of instruction, they may manifest their physical forms, or preach the Dharma,

or manifest the path of the Śrāvaka vehicle, or manifest the path of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, or manifest the practices of all Bodhisattvas— namely, the Bodhisattva’s valor, the Bodhisattva’s samādhis,
the Bodhisattva’s masteries, the Bodhisattva’s abodes, and the Bodhisattva’s contemplations. The Bodhisattva...
The lion yawned and stretched; the Bodhisattva’s liberation was a playful manifestation. In these various ways, he brought sentient beings to maturity.

Having seen and heard this, the youth Sudhana was filled with great joy. He prostrated himself upon the ground, paid homage at the feet of the night goddess, circumambulated her countless times, and standing before her with palms joined, spoke these words: "Noble One, I have already set my mind upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi..."
“...the mind of *samyaksambodhi*. My heart hopes to rely upon spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) to obtain the treasury of the dharmas of the merits of all Tathāgatas.
I only pray that you will show me the path to omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), so that as I travel along it, I may reach the stage of the Ten Powers (*daśabala-bhūmi*).
Then that night goddess said to Sudhana: “Excellent, excellent, noble son! You are able, with a profound mind, to revere spiritual friends...”
They recognize it, delight in hearing its words, and practice its teachings. Because they practice them, they will certainly attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Good son, I have attained the Bodhisattva liberation called "The Radiance of the Dharma that Shatters the Darkness of Ignorance in All Sentient Beings.
Good son, toward sentient beings of evil wisdom, I give rise to a heart of great compassion. Toward those who are...
One gives rise to great compassion toward sentient beings who perform wholesome deeds; one gives rise to sympathetic joy toward sentient beings who perform wholesome deeds;

one gives rise to a mind of non-duality toward sentient beings who engage in both wholesome and unwholesome conduct; and one gives rise to a mind that inspires purity toward sentient beings who are free from defilement.
I give rise to the thought of causing those on wrong paths to produce right practice; I give rise to the thought of causing those of inferior understanding to develop great understanding;
I give rise to the thought of causing those who delight in birth and death to renounce cyclic existence;

and I give rise to the thought of causing those dwelling in the paths of the two vehicles to abide in the mind of omniscience. Son of good family, because I have attained this liberation, I am always with...
Thus, the mind is associated [with these]. Good son, when it is dark at night and quiet, and when ghosts, spirits, thieves, robbers, and various evil beings roam about;

when thick clouds, heavy mists, fierce winds, and torrential rains obscure the sun, moon, and stars so that no forms can be seen—at such times, I see sentient beings whether they have entered the sea or are traveling on land, or upon the mountains.
In forests, wildernesses, and various perilous places, whether they encounter bandits, lack provisions, become confused about the directions,
or lose their way, and are thus terrified, anxious, and unable to escape— I at that time rescue them through various skillful means.
For those in maritime distress, I manifest as a shipmaster, a king of fish, a king of horses, a king of turtles, or a king of elephants.
The king, the asura kings, and the sea deities, for the sake of those sentient beings, stilled the violent winds and rains and calmed the great waves;
they guided their paths and showed them the islands and shores, enabling them to escape fear and attain complete peace and security. Furthermore, they formed this thought:
"By means of these roots of goodness, I dedicate them to sentient beings, wishing that they may abandon all sufferings. For those on land...

For all sentient beings on earth who encounter terror in the darkness of night, he manifests the light of the sun, moon, various constellations, morning mists, evening lightning, and diverse radiances;
or he manifests as dwellings, or as throngs of people, causing them to escape the calamity of fear.
Furthermore, he forms this thought: "I dedicate these roots of goodness to all sentient beings, so that they may all be freed from [fear]."

I extinguish the darkness of all afflictions. Among all sentient beings, there are those who cherish their lives, those who crave fame, those who covet wealth and treasures, those who prize official rank, those who are attached to sons and daughters, and those who dote on wives and concubines; when their desires are not fulfilled, they give rise to much sorrow and fear.
I rescue them all, causing them to be free from suffering. For those who encounter obstacles while traveling through mountainous and perilous regions, I act as a virtuous guide.
The deity manifests a form and approaches them; he becomes a beautiful bird to utter sounds that bring comfort and joy; he becomes a divine medicine to radiate light and illuminate;
he shows them fruit trees, he shows them springs and wells, he shows them the straight path, and he shows them level ground, causing them to escape all misfortunes and distress.
When they travel through vast wildernesses, dense forests, treacherous paths entangled with creeping vines, or shrouded in clouds and mist...
To those who are shrouded in darkness and filled with fear, he shows the true path so that they may attain liberation. He forms this thought:

"May all sentient beings clear away the dense forest of views, sever the net of craving, emerge from the wilderness of birth and death, extinguish the afflictions and attachments, enter the level and true path of omniscience, and reach the state of fearlessness and ultimate peace. Good son, if there are sentient beings...
For those who give rise to attachment toward their country and experience sorrow and suffering, I employ skillful means to cause them to develop weary detachment. I form this thought:
"May all sentient beings not be attached to the aggregates (*skandhas*), but abide in the realm of the *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge) of all Buddhas.
Good son, if there are sentient beings who take pleasure in and are attached to villages, who crave and love their homes, and who constantly dwell in darkness and undergo various sufferings—
For such beings, I teach the Dharma to inspire in them a sense of weary detachment, to bring their practice to fulfillment, and to cause them to abide in accordance with the Dharma.
I form this thought: "May all sentient beings no longer crave or delight in the village of the six sense bases;

may they swiftly attain liberation from the realm of birth and death, and ultimately dwell securely within the city of omniscience. Good son, if there are sentient beings who travel through the darkness of night...
They are deluded within the ten directions, perceiving level roads as perilous and perceiving perilous paths as level;
they mistake the high for the low and the low for the high. Their minds being thus confused, they give rise to great suffering and distress.
I, by means of skillful expedients, extend my light to reach them; to those who wish to emerge, I show the gateway, and to those who wish to travel, I show the path.
On the road, when they wish to cross ditches and moats, he shows them the bridges; when they wish to ford rivers and seas, he provides them with boats and rafts.
To those who delight in observing the directions, he shows the dangers and the easy paths. To those who wish to rest in places of safety, he points out cities, water sources, and groves of trees.
He forms this thought: "Just as I have here illuminated and dispelled the darkness of night, so shall I cause all worldly affairs to be fully proclaimed."
Preface: May I universally illuminate with the light of wisdom all sentient beings within the dark places of ignorance throughout the long night of birth and death.

These sentient beings lack the eye of wisdom; they are shrouded and obscured by the inversions of perception, thought, and view—conceiving the impermanent as permanent, the suffering as happiness, the non-self as self, and the impure as pure, clinging to these views with firm tenacity.

They are attached to the notions of self, person, sentient being, and the aggregates, elements, and sense bases; they are deluded regarding cause and effect and fail to distinguish between good and evil.
They commit violence against sentient beings and even hold wrong views. They are unfilial toward their parents and show no respect for śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas.
They do not recognize the wicked nor understand the virtuous. They are greedily attached to evil deeds, dwell securely in false teachings, and slander the Tathāgata while destroying the True Dharma.
Wheel: [Those who] revile, humiliate, and harm bodhisattvas; disparage the Mahāyāna path and sever the bodhicitta; commit murder against those who have been kind to them;
harbor perpetual resentment toward those who have done them no wrong; slander the noble ones and associate with evil companions;
steal the property of stupas and monasteries and commit the five heinous crimes—such persons shall before long fall into the three evil realms. May I quickly...
With the light of great wisdom, they shatter the dark ignorance of those sentient beings, causing them to swiftly resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Once they have resolved their minds, they show them the vehicle of Samantabhadra and open the path of the ten powers;
they also show them the realm of the Tathāgata, the Dharma King, as well as the city of all-knowledge of all Buddhas and the conduct practiced by all Buddhas.
The Buddha is sovereign; he has accomplished the dhāraṇīs of all Buddhas. All Buddhas share a single body.
He causes them to dwell securely in the state of equality that is common to all Buddhas.
Good son, when all sentient beings are either entangled by illness, assailed by old age, afflicted by poverty, beset by calamities, or face the execution of royal law...
When they are subjected to punishment and have no one to rely upon, giving rise to great fear, I shall rescue them all and bring them peace and security.

Furthermore, I make this vow: "May I universally gather in all sentient beings through the Dharma, causing them to be liberated from all afflictions, birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, and distress;
may they draw near to spiritual friends, constantly practice the gift of Dharma, diligently perform virtuous deeds, and swiftly attain [enlightenment]."
The Tathāgata’s pure *dharmakāya* abides in the ultimate state of changelessness. Good son, all sentient beings enter the dense forest of views and abide in false paths;
they give rise to false discrimination regarding all objects of experience and constantly perform unwholesome actions of body, speech, and mind.
They falsely engage in various kinds of erroneous ascetic practices and perceive that which is not true awakening as being true awakening.
He perceives those who, regarding the Truly Awakened One as not truly awakened, are influenced by evil associates and, having given rise to wrong views, are about to fall into the evil realms.
I protect and rescue them through various skillful means, causing them to abide in right view and be reborn among humans and devas.
Furthermore, he reflects: "Just as I have rescued these sentient beings who were about to fall into the evil realms..."

...and so forth. May I universally rescue all sentient beings, causing them all to be liberated from every form of suffering, to abide in the supramundane noble path of the *pāramitās*, and to attain non-retrogression regarding omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).

May I fulfill the vows of Samantabhadra, draw near to omniscience, yet never abandon the practices of a bodhisattva. May I always diligently teach and transform all sentient beings. At that time, the World-Honored One...
The Night Goddess Śāntāpraśāntā, wishing to restate the meaning of this liberation, received the Buddha’s spiritual power,
surveyed the ten directions for the sake of the youth Sudhana, and spoke these verses:
This gate of liberation of mine Gives rise to the light of pure dharmas; It can shatter the darkness of ignorance, And is expounded when the time is right.
In the past, throughout boundless eons, I diligently practiced vast compassion That universally covered all worlds.
Sons of the Buddha, you should practice and learn this: The ocean of tranquil and pure great compassion.

The birthplace of the Buddhas of the three times, Who can extinguish the suffering of sentient beings— You should enter this gate, which can produce worldly happiness And also produce supramundane bliss; It makes my heart rejoice— You should enter this gate.
Having abandoned the afflictions of the conditioned, One also remains far from the fruit of the śrāvaka.
Purify the powers of all Buddhas; you should enter this gate.

My eyes are exceedingly pure, seeing the lands of the ten directions everywhere, and I also see the Buddhas therein, sitting beneath the Bodhi trees with bodies adorned by the marks and signs of excellence, surrounded by immeasurable multitudes—within every single pore.
Various kinds of light emerge, revealing all classes of sentient beings;
dying here and being born there, they cycle through the five destinies, constantly undergoing immeasurable suffering. My ears are exceedingly pure;
there is nothing they do not reach as I listen. The ocean of all speech and sounds, I hear it all and am able to remember and maintain it.
The Buddhas turn the wheel of Dharma, Its sound is wondrous and beyond compare; All written characters can be remembered and maintained.
My nose is exceedingly pure, Unobstructed regarding all phenomena, Mastering them all with total freedom. You should enter this gate; My tongue is exceedingly vast.
Pure and eloquent, you expound the wondrous Dharma according to what is appropriate; you should enter this gate.
My body is utterly pure, equal to suchness throughout the three times; it appears in accordance with the minds of all sentient beings, manifesting in every way.
My mind is pure and unimpeded, like space containing the myriad phenomena.
Universally mindful of all Tathāgatas, yet without making any distinctions;
Thoroughly knowing the oceans of all minds, the faculties, and the inclinations within infinite lands, yet without making any distinctions;
By means of my great supernormal powers, I cause infinite lands to tremble, and my body pervades them all.
Taming those who are difficult to tame, my merit is exceedingly vast; Like space, it is inexhaustible as I make offerings to all Tathāgatas.
Benefiting all beings, my wisdom is broad and pure, Thoroughly knowing the ocean of all dharmas;
I eliminate the delusions of sentient beings— You should enter this gateway.
I know the Buddhas of the three periods of time, As well as all phenomena; I also understand their skillful means.

This gateway is everywhere peerless; Within every single atom, I see all lands of the three periods of time, And I also see those Buddhas therein— This is the power of the Universal Gateway, Within the atoms of the lands of the ten directions.
I see Vairocana in his entirety, seated beneath the Bodhi tree; having attained enlightenment, he expounds the wondrous Dharma.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to the Night Goddess: "How long has it been since you first resolved your mind toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?
How long has it been since you attained this liberation, that you are able to bring such benefit?"

"Sentient beings," the deity replied, "Noble son, in the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru, there was an eon named Tranquil Light and a world named Source of Wondrous Jewels. Within that world, five hundred million Buddhas appeared.
In that world, there was a set of four continents named Jewel Moon Lamp Light, and within it a city named Lotus."
In the world named Padmaprabha, there was a king named Dharmamativikrama who transformed others through the gift of Dharma and possessed the seven treasures. He ruled over the four continents.
The king had a queen named Dharmamaticandrā. One night, while she was deep in sleep, there was a great forest to the east of that city called Śāntavihāra.
Within that forest stood a great Bodhi tree named Sarvālokamaṇirājavyūha.

The body produces the light of the spiritual powers of all Buddhas. At that time, there was a Buddha named Sarvadharma-ghoṣarāja (King of the Thunder-Sound of All Dharmas) who attained equal and perfect enlightenment beneath this tree.
He emitted a vast radiance of immeasurable colors, which shone everywhere throughout the world-system of Utpannasurabhi-ratna (Born of Wondrous Jewels).
Within the city of Padma (Lotus), there was a night goddess named Vimalacandrā (Pure Moon) who went to the wife of the king.
The Man of Human Dharma, at the abode of Wisdom Moon, moved his body’s ornaments to awaken the Lady and addressed her, saying:
"Lady, you should know that the Tathāgata Sarvadharmanirghoṣarāja has attained unexcelled enlightenment in the Forest of Tranquil Abiding.
He has extensively expounded upon the merits, sovereign spiritual powers, and all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva for the sake of the King and his Lady."
A person has resolved their mind toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and makes offerings to that Buddha, as well as to the assembly of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas.
Good son, was the King’s consort, Dharmamati-candrā, anyone else? It was none other than my own self.
Because I resolved my mind toward bodhicitta and planted roots of goodness in the presence of that Buddha, on Mount Sumeru...
For as many eons as there are atoms, they shall not be born in the various evil realms of hell, hungry ghosts, or animals;
nor shall they be born into lowly families. With all faculties complete and free from manifold sufferings, they will possess preeminent merit and virtue among gods and humans.
He will not be born in an evil age; he will never be separated from Buddhas, bodhisattvas, and great spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), and will constantly plant roots of goodness in their presence.
For eighty kalpas, as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, he will always experience peace and happiness, yet he will not yet have perfected the faculties (indriya) of a bodhisattva.
After these kalpas have passed, and after another ten thousand kalpas, there will be a kalpa prior to the Bhadrakalpa.
The name of the world was Samantāvabhāsa-vigata-śoka (Universal Illumination Free from Sorrow), and the name of the world-system was Vimala-prabhā-sudarśana (Stainless Wondrous Light).
That world was a mixture of purity and impurity, and five hundred Buddhas appeared therein. The first of those Buddhas was named Sumeru-dhvaja-śānta-sudarśana Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
At that time, I was the daughter of the elder Yaśas, named Prajñāloka (Light of Wisdom); I was beautiful and upright.

It is most wonderful. By the power of her vows, that Night Goddess Pure Moon was born in the city of King Wondrous Banner within a single four-continent world-system in the Stainless World, where she serves as the presiding Night Goddess named Pure Eye.
Once, while I was sleeping late at night beside my parents, that Pure Eye came to me, shook my residence, and emitted a great light.
A radiance appeared from his body, praising the virtues of the Buddha and saying:
"The Tathāgata Sublime Eye has sat upon the seat of enlightenment and has just attained perfect awakening. He exhorts me, my parents, and all our kinsmen to quickly behold the Buddha.
Acting as our guide, he led us to the presence of the Buddha, where we extensively offered worship. As soon as I beheld the Buddha, I immediately attained a samādhi named...
Upon birth, one perceives the wheel of light of the wisdom of the three times that tames sentient beings through seeing the Buddhas.
Because of attaining this samādhi, one is able to recollect as many eons as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru, and also beholds the appearance of all those Buddhas therein.
Having heard the sublime Dharma from those Buddhas, by virtue of hearing that Dharma, one immediately attains this "Light of the Dharma that Shatters the Darkness of All Sentient Beings."
He clearly understands liberation. Having attained this liberation, he immediately sees his own body traveling throughout worlds as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field.
He also sees all the Buddhas present in those worlds, and sees himself in the presence of each of those Buddhas. Furthermore, he sees all sentient beings in those worlds;
he understands their speech and sounds, recognizes their faculties and natures, and knows their past histories.
I was sustained by spiritual friends who manifested their bodies according to my inclinations to inspire joy in me.

At that time, the liberation I attained increased with every thought-moment. Immediately following this state of mind, I again saw myself traveling everywhere throughout worlds as numerous as the atoms in a hundred buddha-fields. Immediately following this state of mind, I again saw myself traveling everywhere throughout a thousand...

In worlds as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, this mind, without interruption, again perceives its own body traveling throughout worlds as numerous as the atoms within hundreds of thousands of Buddha-fields.
Thus, in every thought-moment, it continues until it reaches worlds as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;
therein, it also perceives all the Tathāgatas within those worlds, and likewise perceives its own body therein.
There, he heard the sublime Dharma from that Buddha, receiving, upholding, recollecting, observing, and fully comprehending it.
He also came to know that Buddha’s ocean of past deeds and ocean of great vows. "Just as those Tathāgatas have purified their buddha-fields, so shall I purify mine.
He also beheld all sentient beings in those worlds and manifested his body to them according to their needs, teaching, transforming, and subduing them.
This gate of liberation increases moment by moment, continuing in this manner until it completely fills the dharma-realm.
Good son, I know only this bodhisattva liberation called "The Radiance of the Dharma that Shatters the Darkness of All Sentient Beings.
As for those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have accomplished the boundless practices and vows of Samantabhadra, who universally enter all oceans of the dharma-realm, and who have attained...
The Bodhisattvas’ Samādhi of Sovereign Vajra-Wisdom Banner gives birth to great vows that sustain the lineage of the Buddhas;
in every thought-moment, they fulfill the ocean of all great merits and purify all vast worlds.
With sovereign wisdom, they teach and mature all sentient beings; with the sun of wisdom, they extinguish all worldly [defilements].
Dispelling the darkness of the intervening obscurations, they awaken all sentient beings from their stupor and sleep with courageous wisdom.
With the moon of wisdom, they resolve all the doubts and delusions of sentient beings. With pure sound, they sever all attachments to existence.
Within every single atom of the entire dharma-realm, they manifest all sovereign spiritual powers, their eye of wisdom being bright and clear.
They perceive the three periods of time equally; how then could I know their wondrous conduct, speak of their merits, enter their realms, or demonstrate their sovereign mastery?
Good son, within the Bodhimaṇḍa in the kingdom of Magadha here in Jambudvīpa, there is a night goddess named Samantaguṇaviśuddhaprabhā.
It was from her that I originally set forth toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
"Bodhicitta constantly awakens me with the sublime Dharma. Go to her and ask:
'How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path? At that time, the youth Sudhana turned toward the goddess Vasanti.
And he spoke in verse:
I behold your pure body, With marks and signs surpassing the world;
Like Mañjuśrī, and like the king of jewel mountains, Your Dharma-body is pure, Equal throughout the three times.
The entire world enters within you, And yet the processes of formation and destruction meet no obstruction.
As I contemplate all realms of existence, I see your form everywhere; Within each and every pore, Stars and moons are distributed one by one.
Your mind is utterly vast, Pervading the ten directions like space, Into which all Buddhas enter.
Pure and free from discrimination, From within each and every pore, He emits countless rays of light;
To the abodes of all Buddhas throughout the ten directions, He rains down everywhere articles of adornment.
From within each and every pore, He manifests countless bodies; Throughout the lands of the ten directions, He delivers sentient beings through skillful means.
Within each and every pore, you manifest immeasurable lands; according to the various desires of sentient beings, you cause them all to be purified.

If there are sentient beings who hear your name or behold your body, they shall all obtain the benefit of merit and virtue, accomplishing the path to Bodhi, even if they have remained in the evil realms for many eons.
Now that you have finally been seen and heard, you too should receive this with joy; for by extinguishing the afflictions,
even if one were to praise the virtue of a single pore of yours for as many eons as there are atoms in a thousand lands, the number of eons might yet be exhausted,
but your merit would never end.
When the youth Sudhana had finished reciting these verses, he prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep reverence,
and then took his leave and departed.
From here begins the fifth major section, which contains ten virtuous friends corresponding to the ten stages (*bhūmi*). This is divided into ten parts.

The first is the Night Goddess Vāsantī, who corresponds to the Stage of Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*). Regarding "Joy" (*pramudita*): it refers to the initial attainment of the nature of a noble one (*ārya-dharma*).

It is so called because it fully realizes the two kinds of emptiness and is able to benefit oneself and others, thereby giving rise to great joy. As for the city named Kapilavastu, this translates as "Yellow.
In the past, the Rishi Kapila resided in this place; yellow is the intermediate color, and its color accords with the Middle Way.
Furthermore, it is the city where the Buddha was born, signifying birth into the family of the Buddhas at the first stage (bhūmi). Vāsava...

"Vasanta" means spring. "Vasanti" means lord. Because she presides over the crops during the springtime, it signifies that upon first entering the stages (*bhūmi*), one is able to cause the myriad practices to grow and protect sentient beings.
As for the frequent appearance of night goddesses (*rātridevatā*) on the stages, it is because their realized wisdom is profound and subtle, free from signs, and dispels darkness.
Regarding the initial reliance on the teachings to seek [the goal], one first relies on the preceding...
Having cultivated and realized [this], the youth Sudhana contemplated with single-minded focus, training to enter that wisdom and fathom its profound depth.
Traveling by stages, he arrived at that city and entered through the eastern gate. Before long, the sun set;
yet Sudhana’s mind remained filled with longing to behold [the sage] and to obtain the eye of wisdom that can universally and clearly illumine the ocean of lands in the ten directions.
While he was reflecting thus, the night goddess previously seen in the void, seated upon a lion throne within a lotus treasury, appeared with a majestic and sublime physical form.

From every single pore of her body, there manifested the transformation and deliverance of immeasurable sentient beings of the six realms, as well as their various maturations through the three vehicles. Upon seeing this, Sudhana was filled with joy.
With joy and reverence, he paid homage and, having set forth his resolve, inquired about the essential points of the Dharma. At that time, the night goddess praised him and bestowed the teaching;

first she praised his resolve, then she correctly revealed the Dharma-realm, saying: "I have attained the Bodhisattva liberation called 'The Radiance of the Dharma that Shatters All Darkness of Ignorance.
Following this, she extensively demonstrated its functional activity: 'Toward sentient beings of evil wisdom, I give rise to great compassion.'"
The mind and so forth are of various and distinct types; there are eight kinds of minds that provide benefit as appropriate.
Below this, sixty-four lines of scripture enumerate ten categories, such as responding to rescue from calamity and uprooting suffering. All of these are the functional activities of this liberation.
First, one rescues the world from suffering and enables it to attain worldly happiness; subsequently, through dedication by means of great vows, one causes [beings] to attain...

Thus they ultimately leave suffering behind and attain happiness. At that time, the Night Goddess Vāsantī, having already explained these ten gates concerning the rescue from calamities, further spoke in verse to restate her previous meaning, comprehensively clarifying the vastness of her karmic functions.
At that time, Sudhana asked about the duration since his initial resolve (*cittotpāda*).

The Night Goddess recounted in detail her past causes and conditions over nineteen lines of scripture, fully describing the causal circumstances of her former lives in response to the question regarding the timing of his resolve.

Subsequently, with twenty-four and a half lines of scripture following "After this kalpa," she answered the question regarding the length of time since she attained the Dharma. This collectively reveals [the full extent of her realization].

Regarding the causal conditions of the Dharma: this is presented to clarify that one enters the stages (*bhūmi*) by extensively accumulating many practices and cultivating causes over successive kalpas until reaching this particular stage.
Next, he expresses humility, saying: "I know only this liberation of the Bodhisattva’s Dharma-light that shatters the darkness of all sentient beings;
as for the boundless practices and vows of Samantabhadra accomplished by other Bodhisattvas, I do not know them."

"This vast Dharma gate is not within my knowledge. She then recommended Vimaladattā, saying, "Within this Bodhimaṇḍa, there is a night goddess named Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā. You should go and ask her; she will explain it for you.
At that time, after the youth Sudhana had praised the night goddess's virtues with verses, he prostrated at her feet, gazed upon her with earnest devotion, and took his leave.
And he departed.
