Entering the Dharma Realm, Chapter Thirty-nine, Part Ten. At that time,
the youth Sudhana clearly understood the treasury of bodhisattvas born from that night goddess Vasanti’s initial aspiration for enlightenment,
the vows she had made as a bodhisattva, the perfections she had purified as a bodhisattva, and the bodhisattva stages she had entered.
The stages, the bodhisattva practices he had cultivated, the path of renunciation he had traversed, the ocean of light of omniscience that universally rescues sentient beings,
and the clouds of universal great compassion— these were able to constantly give rise to the conduct and vows of Samantabhadra throughout all buddha-fields until the end of the future.
Proceeding gradually, he arrived at the place of the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, prostrated at her feet, and circumambulated her.
Having circumambulated him countless times, he joined his palms before him and spoke these words:
"Noble One, I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should practice the stages of a bodhisattva."
"How is the bodhisattva stage produced? How is the bodhisattva stage accomplished? The night goddess replied, "Excellent, excellent, son of good family!

You have already been able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and now you further inquire about the production and accomplishment of the practice of the bodhisattva stages. Son of good family, when a bodhisattva accomplishes..."
Regarding ten dharmas, one is able to bring the bodhisattva practice to fulfillment. What are these ten?
First, attaining pure samādhi and constantly seeing all Buddhas. Second, attaining the pure eye and constantly beholding the marks and signs that adorn all Buddhas.
Third, they know the great ocean of the immeasurable and boundless merits of all Tathāgatas.
Fourth, they know the ocean of the light of the infinite Buddha-dharmas, which is equal to the Dharma-realm.

Fifth, they know that each and every pore of all Tathāgatas emits a great ocean of light rays, as numerous as all sentient beings, benefiting immeasurable and infinite sentient beings. Sixth, they see...
Seventh, from every single pore of all Tathāgatas, there issues forth an ocean of flaming radiance in the colors of all jewels;

in every thought-moment, they manifest oceans of the transformations of all Buddhas that fill the Dharma-realm, ultimately bringing sentient beings to maturity within the sphere of activity of all Buddhas.
Eighth, they attain the voice of a Buddha, which accords with the speech and sounds of all sentient beings.
9. The ocean of knowing the infinite names and titles of all Buddhas;
10. The ocean of knowing the inconceivable and sovereign power of all Buddhas to discipline sentient beings.
Son of good family, when a bodhisattva accomplishes these ten dharmas, they are able to fulfill all the practices of a bodhisattva. Son of good family, I have attained...
The liberation of the bodhisattva is called "Tranquil Joy of Universal Wandering in Meditative Concentration.
It universally perceives all Buddhas of the three periods of time, as well as those Buddhas' pure lands, sites of enlightenment, assemblies, supernormal powers, names, teachings, and lifespans.
Although their voices, physical forms, and various characteristics differ, they perceive them all clearly without attachment. Why is this?

One knows that all Tathāgatas do not depart, because the worldly realms have been eternally extinguished; they do not come, because their essential nature is unborn; they are not born, because the Dharma-body is equal;
they do not perish, because they lack the characteristics of arising; they are not real, because they abide in illusion-like phenomena; they are not false, because they benefit sentient beings;
they do not transmigrate, because they have transcended birth and death; and they do not decay, because their nature is eternal and unchanging.
It is of one mark, for it is entirely free from speech and language. It is markless, for its nature and characteristics are fundamentally empty.

Good son, when I thus realized all Tathāgatas, my joyful experience of the bodhisattva’s tranquil meditative concentration, the liberation door of universal roaming, became clearly understood, attained, increased, contemplated, observed, firmly adorned, and not a single [thought of] arising occurred.
Cutting off all false conceptualizations and discriminations, he protects and saves all sentient beings with great compassion.

With a single, unmoving mind, he cultivates the first dhyāna, stilling all mental karma and gathering in all sentient beings. With courageous power of wisdom and a heart of joyful gladness, he cultivates the second dhyāna.
Contemplating the intrinsic nature of all sentient beings and feeling weary of and detached from birth and death, he cultivates the third dhyāna. All...
They are able to extinguish all the suffering, heat, and afflictions of all sentient beings. They cultivate the fourth dhyāna, increasing and perfecting the vows for omniscience.
They give birth to the ocean of all samādhis and enter the gates of the ocean of bodhisattva liberations.
They sport with all supernatural powers and accomplish all transformations. Through pure wisdom, they universally enter the Dharma-realm. Skillful...
"Good man, when I cultivate this liberation, I bring sentient beings to maturity through various skillful means.

That is to say, for those lay beings who are heedless, I cause them to conceive the perception of impurity, the perception of loathsomeness, the perception of exhaustion, and the perception of oppression."

The perception of bondage; the perception of rākṣasas; the perception of impermanence; the perception of suffering; the perception of non-self; the perception of emptiness; the perception of non-arising;

the perception of lack of self-mastery; and the perception of old age, sickness, and death. One does not give rise to attachment or delight in the five desires oneself, and likewise encourages sentient beings not to cling to sensual pleasures but to abide solely in the joy of the Dharma.
Having departed from the household life to enter the homeless state, if there are sentient beings who dwell therein...

In the midst of space, I shall silence all evil sounds. During the stillness of the night, I shall preach the profound Dharma, provide favorable conditions, open the gate of renunciation, and show the true path.
I shall act as a light to remove the veil of darkness, extinguish their fears, and praise the practice of renunciation.
I shall extol the virtues of the Buddha, the Dharma, the Sangha, and spiritual friends. Furthermore—

This is a praise of the practice of drawing near to spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). Furthermore, noble son, when I was cultivating liberation, I caused all sentient beings not to give rise to unrighteous craving, not to produce false discrimination, and not to commit various sinful deeds; if they had already committed them, I caused them all to cease.
As for those who had not yet produced wholesome dharmas, had not yet cultivated the practices of the *pāramitās*, or had not yet sought omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), [I caused them to do so].
I cause those who have not yet given rise to great compassion and have not yet performed the karma for rebirth among humans or devas to all be born [in such states];

and for those already so born, I cause them to increase [in virtue]. I provide them with such favorable conditions conducive to the Path, even until they achieve the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).
Good son, I have attained only this Bodhisattva liberation door of the Universal Gait, which is the bliss of tranquil meditative concentration; as for those others...
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva fulfills all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra. He thoroughly understands the entire boundless Dharma-realm and is constantly able to increase all roots of goodness.
He illuminates and perceives the power of wisdom of all Tathāgatas and abides in the sphere of all Tathāgatas.
Ever dwelling within birth and death, his mind is free from obstruction, and he is swiftly able to fulfill all-knowledge.
I vow that they may be able to travel to all worlds, behold all Buddhas, and universally receive and uphold all Buddha-dharmas;

that they may shatter the darkness of ignorance of all sentient beings and give rise to the light of all-encompassing wisdom within the great night of birth and death. How could I possibly know or describe their merits?
"Go, noble son. Not far from here, on the right side of the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), there is a night goddess named Joyful Sun Observing Sentient Beings.
Go to her and ask: 'How does a bodhisattva learn the conduct of a bodhisattva and cultivate the path of a bodhisattva?
At that time, the night goddess Samantaguṇaviśuddhaprabhā, wishing to restate the meaning of this liberation, spoke for the sake of the youth Sudhana:
Then he spoke in verse:
"If one possesses a mind of faith and understanding, They shall see all Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Such a person’s eyes are pure, And they can enter the ocean of all Buddhas. Behold the bodies of the Buddhas, Adorned with pure marks."
With the supernatural power of a single thought, he fills the entire Dharma-realm.
The Tathāgata Vairocana attained perfect enlightenment at the site of awakening; Throughout all realms of phenomena, he turns the pure wheel of Dharma.
The Tathāgata knows the nature of dharmas, which are quiescent and non-dual; His body is adorned with the marks of purity.

Universally manifesting throughout all worlds, the Buddha’s body is inconceivable; it completely fills the entire Dharma-realm and appears everywhere in all lands. There is nowhere that it is not seen.
The Buddha’s body is ever-luminous, equal in number to the atoms within all lands, possessing various pure colors, pervading the Dharma-realm in every thought-moment.
From a single pore of the Tathāgata, He emits inconceivable light, Universally illuminating all sentient beings And causing their afflictions to be extinguished.
From a single pore of the Tathāgata, He produces inexhaustible emanations that pervade the entire Dharma-realm, Eliminating the suffering of sentient beings. The Buddha utters a single sublime sound;
Causing all to understand according to their kind, He rains down the vast and great Dharma everywhere, Causing them to resolve upon Bodhicitta.
In the past, when the Buddha cultivated various practices, He already took me under his care; Therefore, I am able to see the Tathāgata Manifesting universally in all lands.
The Buddhas appear in the world, Their number equal to that of all sentient beings.
The various realms of liberation are not within my power to know;
that all Bodhisattvas enter into a single pore of the Buddha—such wondrous liberation is not within my power to know.
Nearby there is a night goddess named Joyful Eyes Who Observes; you should go to her.
Question: When practicing the bodhisattva path,
Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed upon him with deep reverence, and then took his leave and departed.
The second night goddess, Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, represents the spiritual friend of the Stainless Stage (*vimalā-bhūmi*).
The Stainless Stage refers to truly pure ethical discipline (*śīla*), for it is free from the defilements of afflictions that could give rise to even subtle transgressions.
Because the youth Sudhana understood the causes and conditions by which that night goddess, Vāsantī, first resolved upon awakening (*bodhicitta*), [he attained this stage].
Recalling the ten kinds of supreme practices that arise from such thought, he followed the instructions to seek them out.

He went to the presence of the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, where he beheld her, paid his respects, inquired after her well-being, prostrated with palms joined, and first set forth his resolve for enlightenment before asking about the cultivation of the bodhisattva practices.
The night goddess replied, first praising his resolve for enlightenment, and then formally imparting the Dharma-realm, saying: "O son of noble family, Bodhi..."
The Bodhisattva accomplishes ten dharmas and is thus able to fulfill the bodhisattva practices.
First, by attaining pure samādhis and so forth, he fully demonstrates the ten practices; this is the general answer to the question posed. Next, he says:
"I have attained a bodhisattva liberation named 'Tranquil Joy of Meditative Concentration and Universal Striding. This specifically indicates the name and essence of the dharma-gate he has realized.

The commentary explains: "To be in accord with principle and free from attachment is 'tranquility' (śamatha); the simultaneous cultivation of both śamatha and vipaśyanā is 'meditative concentration' (dhyāna);
dwelling in the joy of the True Dharma is 'bliss'; and vast, boundless activity is 'universal stride. These are the fundamental practices of this spiritual friend.

Although he primarily cultivates meditative concentration, according to his assignment to the second bhūmi, he should be characterized by the perfection of ethical discipline (śīla-pāramitā). The mention of 'meditative concentration' here is intended to manifest his mastery of samādhi."

Because they share the same precepts, the subsequent passage beginning with "Universally seeing all Buddhas of the three periods of time" extensively reveals their functional activity (*karmayoga*), clarifying the four kinds of dhyāna.
The first six lines of the sūtra clarify the dhyāna of "clinging to suchness" (*tathatālambana-dhyāna*) as being identical to the pure dhyāna of the Tathāgata;
this is the functional activity of tranquility (*śānti*). Next, [the text says]: "Good son, I thus understand all Tathāgatas..."

The following clarifies the dhyāna for dwelling in happiness in the present life (*dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāra*), thereby manifesting the functional activity of meditative concentration (*samādhi*). The first two lines of the sūtra cite what precedes to introduce what follows.

Next, there are four sections that clarify dwelling in happiness by way of the names of the four dhyānas. The first two lines of the sūtra state that one does not give rise to discursive thoughts through contemplation and observation;
this refers to the cultivation of the first dhyāna. Next, it states that one quiets all mental activities; this refers to the cultivation of [the second dhyāna].
The second dhyāna. Next, the line "contemplating the self-nature of all sentient beings" refers to the cultivation of the third dhyāna.
The line "the four *siddhāntas* can extinguish [afflictions]" refers to the cultivation of the fourth dhyāna. These are explained solely in terms of the fourth dhyāna to clarify abiding in bliss;
this is the cultivation according to the One Vehicle (*ekayāna*). Therefore, the subsequent text says, "universally entering the *dharmadhātu*," followed by "increasing and perfecting."
The two lines of scripture following "The vow for omniscience" clarify the meditative concentration that draws forth merit.

The phrase "sporting with supernormal powers" (ṛddhi-vidhi) carries the meaning of "universal roaming. Next, the twelve and a half lines of scripture beginning with "Good son, I have cultivated this...

clarify the meditative concentration that benefits sentient beings. It states that there are no various skillful means (*upāya*) that do not provide benefit; therefore, it says, "I cultivate understanding."

Upon emerging from this state, it causes all sentient beings not to give rise to unrighteous greed and so forth, even leading them to achieve the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*).
Next, he humbles himself, saying: "I have attained only this Bodhisattva liberation door of the 'Universal Pacing' which delights in the tranquility of meditative concentration;
as for the Bodhisattvas who are fully endowed with all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra, [they are beyond my reach]. (The text continues with the ten [vows]).

"These two kinds of vast Dharma gates are not within my knowledge. He then pointed toward a companion behind him and said, "Not far from here, on the right side of the site of enlightenment, there is a night goddess named Priyadarśanāvekṣaṇā; you should go and ask her."
At that time, the night goddess Samantāśrīviśuddhaprabhā spoke in verse; there were thirteen stanzas. The first ten stanzas eulogize the Dharma-gate of direct transmission.
The next two stanzas express self-effacement and deference to the superior. The final stanza points out the subsequent spiritual friend.
The reason for repeating the verse is to express deep reverence. At that time, the youth Sudhana gazed up at him with earnest devotion, took his leave, and departed.
Then, the youth Sudhana, honoring the instructions of the spiritual friend and acting according to the words of the spiritual friend, reflected thus:
A virtuous friend is difficult to see and difficult to encounter. Seeing a virtuous friend causes the mind to be undistracted.
Seeing a virtuous friend shatters the mountains of obstacles. Seeing a virtuous friend enter the ocean of great compassion to rescue and protect sentient beings.
Seeing a virtuous friend attain the light of wisdom that universally illumines the Dharma-realm. Seeing a virtuous friend is able to fully practice all-knowledge.
He thought: "By seeing a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), one is able to behold everywhere the ocean of Buddhas of the ten directions;

by seeing a spiritual friend, one attains the vision of all Buddhas turning the wheel of Dharma and retains it without forgetting. Having formed this thought, he resolved to go to the place of the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā.
At that time, the goddess Pramuditā empowered the youth Sudhana, causing him to know how to draw near to spiritual friends.

Knowledge can give rise to all wholesome karmas and cause them to increase and ripen. That is to say, it causes one to know that by approaching spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), one is able to cultivate the requisites for awakening;
it causes one to know that by approaching spiritual friends, one is able to give rise to a courageous mind;

it causes one to know that by approaching spiritual friends, one is able to perform indestructible deeds; and it causes one to know that by approaching spiritual friends, one is able to attain what is difficult to subdue.
Power: It causes one to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), one can enter boundless regions;

it causes one to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends, one can practice for a long duration; it causes one to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends, one can accomplish boundless deeds;
it causes one to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends, one can traverse immeasurable paths; it causes one to know that by drawing near to spiritual friends, one can attain swiftness.

His power reaches all lands, enabling one to know how to draw near to spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) without ever leaving one’s original place, yet arriving everywhere throughout the ten directions.
At that time, the youth Sudhana suddenly had this thought: "By drawing near to spiritual friends, one is able to courageously and diligently cultivate the path to omniscience;
by drawing near to spiritual friends, one is able to swiftly give birth to the great ocean of vows."
By associating with spiritual friends, one is able to undergo boundless suffering for all sentient beings throughout all future eons.
By associating with spiritual friends, one is able to don the great armor of diligence and proclaim the sound of the Dharma within a single atom so that it pervades the entire Dharma-realm.
By associating with spiritual friends, one is able to swiftly travel to the oceans of all directions. By associating with...
A spiritual friend practices the conduct of a bodhisattva throughout all future eons within the space of a single hair-pore.
By relying upon a spiritual friend, one practices the conduct of a bodhisattva in every thought-moment and ultimately dwells securely on the stage of omniscience.
By relying upon a spiritual friend, one is able to enter the paths of adornment consisting of the sovereign spiritual powers of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time. By...
"By associating with spiritual friends, one is able to constantly and universally enter the gates of all dharma-realms.

Through associating with spiritual friends, while always taking the dharma-realm as one's object and never wavering from it, one is able to travel everywhere throughout the lands of the ten directions.
At that time, having formed this thought, the youth Sudhana went to the place where the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā was, and he saw that night goddess.
Seated upon the Lotus-Treasury Lion Throne within the Tathāgata’s assembly at the site of enlightenment,
he entered the liberation of the Universal Joy Banner of Great Power. From every single pore of his body, he emanated clouds of immeasurable varieties of transformation bodies,
which, according to the needs of beings, preached the Dharma with wondrous voices, universally gathering in all infinite multitudes.

They cause all beings to rejoice and obtain benefit. That is to say, they emit clouds of immeasurable transformation bodies that fill all worlds throughout the ten directions, preaching the bodhisattva practice of the perfection of giving (*dāna-pāramitā*).
They are entirely without attachment to any thing; they bestow gifts universally upon all sentient beings with a mind of equanimity, free from contempt or arrogance. Internally...

Externally, they practice the giving of all things that are difficult to relinquish; they manifest clouds of transformation bodies equal in number to all sentient beings, filling the Dharma-realm and appearing before all beings everywhere.

They proclaim the upholding of pure precepts without any transgression, the complete fulfillment of all ascetic practices, non-reliance upon any worldly things, and freedom from attachment to any sensory objects.
He spoke of wandering back and forth within the cycle of birth and death; he spoke of the prosperity and decline, the suffering and joy, of all humans and devas;
he spoke of how all objective realms are impure; he spoke of how all phenomena are impermanent; and he spoke of how all conditioned activities are suffering and devoid of essence.
He caused all those in the world to abandon their inverted views, to dwell in the realm of the Buddhas, and to uphold the precepts of the Tathāgata. Thus he expounded.
They proclaim various forms of ethical conduct, and the fragrance of their precepts pervades everywhere, causing all sentient beings to reach full maturity. Furthermore,
they manifest clouds of various bodies as numerous as all living beings, teaching the ability to endure all manner of suffering— namely, being cut, beaten, reviled, and humiliated—
with minds that remain serene, unmoved, and undisturbed, neither disparaging nor [exalting] any form of practice.
He is exalted; he does not give rise to pride toward any sentient beings. He dwells in patient acceptance regarding the nature of all phenomena.
He speaks of the bodhicitta as being inexhaustible; because the mind is inexhaustible, wisdom is also inexhaustible. He universally severs the afflictions of all sentient beings.
He describes the lowly, ugly, and incomplete bodies of sentient beings to inspire in them a sense of weary detachment, while praising all the Tathāgatas.
They manifest a body of supreme, pure, and wondrous form to inspire joy and delight. Through such skillful means, they bring sentient beings to maturity.

Furthermore, they emit clouds of various bodies equal in number to the realm of sentient beings, and according to the inclinations of the minds of those beings, they proclaim the methods for cultivating all-knowledge that aid the path through courageous diligence, and they subdue demonic adversaries through courageous diligence.
With courageous diligence, they give rise to the bodhicitta, remaining unshakable and non-retrogressive;
with courageous diligence, they deliver all sentient beings across the ocean of birth and death; with courageous diligence, they eliminate all hardships and calamities of the evil realms;
with courageous diligence, they shatter the mountain of ignorance; and with courageous diligence, they make offerings to all Buddhas and Tathāgatas without ever becoming weary.
With weariness [toward worldly things], they courageously and vigorously uphold the Dharma-wheels of all Buddhas;
with courageous and vigorous effort, they shatter and disperse all mountains of obstacles; with courageous and vigorous effort, they teach and bring all sentient beings to maturity;
with courageous and vigorous effort, they adorn and purify all Buddha-lands. By such skillful means, they bring sentient beings to maturity, and furthermore, they produce various...
They manifest clouds of immeasurable bodies. Through various skillful means, they cause the minds of all sentient beings to give rise to joy, abandon evil intentions, and feel weary of all desires.
They preach shame and remorse, causing sentient beings to guard their sense faculties.
They preach the unsurpassed, pure Brahma-conduct. They preach that the desire realm is the domain of Māra, causing them to feel dread. They manifest...

They take no pleasure in worldly desires, but abide in the joy of the Dharma. Following their respective stages, they enter the bliss of the various dhyānas and samādhis, causing them to contemplate and investigate so as to eliminate all afflictions.
Furthermore, they expound upon the ocean of all bodhisattva samādhis, their spiritual powers, transformations, and sovereign play, causing all sentient beings to rejoice.
Filled with joy and delight, they are free from all sorrow and fear; their minds are pure and their faculties are sharp and keen. Cherishing and honoring the Dharma, they cultivate and increase it.

Furthermore, they manifest various clouds of bodies equal in number to the realms of sentient beings, in order to teach them how to travel to the lands of the ten directions to make offerings to the Buddhas, as well as to teachers and true spiritual friends, and to receive and uphold all the teachings of the Buddhas.
They apply themselves with tireless diligence. Furthermore, they expound and praise the ocean of all Tathāgatas; they observe the ocean of all dharma-gates;
they reveal the essential natures and characteristics of all dharmas; they open up all doors of samādhi; they expand the realm of wisdom;
they exhaust the ocean of doubts of all sentient beings; and they manifest the vajra of wisdom to shatter [all obstacles].
All sentient beings behold the mountain as the sun-disk of wisdom rises, shattering the darkness of ignorance of all beings and causing them all to rejoice and attain omniscience.
Furthermore, there emerge various clouds of bodies equal in number to the realms of sentient beings, which go before all beings everywhere;
according to what is appropriate for each, they preach the Dharma using various modes of speech, sometimes speaking of the mundane world.

By the power of their supernormal faculties and merit, they may say that the three realms are all terrifying, causing beings to cease performing worldly karmic actions and to depart from the three realms to emerge from the thicket of afflictions.
Or, for the sake of praising the path of omniscience, they cause them to transcend the stages of the two vehicles.
Or, for the sake of expounding non-abiding in saṃsāra and non-abiding in nirvāṇa, they cause them to be free from attachment.

Whether concerning the conditioned or the unconditioned, he may preach while dwelling in celestial palaces or even at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), causing them to rejoice and resolve to attain bodhicitta.
Through such skillful means, he teaches and transforms sentient beings, leading them all to ultimately attain omniscience (sarvajñatā).
Furthermore, they emit clouds of bodies as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, universally approaching the presence of all sentient beings.
In every thought-moment, they manifest all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; in every thought-moment, they manifest pure great vows that fill the Dharma-realm;
in every thought-moment, they manifest the adornment and purification of all oceans of worlds; and in every thought-moment, they manifest offerings.
The ocean of all Tathāgatas, in every thought-moment, manifests entry into the ocean of all dharma-gates; in every thought-moment, manifests entry into the ocean of all world-systems;
in every thought-moment, within world-systems as numerous as atoms, manifests the pure cultivation of the path to omniscience throughout all kalpas until the end of the future across all lands;
in every thought-moment, manifests entry into the powers of the Tathāgata. In every thought-moment...
Within every thought-moment, he demonstrates the ocean of skillful means for entering all three periods of time.

Within every thought-moment, he travels to and dwells in all lands, manifesting various supernatural powers and transformations. Within every thought-moment, he reveals to all bodhisattvas their various practices and vows, causing all sentient beings to abide in omniscience.
Such deeds are performed constantly without rest. Furthermore, he manifests forms equal in number to all sentient beings.

They give rise to clouds of mental-derivative bodies that go everywhere before all sentient beings, proclaiming the boundless power of the bodhisattvas’ methods for gathering the aids to the path toward omniscience;
the indestructible power of seeking omniscience; the inexhaustible power;
the non-retrogressive power of cultivating supreme practices; the uninterrupted power; and the power of being unstained by the phenomena of birth and death.
The power that can shatter all the forces of the hosts of Māras; the power that remains far removed from all the defilements of affliction;
the power that can shatter the mountains of all karmic obstructions; the power that dwells through all kalpas practicing the conduct of great compassion without weariness;
the power that causes all Buddha-fields to tremble and brings joy to birth to all sentient beings; the power that can shatter all external [non-Buddhist]...

The power of the Way; the power to universally turn the wheel of Dharma throughout the world. By means of such skillful expedients, they bring sentient beings to maturity, leading them to all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*).

Furthermore, they manifest clouds of transformational form-bodies (*rūpakāya*) as infinite as the mental calculations of all sentient beings, traveling everywhere to immeasurable worlds in the ten directions. According to the inclinations of sentient beings, they expound upon all the bodhisattva practices.

The practice of wisdom. That is to say: it is the teaching on the wisdom that enters the ocean of all sentient beings' realms; the teaching on the wisdom that enters the ocean of all sentient beings' minds;
the teaching on the wisdom that enters the ocean of all sentient beings' faculties; and the teaching on the wisdom that enters the ocean of all sentient beings' conducts.
It speaks of the wisdom that delivers all sentient beings without ever missing the proper time; it speaks of the wisdom of the sounds of all dharma-realms;
it speaks of the wisdom that pervades the ocean of all dharma-realms in every thought-moment; it speaks of the wisdom that knows the destruction of all oceans of worlds in every thought-moment;
it speaks of the wisdom that knows the differences in the formation, abiding, and adornment of all oceans of worlds in every thought-moment; it speaks of every thought-moment...

The wisdom of freely approaching, making offerings to, and hearing the Wheel of Dharma from all Tathāgatas manifests such a perfection of wisdom (*jñāna-pāramitā*), causing all sentient beings to experience great joy, serenity, and delight;

their minds become pure, they give rise to resolute understanding, and they seek omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) without ever turning back. Thus are the various perfections (*pāramitā*) of the bodhisattvas accomplished as described.
Maturing sentient beings, he thus proclaims all the various practices of the bodhisattvas for their benefit.
Furthermore, from each and every pore, he emits immeasurable clouds of bodies of sentient beings;
that is to say, he brings forth clouds of bodies resembling those of the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, the Sudarśana Heaven, the Sudṛśa Heaven, the Atapa Heaven, and the Avṛha Heaven. He emits...
Clouds of bodies resembling those of the Śuddhāvāsa, Vṛhatphala, Puṇyaprasava, and Anabhraka heavens emerge;
clouds of bodies resembling those of the Śubhakṛtsna, Apramāṇaśubha, and Parīttaśubha heavens emerge; clouds of bodies resembling those of the Ābhāsvara, Apramāṇābha, and Parīttābha heavens emerge;

clouds of bodies resembling those of the Mahābrahmā, Brahmāpurohita, and Brahmakāyika heavens emerge; and [clouds resembling those of] the Paranirmita-vaśavartin, Nirmāṇarati, and Tuṣita heavens emerge.
Clouds of bodies resembling those of the gods of the Yāma, Tuṣita, and Trāyastriṃśa heavens, along with their celestial maidens and hosts of devaputras;
clouds of bodies resembling those of the Gandharva King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, his Gandharva sons, and his Gandharva daughters;
[clouds of bodies] resembling those of the Kumbhāṇḍa King Virūḍhaka, his Kumbhāṇḍa sons, and his Kumbhāṇḍa daughters...
There emerged clouds of bodies resembling those of the Naga King Virūpākṣa, as well as his sons and daughters;
clouds of bodies resembling those of the Yakṣa King Vaiśravaṇa, as well as his sons and daughters;
and [clouds of bodies resembling] the Kiṃnara King Mahādruma, the Mahoraga King Kalyāṇabuddhi, the Garuḍa King Mahājava, and Rāhu.
From the asura kings, the Dharma King Yama, and their sons and daughters, clouds of similar bodies issued forth;
from the human kings and their sons and daughters, clouds of similar bodies issued forth; from the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the assemblies of Buddhas, clouds of similar bodies issued forth;
and from the earth spirits, water spirits, fire spirits, wind spirits, river spirits, ocean spirits, mountain spirits, and tree spirits, [clouds of similar bodies issued forth].
Clouds of similar bodies belonging to the deities presiding over the directions of day and night pervade the ten directions and fill the entire Dharma-realm.

Before all those sentient beings, they manifest various sounds, namely: the sound of wind-circles, the sound of water-circles, the sound of flames, the sound of ocean tides, the sound of earthquakes, the sound of great mountains colliding, the sound of celestial cities trembling, and the sound of *maṇi* jewels.
The sound of clashing [instruments]; the voice of the Heavenly Kings; the voice of the Dragon Kings; the voice of the Yakṣa Kings; the voice of the Gandharva Kings;
the voice of the Asura Kings; the voice of the Garuḍa Kings; the voice of the Kiṃnara Kings; the voice of the Mahoraga Kings;
the voice of the Kings of Men; the voice of the Brahmā Kings; the sound of the singing of celestial maidens; the sound of the music of all the devas; and the sound of the sovereign maṇi jewels.
With such various sounds as these, she spoke of the merits accumulated by the night goddess Priyadarśanā-sattvāvalokanī from the time of her first resolve:
namely, serving all spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), drawing near to all Buddhas to practice wholesome dharmas,

practicing the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) by being able to relinquish what is difficult to give, and practicing the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*) by renouncing kingship.
While residing in his palace with his retinue, he left the household life to study the Way.

He practiced the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*), being able to endure all worldly sufferings as well as the ascetic practices cultivated by bodhisattvas. The Right Dharma he upheld was entirely firm and his mind remained unshakable.
Furthermore, he was able to endure all the evil deeds and malicious speech directed at his own body and mind by sentient beings. Thus he practiced patience.
All karma is never lost or destroyed. One endures all phenomena and gives rise to the definitive understanding; one endures the nature of all dharmas and contemplates them with truth.
One practices the perfection of vigor, initiates the conduct of omniscience, and accomplishes all Buddha-dharmas.
One practices the perfection of dhyāna, including all its requisites, all its cultivation, and all its accomplishment.
He fully manifests all purities, all arisings of samādhi and supernormal powers, and all entrances into the ocean-gates of samādhi.
He practices the *prajñāpāramitā*, and he fully displays all the requisites for that *prajñāpāramitā*:
its purities, the great sun of wisdom, the great cloud of wisdom, the great treasury of wisdom, and the great gateways of wisdom.
He fully reveals [them]. He practices the perfection of skillful means (*upāya-pāramitā*).
He fully reveals all the requisites, all the practices, all the essential natures, all the principles, all the purifications, and all the associated matters of that perfection of skillful means.
He practices the perfection of vows (*praṇidhāna-pāramitā*). [He reveals] all the essential natures of that perfection of vows...
He fully reveals all accomplishments, all practices, and all associated matters.
He fully reveals the perfection of power (*bala-pāramitā*), including all its requisites, all its causal conditions, all its principles, all its expositions, and all its associated matters.
He fully reveals the perfection of wisdom (*jñāna-pāramitā*). As for that perfection of wisdom...
All requisite articles; all essential natures; all accomplishments; all purities; all locations;
all increases; all profound entries; all radiances; all manifestations; and all principles.
All associated matters; all forms of discernment; all modes of activity; all associated dharmas; all encompassed dharmas; all dharmas to be known;
all karma to be known; all realms to be known; all kalpas to be known; all worlds to be known; all appearances of Buddhas to be known;
all Buddhas to be known; all Bodhisattvas to be known; all Bodhisattva minds to be known; the stages of a Bodhisattva; and the Bodhisattva [himself].

The requisites for practice, the bodhisattva’s setting forth, the bodhisattva’s dedication, the bodhisattva’s great vows, the bodhisattva’s wheel of Dharma, the bodhisattva’s discernment of phenomena,
the bodhisattva’s ocean of Dharma, the bodhisattva’s ocean of Dharma-gates, the bodhisattva’s whirlpool of Dharma, and the bodhisattva’s principles of Dharma—
all such realms corresponding to the perfection of wisdom are fully revealed, thereby maturing sentient beings.
Furthermore, it describes the continuous succession of merits accumulated from the first generation of the mind of enlightenment; the continuous succession of the roots of goodness practiced;
the continuous succession of the immeasurable *pāramitās* cultivated; the continuous succession of dying here and being born there, as well as their respective names;
and the successive acts of drawing near to spiritual friends, serving the Buddhas, and upholding the True Dharma.

The Dharma. Practicing the bodhisattva path, they enter various samādhis. By the power of these samādhis, they universally behold all Buddhas, universally behold all lands, and universally know all kalpas.
They penetrate deeply into the dharma-realm to observe sentient beings; entering the ocean of the dharma-realm, they know where all beings die here and are born there.
Having attained the pure divine ear, they hear all sounds; having attained the pure divine eye, they see all things.
Regarding form: they attain the knowledge of others' minds and know the thoughts of sentient beings; they attain the knowledge of past lives and know the events of the prior limit;
they attain the supernormal power of the bases of psychic mastery that is independent and effortless, traveling freely throughout the lands of the ten directions.

Such is the sequential continuity of all these attainments: they obtain the liberation of a bodhisattva, enter the ocean of bodhisattva liberation, and obtain the sovereignty of a bodhisattva. They obtain...
Sā-vīrya (Valiant Courage) attains the stride of a bodhisattva, abides in the perception of a bodhisattva, and enters the path of a bodhisattva.
Thus, he fully expounds, analyzes, and demonstrates the continuous succession of all such meritorious qualities, thereby bringing sentient beings to maturity.
When this was spoken, in every moment of thought, he purified unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-lands in each of the ten directions;
he liberated immeasurable sentient beings from the evil realms; he caused immeasurable sentient beings to be born among gods and humans in states of wealth, nobility, and sovereignty;
he caused immeasurable sentient beings to emerge from the ocean of birth and death; and he caused immeasurable sentient beings to dwell in peace.
[He established] Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas on the stage of the Tathāgata, causing immeasurable sentient beings to dwell in the stage of the Tathāgata.

At that time, the youth Sudhana saw and heard all these aforementioned rare and wondrous events; from moment to moment he observed, contemplated, understood, and deeply entered into them, dwelling therein securely.
By virtue of the Buddha’s majestic power and the power of his own liberation, he attained the inconceivable [wisdom] of a Bodhisattva.
The liberation of Sovereign Power of the Universal Banner of Great Might and Joy. Why is this? Because she practiced together with the night goddess Priyadarśanā in the past;
because she is sustained by the spiritual power of the Tathāgata; because she is aided by inconceivable roots of goodness;
because she has attained the faculties of a bodhisattva; because she is born into the lineage of the Tathāgatas; and because she has obtained the power of virtuous friends.
Because he was embraced [by the Buddhas]; because he received the protective mindfulness of all Tathāgatas; because he had previously been transformed by Vairocana Tathāgata;
because his roots of goodness in that portion were already matured; and because he was capable of practicing the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
At that time, having attained this liberation, the youth Sudhana felt great joy in his heart; with palms joined, he turned toward the one named Joyful-Eye-Contemplating.
The Night Spirit Sattva praised him with these verses:
Throughout immeasurable and innumerable eons, You have studied the Buddha’s most profound Dharma. According to those who should be transformed, you manifest wondrous physical bodies;
You thoroughly understand all sentient beings, Who are mired in delusion and bound by false conceptions.
Various bodies are all manifested, taming beings according to their needs. The Dharma-body is eternally quiescent, pure, and without dualistic characteristics;
yet for the sake of transforming sentient beings, it manifests various forms.
Regarding the aggregates, elements, and sense bases, there has never been any attachment; thus it displays both conduct and the physical body.
Taming all sentient beings, Unattached to internal or external phenomena, Having crossed the ocean of birth and death,
yet manifesting in various forms, Abiding within the realms of existence, Unshakable by all conceptual proliferation and discrimination,
For those attached to deluded thoughts, He widely proclaims the Dharma of the Ten Powers.
Abiding single-mindedly in samādhi, unmoving for immeasurable eons, they emit clouds of emanations from their pores to make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Having attained the power of the Buddha’s skillful means, they manifest various bodies in every thought-moment without limit,
universally gathering all sentient beings and thoroughly understanding the ocean of all realms of existence.
Adorned with various karmas, he expounds the unimpeded Dharma, causing all to become completely purified.
His physical body is wondrous beyond compare, pure like Samantabhadra; according to the minds of sentient beings, he manifests the signs of the world.
At that time, having spoken these verses, the youth Sudhana said:
"O Celestial Deity, how long has it been since you first resolved your mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and how long has it been since you attained this liberation?
Then, the night goddess Rātridevatā Viśvālokana, observing all beings, replied in verse:
I recall a past life, more than as many eons ago as there are atoms in a buddha-field; that field was named Maṇiprabhā and the eon was named Śāntanirghoṣa.
There were a million nayutas of koṭis of four-continent worlds, and the number of their kings was likewise.
Each ruled over his own domain, and among them was one royal capital.
Named the Jewel Fragrant Banner, its adornments are most exquisite; all who see it are filled with joy.
Within it dwells a wheel-turning king, his body exceedingly subtle and wondrous, adorned with the thirty-two marks and the secondary characteristics.
He is born by transformation within a lotus, his body radiant with golden light.
Rising into the air, he illuminated near and far, spreading his light throughout the realm of Jambudvīpa.
That king had a thousand sons, brave and of handsome form; his ministers numbered one hundred million.
His consorts were ten billion in number, their countenances like those of celestial maidens, possessing beneficial and gentle minds.
With a heart of loving-kindness, he served the king; that king transformed the world through the Dharma.
Throughout the four continents and within the great earth bounded by the Cakravāḍa mountains, all became abundant and prosperous.
At that time, I was a precious woman endowed with the voice of Brahmā; my body emitted golden light that illuminated a thousand yojanas.
The sun having already set, all music fell silent; the Great King and his attendants all lay down in peaceful sleep.
At that time, the Buddha Sāgaradatta appeared in the world, manifesting supernatural powers that filled the realms of the ten directions and emitted a vast ocean of great radiance.
Bodies of various sovereign powers, as numerous as the atoms of all lands, pervade the ten directions.
As the earth quakes, a wondrous sound issues forth, universally proclaiming that a Buddha has appeared in the world. The hosts of devas, humans, nāgas, and spirits are all filled with joy.
From within each and every pore, oceans of the Buddha’s transformation bodies emerge.
Pervading all ten directions, he taught the wondrous Dharma according to the needs of beings.
At that time, within my dream, I beheld the Buddha’s various miraculous transformations and also heard the profound and wondrous Dharma; my heart was filled with great joy.
Ten thousand night goddesses together dwelt in the air, praising the appearance of the Buddha in the world.
Simultaneously awakening me, O wise one, you should arise!
A Buddha has appeared in your land, difficult to encounter even in an ocean of kalpas; those who see him attain purity.
At that time, I awoke from sleep and beheld a pure light; observing whence it came, I saw [the Buddha] beneath the King of Trees.
The body adorned with all marks, like the king of jewel mountains, From every pore emits a great ocean of light;
Having seen this, my heart rejoiced, And I immediately gave rise to this thought:
"May I attain such great supernormal powers as the Buddha's. At that moment, I attained awakening.
The Great King and his retinue were caused to behold the Buddha’s radiance, and they all rejoiced.

At that time, together with the Great King and his thousands of millions of mounted attendants, as well as immeasurable sentient beings, I proceeded together to the Buddha’s abode. For twenty thousand years, I made offerings to that Tathāgata.
The seven treasures and the four continents— I offer them all as gifts.
At that time, that Tathāgata preached the *Sūtra of the Universal Cloud of Merit*, Universally responding to the minds of all sentient beings.

I have attained the pure eye, the samādhi of quiescence, and the dhāraṇī; In every thought-moment, I am able to see the ocean of all Buddhas.

Having accomplished the powers of the Tathāgata, I behold the delusions of sentient beings.

they engage in the forest-like thickets of afflictions, views, and activities,

May I become like all the Honored Ones of Ten Powers throughout the ten directions;
taking the Buddhas and sentient beings as my object, I shall raise a great cloud of vows and from this point cultivate merit.
Entering the path of skillful means, may the clouds of aspiration completely pervade all;
universally entering all Buddha-arrays and fulfilling the pāramitās, filling the entire dharma-realm;

From that time until now, throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, I have never fallen into the evil realms but have always been born among humans and devas.
In every place, I have constantly beheld all the Buddhas, even up to the presence of the Buddha *Sudīpa-guṇa-ketu*.
I have attained this bodhisattva liberation of the Banner of Universal Joy with Great Power. By means of this liberation, I thus benefit all sentient beings.
