Entering the Dharma Realm, Chapter Thirty-nine, Part Eleven. At that time, the youth Sudhana,
having heard from the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā the liberation door of the Banner of Universal Joy,
believed, understood, entered into, comprehended, accorded with, contemplated, and practiced it, while remaining mindful of his spiritual friend.
There are instructions to be followed, which the mind never abandons for even a moment. With the sense faculties undistracted, one single-mindedly aspires to meet spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
One diligently seeks them throughout the ten directions without weariness, vowing to always remain in their presence to give rise to all merits.

Sharing the same roots of goodness as the spiritual friends, one attains the skillful means and practices of the spiritual friends. Relying upon the spiritual friends, one enters the ocean of diligence. In...
"May I never be separated from this for immeasurable kalpas. Having made this vow, he went to where the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā was.
At that time, the night goddess manifested for the youth Sudhana the supernatural power of a bodhisattva’s liberation for taming sentient beings.
Her body was adorned with all the marks and signs of excellence, and from between her two eyebrows she emitted a great light named...
The Banner of Universal Illumination and Purity of the Lamp of Wisdom has immeasurable radiance as its retinue.
This light shines universally upon all worlds. Having illuminated the worlds, it enters the crown of Sudhana’s head and fills his body.
At that moment, Sudhana immediately attains the Samādhi of the Ultimate Pure Wheel. Having attained this samādhi, he sees both goddesses within the space between them.
In every instant, within each and every atom of all the dust of the earth, the dust of water, and the dust of fire;

within each atom of the various jewels such as diamond-maṇi gems; and within each atom of all ornaments such as flowers, incense, and necklaces—one perceives the formation and destruction of worlds as numerous as the atoms of a Buddha-field, as well as all the elements of earth, water, fire, and wind.
He also saw all the great accumulations and the continuous succession of all worlds, all of which abide supported by the earth-element. He saw various mountains and seas,
various rivers and ponds, various forests, and various palaces— namely, the palaces of devas, the palaces of nāgas,
the palaces of yakṣas, and even the palaces of mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.

He saw entirely all dwellings—houses, hells, the animal realm, and the domain of King Yama—as well as the revolving through the various destinies, the coming and going of birth and death, and the receiving of retribution according to karma, each distinct and different. Furthermore, he saw the distinctions of all worlds;
that is to say, some worlds were defiled and impure, while some worlds were pure, and some worlds...
There are worlds tending toward impurity; there are worlds tending toward purity; there are worlds that are both impure and pure;
there are worlds that are pure and impure; and there are worlds that are entirely pure. There are worlds whose form is level and upright;
there are those that dwell inverted; and there are those that dwell sideways. Such are all worlds and all destinies.

In the midst [of this], he saw entirely this Night Goddess Who Universally Saves All Beings, at all times and in all places, according to the differences in the physical forms, speech, conduct, and understanding of sentient beings, manifesting before them through the power of skillful means to transform and deliver them as appropriate.
She causes the sentient beings in the hells to escape all bitter poisons; she causes the sentient beings among animals not to devour one another; she causes...
May the sentient beings of the hungry ghost realm be free from hunger and thirst. May the nāgas and others be freed from all fears.

May the sentient beings of the desire realm be freed from the sufferings of the desire realm. May the sentient beings of the human realm be freed from the fear of dark nights, the fear of being reviled, and the fear of ill repute.
The fear of the great masses; the fear of being unable to subsist; the fear of death; the fear of the evil realms; the fear of severing the roots of goodness;

the fear of regressing from the bodhicitta; the fear of encountering evil associates; the fear of being separated from virtuous friends; the fear of falling into the stages of the two vehicles; and the various fears of birth and death.
The fear of dwelling together with beings of different kinds; the fear of taking birth during an evil age; the fear of taking birth among an evil lineage; the fear of committing evil karma;
the fear of the obstructions of karma and afflictions; and the fear of being bound by attachment to various perceptions—he causes them to abandon all such fears.
Furthermore, he sees all sentient beings—those born from eggs, those born from wombs, those born from moisture, and those born by transformation; those with form and those without...

Whether in the realm of form, the realm of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, or the state that is neither with nor without perception, [the Buddhas] appear before them everywhere to constantly and diligently provide protection and rescue.

This is for the sake of fulfilling the power of the Bodhisattvas' great vows; for the sake of penetrating deeply into the power of the Bodhisattvas' samādhis; for the sake of strengthening the power of the Bodhisattvas' supernormal knowledges;
for the sake of giving birth to the power of Samantabhadra’s practices and vows; and for the sake of expanding the ocean of the Bodhisattvas' great compassion.

Because they have attained the great compassion that universally covers all sentient beings without obstruction; because they have attained the universal bestowing of immeasurable joy and bliss upon sentient beings;

because they have attained the wisdom and skillful means that universally gather in all sentient beings; because they have attained the vast liberation, mastery, and supernormal powers of a bodhisattva;
because they have purified all Buddha-fields; because they have awakened to the understanding of all phenomena; and because they make offerings.
Because they are all Buddhas; because they uphold all the Buddha-teachings; because they accumulate all roots of goodness and cultivate all sublime practices;
because they enter the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings without obstruction;
because they know the faculties of all sentient beings and teach and mature them; and because they purify the faith and understanding of all sentient beings and remove their evil obstructions.
Because she destroys the dark ignorance of all sentient beings and causes them to attain the pure radiance of omniscience,
when the youth Sudhana beheld this night goddess’s inconceivable and profound realm of such supernatural power—
the Bodhisattva liberation that universally manifests to discipline all sentient beings— he was filled with immeasurable joy. He bowed his head...

He paid homage and gazed up at her with a single-minded heart. Then that night goddess cast off her form adorned with the ornaments of a bodhisattva and returned to her original appearance, yet she did not relinquish her sovereign spiritual power. At that time, the youth Sudhana joined his palms in respectful salutation.
He stood to one side and praised him with these verses:
"I, Sudhana, have beheld such great supernormal power; My heart is filled with joy as I speak these verses of praise.
I behold your venerable and wondrous body, Adorned with all the marks of excellence."
Just as the stars in the sky are all adorned and pure, They emit supreme light in quantities as numerous as the atoms of immeasurable lands, In various subtle and wondrous colors.
Shining universally throughout the ten directions, from every single pore, They emit rays of light equal in number to the minds of sentient beings; At the tip of each and every ray of light...
From all [the Buddhas] emerge precious lotus flowers; from within these flowers emerge transformation bodies. They are able to extinguish the suffering of sentient beings.
From their light issues forth wondrous sound, universally perfuming all sentient beings. Furthermore, they rain down various kinds of flowers as an offering to all Buddhas.
Between their two eyebrows they emit wondrous light, the magnitude of which is equal to Mount Sumeru.
Universally touching all sentient beings, he causes the darkness of ignorance to be extinguished.
From his mouth he emits pure light, like immeasurable suns, universally illuminating the vast realm of Vairocana.
From his eyes he emits pure light, like immeasurable moons, universally illuminating the lands of the ten directions.
Completely extinguishing the cataracts of worldly delusion, you manifest various emanated bodies;
with forms equal in number to all sentient beings, they fill the realms of the ten directions. You deliver beings from the ocean of the three realms of existence.
Your wondrous body pervades the ten directions, appearing before all living beings to eliminate all fears, such as those of water, fire, thieves, and kings.
Receiving the instruction of the Joyful-Eyed One, I was led to the presence of the Honored One.
I beheld the mark between the Honored One’s eyebrows emitting a vast, pure light that universally illumines the oceans of the ten directions.
It completely extinguishes all darkness and manifests supernatural powers as it enters my body; I have encountered this perfect radiance.
My heart gave rise to great joy, as I attained the samādhi of dhāraṇī. I saw the Buddhas of the ten directions everywhere;
in every place I passed through, I beheld all the subtle atoms.
Within each and every atom, I saw lands as numerous as those very atoms—some were infinite lands, all of them turbid and defiled.
Sentient beings undergo various sufferings, constantly lamenting and wailing in grief. In some realms, whether defiled or pure, there is little joy and much sorrow and suffering;
there he manifests the forms of the Three Vehicles and goes to those places to rescue and deliver them.
In other realms, whether pure or defiled, which sentient beings delight in beholding, Bodhisattvas always fill them completely.
Abiding in the teachings of all Buddhas, within each and every atom, are infinite oceans of pure lands.
These were purified by Vairocana Buddha throughout past eons.
In all these lands, the Buddha sits beneath the Bodhi tree, attains enlightenment, turns the wheel of Dharma, and delivers all sentient beings.
"I see the Goddess Universal Savior throughout those immeasurable lands, going to all the abodes of the Buddhas to make offerings everywhere.
When the youth Sudhana had spoken these verses, he addressed the Night Goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā.
"Devaputra, this liberation is profound and rare; what is its name? How long has it been since one attained this liberation?
What kind of practice must be cultivated to attain its purity?"
The fourth is the Night Goddess Samantasattvatrāṇojaḥśrī, who is associated with the stage of Arciṣmatī.
This means she dwells in the most excellent factors of enlightenment (*bodhipakṣadharma*), burning the fuel of afflictions as the flames of wisdom increase.

At the abode of the Night Goddess Priyadarśanāsatvāvalokanī, Sudhana heard the liberation door called "Universal Joy Banner" (*Samantaprītidhvaja-vimokṣamukha*); he believed, understood, and entered it, proceeding according to her instructions.
Seeking with single-minded devotion to behold the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), he sought diligently and without slackening, vowing to remain constantly in their presence.
He went to the place where the Night Goddess of Wondrous Virtue Who Universally Saves All Beings resided;

before he had even begun to inquire, that Night Goddess silently revealed to Sudhana the dharma-realm she had realized herself, manifesting the bodhisattva’s power of liberation for taming and transforming sentient beings.
From between his two eyebrows, he emitted a great light named "The Banner of Universal Illumination and Purity of the Lamp of Wisdom.
With immeasurable rays of light as its retinue, it universally illuminated the world and then entered the crown of Sudhana’s head, filling his entire body.
By means of this single ray of light, the entirety of the Dharma-realm was suddenly revealed to Sudhana, and he was empowered by it; therefore, Sudhana—
Vasudatta attained the Samādhi of the Ultimate Purification Wheel and entered the Dharma-realm instantaneously.

Having attained this samādhi, he beheld all the atoms existing between the two deities; within each and every atom, he saw world-systems as numerous as the atoms of a Buddha-field undergoing destruction, formation, and abiding, as well as the palaces of the six realms of existence and the sentient beings born therein.
Regarding the various distinctions in the cycles of death and rebirth, as well as the establishment of the defilement and purity of the worlds—
in every realm and every destiny, one sees the Night Goddess Universal Savior appearing in diverse forms to transform and deliver sentient beings according to their needs,
causing the nine classes of beings, including those in the hells, to all be freed from suffering; and one beholds the reason for the Night Goddess’s manifestation.

The intention behind this transformation is as follows: there are thirty-two and a half lines of scripture stating that within the light, one perceives the objects of the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*).
Having witnessed such inconceivable and profound states of supernatural power by the night goddess, Sudhana was filled with immeasurable joy;
he prostrated himself with his head at her feet and gazed up at her with single-minded devotion. At that moment, the night goddess...
She relinquished her radiant form and returned to her original appearance. At that time, Sudhana spoke twenty and a half verses in praise.
The first verse was general; the remainder praised the boundless utility of the light, as well as matters such as the merits attained and the benefits received.
When Sudhana had finished speaking these stanzas, he asked the night goddess: "This liberation is extremely profound. What is its name?"
"What is it? asks for its name. "How long has it been since you attained this liberation? asks regarding the duration of attaining that dharma.
"By practicing what conduct have you attained purity? asks regarding the cultivation of the cause. Having posed these three questions, the Night Goddess answers below.
The Night Goddess said, "Noble son, this place is difficult to know; it cannot be fathomed by gods, humans, or any of those of the two vehicles. Why is this?
Because this is the sphere of activity of those who dwell in the practice of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; because it is the sphere of activity of those who dwell in the treasury of great compassion;
because it is the sphere of activity of those who rescue and protect all sentient beings; and because it is able to purify all three..."
It is the sphere of those who avoid the eight difficult conditions; it is the sphere of those who can ensure that the lineage of the Buddhas is perpetuated and never severed within all Buddha-fields;
it is the sphere of those who can uphold and maintain all Buddha-dharmas;

it is the sphere of those who can cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva throughout all kalpas to fulfill the ocean of great vows; it is the sphere of those who [can act] within the ocean of all dharma-realms...
Because it is the realm where the darkness of ignorance is extinguished by the light of pure wisdom;

because it is the realm where the ocean of skillful means of all three periods of time is universally illuminated by the radiance of a single thought-moment of wisdom—I now speak for you, upholding the power of the Buddha.
Good son, in the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, at that time there was...
The eon was named Perfectly Pure, and the world-system was named Vairocana of Great Majestic Virtue.
Within it, as many Tathāgatas appeared as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru. That Buddha-world had as its substance all kinds of fragrant king-maṇi jewels;
it was adorned with various treasures and rested upon an ocean of stainless radiant maṇi kings. Its shape was perfectly square.
Pure and impure realms merge together; clouds of canopies formed by all manner of ornaments cover them from above.

Mountains of *maṇi* wheels of every adornment encircle them in a thousandfold circuit. There are hundreds of thousands of billions of *nayutas* of four-continent worlds (*cāturdvīpaka*), all exquisitely adorned.
Some of these four-continent worlds are inhabited by sentient beings of evil karma, while others contain a mixture of both.
Sentient beings of karma dwell therein; some sentient beings with roots of goodness from the four continents dwell therein;
and some great bodhisattvas who are entirely pure throughout the four continents dwell therein.

On the eastern edge of this world-system, by the side of the Cakravāḍa mountain range, there is a set of four continents named Ratnapradīpapuṣpadhvaja. Its national boundaries are pure, and its food and drink are [exquisite].

Abundant and prosperous, rice and grain grow there without the need for plowing or weeding. The palaces and towers are all wondrous and marvelous. Rows of various wish-fulfilling trees stand everywhere;
various incense trees constantly emit clouds of fragrance; various garland trees constantly produce clouds of garlands;
various flower trees perpetually rain down exquisite blossoms; and various jewel trees produce all manner of rare treasures. Immeasurable...
Rays of light from their forms radiated and shone all around. From the various musical trees, all kinds of music emerged; as they swayed in the wind, they produced exquisite sounds.
The brilliance of the sun and moon and the sovereign maṇi-jewels illuminated everything universally. Day and night they experienced pleasure without interruption.
Within these four continents, there were hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of royal kingdoms. In each and every kingdom...
The land is surrounded on all sides by a thousand great rivers, each covered with exquisite flowers.
As they flow and ripple, they produce the sounds of celestial music. Rows of jewel-trees are planted along their banks, adorned with various rare and wonderful treasures.
Boats come and go, providing entertainment for the heart’s desire. Between each of these rivers are hundreds of billions of cities. Each...
The city contained hundreds of billions of nayutas of villages. All such cities and villages were each surrounded by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of palaces and gardens.
Within Jambudvīpa of these four continents, there was a land named Ratnapuṣpadīpa, which was peaceful, prosperous, and teeming with people.

Within that realm, sentient beings fully practiced the ten virtuous actions. A wheel-turning monarch appeared therein, named Vairocana-Maṇiratna-padma-śekhara (Vairocana Wondrous Jewel Lotus Topknot).
He was suddenly born by transformation within a lotus flower, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man and endowed with the seven treasures;
he ruled over the four continents and constantly instructed all living beings through the True Dharma. This king possessed...
He had a thousand sons, handsome, brave, and strong, capable of subduing enemies and foes.
He had a hundred trillion nayutas of palace ladies and handmaidens, all of whom had planted roots of goodness together with the king, practiced the same virtues, and were born at the same time;
they were as beautiful and exquisite as celestial maidens, their bodies were of true golden color and constantly emitted radiance, and from every pore they perpetually issued forth wondrous sounds.
He was fully endowed with ten billion excellent ministers and fierce generals. The king had a principal consort named Pūrṇamukhī, who was a jewel among women.
She was exceptionally beautiful and peerless; her skin was golden, and her eyes and hair were deep blue. Her speech was like the Brahma-voice, and her body possessed a celestial fragrance.

It constantly emits radiance that illuminates a thousand *yojanas*. It has a daughter named Samantaprajñārci-vicitraguṇanetra, whose physical form is upright and majestic, and whose appearance is exceptionally beautiful; sentient beings who behold her can never tire of doing so.
At that time, the lifespan of sentient beings was immeasurable, though some were of indeterminate duration and met with untimely death. They possessed various forms and colors, and various voices.
There are various names, various clans and lineages, and differences in ignorance or wisdom, courage or timidity, poverty or wealth, and suffering or happiness;
these immeasurable categories are all distinct. At times, some person may say to another, "My body is handsome, while your form is base and ugly.

Having spoken such words, they mutually revile and insult one another, thereby accumulating unwholesome karma. Because of this karma, their lifespan, physical appearance, and strength—[are diminished].
All pleasant things were entirely diminished. At that time, to the north of that city, there was a bodhi tree named Universal Radiance Dharma-Cloud Sound Banner.
It manifested the adornments of the *bodhimaṇḍa* of all Tathāgatas in every thought-moment;
its roots were made of firm *maṇi* jewels, its trunk of all kinds of *maṇi* gems, and its leaves of various exquisite treasures.
They were arranged in successive order, harmoniously proportioned, and perfectly adorned throughout the four directions, above, and below.
They emitted precious light and produced wondrous sounds, proclaiming the profound realm of all Tathāgatas.

Before those trees was a fragrant pond named Jewel Flower Radiance (*Ratnapuṣpāvabhāsa*), which resounded with the thunderous voice of the Dharma. Its banks were made of exquisite jewels, and it spanned hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas.
It was surrounded by jewel trees, each shaped like a bodhi tree, with various precious necklaces hanging down from them.
Immeasurable pavilions, all made of jewels, stood everywhere throughout the site of enlightenment as magnificent adornments.
Within that fragrant pond emerged a great lotus flower named "Cloud of the Adorned Realm Manifesting All Tathāgatas of the Three Times. Mount Sumeru...
Within it, Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of a mountain appeared. The first of these Buddhas was named Universal Wisdom Jewel Flame Wondrous Virtue Banner;
upon this flower, he first attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
For immeasurable thousands of years, he expounded the True Dharma to mature sentient beings. Before that Tathāgata had attained Buddhahood, for ten thousand years—
Prior to this, a great lotus emitted pure radiance called "Manifesting All Supernatural Powers to Mature Sentient Beings.

Any sentient being who encountered this light would have their minds spontaneously awakened, such that there was nothing they did not understand; they knew that ten thousand years hence, a Buddha would appear.
Nine thousand years prior, it emitted pure radiance called "Stainless Lamp for All Sentient Beings. If...
Any sentient beings who encounter this light obtain pure eyes and see all forms; they know that nine thousand years hence a Buddha shall appear.
Eight thousand years prior to that, he emits a great radiance called "The Sound of the Karmic Results of All Sentient Beings."
If there are sentient beings who encounter this light, they shall all come to know for themselves the retributions of their various karmas.
They will know that eight thousand years hence a Buddha shall appear, and seven thousand years prior to his appearance, he will emit a great radiance named "Sound that Produces All Roots of Virtue."
If there are sentient beings who encounter this light, all their faculties will become fully perfected. They will know that seven thousand years hence a Buddha shall appear.
Six thousand years prior [to that], he emits a great radiance called "The Sound of the Inconceivable Realm of the Buddha.
If there are sentient beings who encounter this light, their minds will become vast and they will universally attain mastery. They will know six thousand...
Five thousand years before the Buddha’s appearance, he will emit a great radiance called “The Sound that Adorns and Purifies All Buddha-fields.
Any sentient beings who encounter this light will see all pure buddha-fields and know that the Buddha shall appear five thousand years hence.
Four thousand years before his appearance, he will emit a great radiance called “All Tathāgatas.”
The Lamp of Non-differentiation of Realms: If there are sentient beings who encounter this light, they are all able to go and behold all Buddhas.
They know that four thousand years hence a Buddha shall appear. Three thousand years prior [to his appearance], he emits a great radiance named "Lamp Illuminating the Three Times.
If there are sentient beings who encounter this light, they are all able to manifest and see all Tathāgatas.
In the ocean of past events, he knew that three thousand years hence a Buddha would appear.
Two thousand years prior to that, he emitted a great radiance called "The Tathāgata’s Lamp of Wisdom Free from Obscuration.

Any sentient being who encountered this light would obtain the universal eye (*sarvacakṣus*), whereby they could see the spiritual transformations of all Tathāgatas, all Buddha-fields, and all sentient beings in all worlds.

He knows that two thousand years hence a Buddha shall appear. One thousand years prior to that, he emits a great radiance called "Causing All Sentient Beings to See the Buddha and Accumulate Roots of Goodness. Any sentient being who encounters this light attains the Samādhi of Seeing the Buddha.
He knows that one thousand years hence a Buddha shall appear. Seven days prior to that, he again emits a great...
This light is named "The Sound of Joy for All Sentient Beings. If there are sentient beings who encounter this light, they will be able to see all Buddhas everywhere and give rise to great joy.
They will know that after seven days, a Buddha shall appear. When the seven days have fully elapsed, all worlds will tremble;
they will become purely clean and untainted, and in every thought-moment, all the pure [realms] of the ten directions will be universally manifested.

He purifies the Buddha-fields and also manifests their various adornments. If there are sentient beings whose faculties and natures are matured and who ought to see the Buddha, they all proceed to the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*).

At that time, within those worlds, all the peripheral mountain ranges (*cakravāḍa*), all the Sumeru mountains, all the various mountains, all the great oceans, all the lands, all the cities, and all the walls—
From all the palaces, all the music, and all the speech, there issued forth sounds praising and expounding the realm of the supernatural powers of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, there issued forth clouds of all kinds of incense, clouds of all kinds of burning incense, clouds of all kinds of powdered incense,
clouds of all kinds of fragrant maṇi images, clouds of all kinds of jewel flames, and clouds of all kinds of flame-treasures.
They manifested clouds of all kinds of mani-gem garments, clouds of all kinds of necklaces and ornaments, clouds of all kinds of exquisite flowers, clouds of the light of all Tathāgatas,
clouds of the circular halos of all Tathāgatas, clouds of all kinds of music, clouds of the voices of the vows of all Tathāgatas,
clouds of the ocean of the speech-sounds of all Tathāgatas, and clouds of the primary and secondary marks of all Tathāgatas.

The appearance of the Tathāgata in the world is an inconceivable phenomenon. Good son, this Great Jewel Lotus King, which adorns the spheres of all Tathāgatas throughout the three periods of time, is surrounded by as many lotuses as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields.
Within each of these lotuses is a lion throne made of a treasury of mani jewels. One by one...
Upon each seat, there were bodhisattvas sitting in the full lotus posture. "Good son,
when that Tathāgata Universal Wisdom Jewel Flame Wondrous Virtue Banner King attained unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment here,
he simultaneously attained unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment in all worlds throughout the ten directions, in accordance with the minds of sentient beings."
He appears before them all to turn the wheel of Dharma. In each and every world, he causes immeasurable sentient beings to leave the suffering of the evil realms;
he causes immeasurable sentient beings to attain birth in the heavens; he causes immeasurable sentient beings to abide in the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
and he causes immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the practice for the awakening of renunciation. He causes immeasurable...
They cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the bodhi-practice of the Banner of Valour;
they cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the bodhi-practice of the Radiance of Dharma; they cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the bodhi-practice of Pure Faculties;
they cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the bodhi-practice of Equal Power; they cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish...

The bodhisattva practice of entering the city of Dharma; the bodhisattva practice of causing immeasurable sentient beings to achieve the indestructible power of spiritual penetrations that reaches all places;
the bodhisattva practice of causing immeasurable sentient beings to enter the path of universal-gate skillful means;
the bodhisattva practice of causing immeasurable sentient beings to dwell securely in the gates of samādhi; the bodhisattva practice of causing...
They measure the maturation of sentient beings by accomplishing the bodhisattva practice that takes all pure objects as its condition.
They cause immeasurable sentient beings to resolve upon bodhicitta; they cause immeasurable sentient beings to abide in the bodhisattva path;

they cause immeasurable sentient beings to dwell securely in the path of the pure pāramitās; they cause immeasurable sentient beings to abide in the first stage of a bodhisattva; they cause immeasurable...
Sentient beings dwell in the second through the tenth bodhisattva stages. They cause immeasurable sentient beings to enter the supreme practices and vows of a bodhisattva;
they cause immeasurable sentient beings to abide securely in the pure practices and vows of Samantabhadra. Good son!
When that Tathāgata Samantabhadrajñānaratnārci-sudharmadhvaja manifested such inconceivable and sovereign spiritual powers while turning the wheel of Dharma,
he tamed immeasurable sentient beings in each and every world-system, according to their needs, moment by moment.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra knew that the sentient beings within the city of Ratnakusumapradīparāja were relying on their own [pride].
Due to their physical appearance and various sensory objects, they give rise to arrogance and treat others with contempt.
They manifest wondrous bodies that are upright and extraordinary, and proceed to that city, emitting great radiance that illuminates everything universally,
causing all other lights— the light of that noble king, his various exquisite jewels, the sun, moon, stars, and the bodies of sentient beings— to become completely invisible, just like...
When the sun rises, its brilliance eclipses all other sights, just as a mass of ink is set against Jāmbūnada gold. At that time, all sentient beings spoke thus:
"Who is this? Is it a deva or a Brahmā who now emits this light, causing all the radiance of our own bodies to become unmanifest?
Though they reflected in various ways, none could understand it. Then, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra—
Dwelling in the sky above that precious palace of the wheel-turning monarch, they addressed him, saying:
"Great King, you should know that a Buddha has now appeared in the world within your kingdom, beneath the Bodhi tree named Universal Radiance Dharma-Cloud Sound Banner."

At that time, the noble king’s daughter, Padmavilocanā, beheld the sovereign radiance of the physical body manifested by Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and heard the sublime sounds issuing from the various ornaments upon his body;
her heart was filled with joy, and she formed this thought: "By all my roots of goodness, may I obtain such a body, such adornments, and such marks."

Excellent. With such majestic deportment and such mastery, this Great Sage is now able to emit a great radiance within the long night of darkness of the birth and death of sentient beings, revealing that the Tathāgata has appeared in the world.
May I also attain such [power] to act as a light of wisdom for all sentient beings, shattering all the darkness of their ignorance.
“O Darkness! May I never be separated from this spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) in whatever place I am born.

“Good son, at that time the Wheel-Turning King, together with his precious queen, his thousand sons, his retinue, his ministers and assistants, the fourfold army, and the immeasurable people within the city, surrounded him on all sides. By the king’s supernatural power, they ascended together into the void.”

It was one yojana in height and emitted a great radiance that illuminated the four continents, causing all beings everywhere to behold it, so that sentient beings might encounter the Buddha at every turn. He then praised him in verse, saying:
The Tathāgata has appeared in the world to universally save all living beings; you should all rise quickly and go to where the Guide resides.
Only after immeasurable and incalculable eons does a Buddha arise in the world to proclaim the profound and wondrous Dharma, benefiting all multitudes. The Buddha observes all worlds.
Perpetually deluded by inversions, they suffer the pains of saṃsāra; Thus, for countless billions of kalpas, he gave rise to the mind of great compassion.
Cultivating the practices of bodhi, he sought to deliver all sentient beings.
By the power of this great compassion, he was able to relinquish everything— His head, eyes, hands, feet, and so forth.
For the sake of seeking enlightenment, throughout such immeasurable kalpas—indeed, across countless billions of kalpas—a Teacher is difficult to encounter.
If one should see, hear, or serve him, none of it shall pass in vain.
Now, together with you all, let us go to behold the Honored Tamer, seated upon the seat of the Tathāgata.
Having subdued Māra and attained perfect enlightenment, I gaze upon the body of the Tathāgata,
Which radiates immeasurable light of various subtle and wondrous colors, Extinguishing all darkness. From every single pore,
inconceivable rays of light are emitted, Universally illuminating all living beings, Causing them all to experience great joy.
"You all should together give rise to a mind of vast and great diligence, and go to where that Tathāgata dwells to pay him respectful homage and make offerings.
At that time, the Wheel-Turning Sage King, having spoken these verses in praise of the Buddha and awakened all sentient beings, [departed] from the wheel-turning king...
From their roots of goodness, ten thousand kinds of great clouds of offerings emerged and proceeded to the site of enlightenment toward the presence of the Tathāgata.

These were: clouds of all kinds of jewel canopies, clouds of all kinds of flower curtains, clouds of all kinds of precious robes, clouds of all kinds of nets of precious bells, clouds of all kinds of oceans of incense, clouds of all kinds of precious thrones, clouds of all kinds of precious banners, and clouds of all kinds of palaces.
Clouds of all kinds of exquisite flowers and clouds of all manner of ornaments filled and adorned the entirety of space.

Having arrived, she prostrated at the feet of the Tathāgata Universal Wisdom Jewel Flame Exquisite Virtue Banner King, circumambulated him countless hundreds of thousands of times, and sat before the Buddha upon a jewel lotus throne that radiates light throughout the ten directions. At that time, the daughter of the universal monarch—
Samantaprajñārci-vicitraguṇanetra immediately untied all the ornaments upon her body and scattered them over the Buddha.
At that moment, the ornaments transformed in mid-air into a precious canopy with jeweled nets hanging down, which the Dragon King held aloft.
All the palaces were arranged in rows in the center, surrounded on all sides by ten kinds of precious canopies, their shapes like multi-storied pavilions both inside and out.
Pure were the clouds of various necklaces and the various jewel-trees, adorned with mani-jewels from the ocean of fragrance.
Within this canopy was a Bodhi tree, its branches and leaves flourishing and spreading to universally cover the Dharma-realm, manifesting infinite adornments in every thought-moment.
Beneath this tree sat the Tathāgata Vairocana, [surrounded by] as many beings as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-lands.

They were surrounded by a multitude of bodhisattvas from before and behind, all of whom had arisen from the practices and vows of Samantabhadra and dwelt in the non-differentiated abodes of bodhisattvas.
They also saw all the lords of the world, and they also beheld the sovereign spiritual powers of the Tathāgata.
Furthermore, he saw the successive formation and destruction of all worlds throughout all kalpas.
He also saw the successive appearance of all Buddhas in all those worlds.
He also saw that in each and every one of those worlds, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva was making offerings to the Buddhas and taming sentient beings. He also saw all those bodhisattvas.
There is nothing that does not abide within the body of Samantabhadra. One also sees one's own body within that body;
and one also sees that body before all Tathāgatas, before all Samantabhadras, before all Bodhisattvas, and before all sentient beings.
Furthermore, one also sees all those worlds, each of which contains as many worlds as there are atoms in a Buddha-field.
Various boundaries; various supports; various shapes; various essential natures; various arrangements;
various adornments; various purities; covered above by clouds of various adornments; various names of eons; various appearances of Buddhas;
various periods of the three times; various locations; various ways of abiding within the Dharma-realm; various...
Entering the Dharma-realm: various abodes in space; various bodhimaṇḍas of the Tathāgatas; various supernormal powers of the Tathāgatas;
various lion thrones of the Tathāgatas; various oceans of assemblies of the Tathāgatas; various distinctions among the congregations of the Tathāgatas;
various skillful means of the Tathāgatas; various turnings of the wheel of Dharma by the Tathāgatas; various...

Having beheld the arrival of wondrous sounds, the ocean-like utterances of various Tathāgatas, and the cloud-like sūtras of various Tathāgatas, his mind became pure and he gave rise to great joy. [He saw] the Tathāgata Universal Wisdom Jewel-Flame Wondrous Virtue Banner King.
For her, he preached the sūtra named "The Turning of the Wheel of Dharma by All Tathāgatas," with sūtras as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields serving as its retinue.
When that woman had heard this sūtra, she immediately attained ten thousand gateways of samādhi;
her mind became supple and free from rigidity, like one newly conceived in the womb, like one just born, or like...
Just as the śāla tree first produces sprouts, so too is that samādhi-mind; namely,
the samādhi of manifestly seeing all Buddhas, the samādhi of universally illuminating all lands, the samādhi of entering the gates of all three periods of time,
the samādhi of proclaiming the Dharma wheel of all Buddhas, the samādhi of knowing the ocean of vows of all Buddhas, and the samādhi of awakening all sentient beings.
The samādhi that causes birth to transcend the suffering of saṃsāra; the samādhi of constantly aspiring to shatter the darkness of all sentient beings;
the samādhi of constantly aspiring to extinguish the suffering of all sentient beings; the samādhi of constantly aspiring to give rise to the happiness of all sentient beings;
the samādhi of teaching and transforming all sentient beings without ever becoming weary; and the samādhi of the unobstructed banner of all bodhisattvas.
The Samādhi of Universally Visiting All Pure Buddha-fields.

Having attained these ten thousand samādhis, he further attained the mind of wondrous concentration, the immovable mind, the joyful mind, the comforting mind, the vast mind, the mind that accords with spiritual friends, the mind that takes as its object all-pervasive profound omniscience, and the mind that abides in the ocean of vast skillful means; he abandoned all attachments.
A mind free from attachment; a mind that does not dwell upon any worldly realms; a mind that enters the realm of the Tathāgatas;
a mind that universally illumines the ocean of all forms; a mind free from affliction and harm; a mind free from arrogance; a mind free from weariness; and a mind free from regression.
A mind free from indolence; a mind contemplating the self-nature of all phenomena; a mind dwelling securely in the ocean of all dharma-gates; a mind observing the ocean of all dharma-gates;
a mind that thoroughly understands the ocean of all sentient beings; a mind that rescues and protects the ocean of all sentient beings;
a mind that universally illumines the ocean of all worlds; and a mind that universally gives rise to the ocean of all Buddhas' vows. All...
The mind that shatters the mountain of all obstacles; the mind that accumulates merit as an aid to the path; the mind that directly perceives the ten powers of all Buddhas;
the mind that universally illumines the realm of Bodhisattvas; the mind that increases the Bodhisattva’s aids to the path; the mind that universally takes all oceans of directions as its object;
and the single-minded contemplation of the great vows of Samantabhadra, which issues forth [vows] as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-lands of all Tathāgatas.
The ocean of vows: the vow to adorn and purify all Buddha-lands; the vow to tame all sentient beings; the vow to universally know the entire dharma-realm;
the vow to universally enter the ocean of all dharma-realms; the vow to cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva in all Buddha-fields throughout all kalpas until the end of the future;
the vow never to abandon any bodhisattva practice throughout all kalpas until the end of the future. The vow...
May I attain proximity to all Tathāgatas. May I vow to serve all spiritual friends. May I vow to make offerings to all Buddhas.
May I vow that in every thought-moment I cultivate the bodhisattva practices, increasing all-encompassing wisdom without interruption.
Having thus made oceans of vows as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields, she accomplished all the great vows of Samantabhadra.
Then, that Tathāgata further revealed and expounded for her daughter the roots of goodness accumulated since first generating the mind of enlightenment and the sublime practices cultivated therein;
he caused her to realize the great fruits attained and to fulfill the ocean of all the Tathāgatas' vows.
