"You are able to seek the bodhisattva conduct by relying on a spiritual friend. Son of good family, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation door called 'The Great Adornment of Joy Arising in Every Thought-Moment. Sudhana said, 'Noble One, what is the activity of this liberation door?
What is its sphere of action? By what means does it arise? What does it observe? The night goddess replied, 'Son of good family..."
I give rise to a mind of pure, impartial aspiration. I give rise to a mind of pure, firm, and indestructible aspiration, free from all worldly dust and defilement.
I give rise to a mind that never regresses, taking the stage of non-retrogression as its object.
I give rise to an immovable mind, adorned with the jewel-mountain of merit. I give rise to...
I give rise to a mind that dwells nowhere. I give rise to a mind that universally manifests before all sentient beings to rescue and protect them.
I give rise to a mind that never tires of beholding the ocean of all Buddhas. I give rise to a mind that seeks the power of the pure vows of all Bodhisattvas.
I give rise to a mind that abides in the ocean of the light of great wisdom. I give rise to a mind that causes all sentient beings...
I give rise to a mind that transcends the wilderness of sorrow and affliction. I resolve to cause all sentient beings to abandon hearts of grief, lamentation, suffering, and distress.
I resolve to cause all sentient beings to abandon hearts that find no pleasure in forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental phenomena.
I resolve to cause all sentient beings to abandon the suffering of separation from the beloved and the encounter with the hated and the malicious.
I resolve to give rise to the mind that causes all sentient beings to abandon the suffering of evil conditions, ignorance, and the like.
I resolve to give rise to the mind that acts as a refuge for all sentient beings in perilous difficulties.

I resolve to give rise to the mind that causes all sentient beings to emerge from the realm of suffering within birth and death. I resolve to give rise to the mind that causes all sentient beings to abandon the sufferings of birth, old age, and sickness.
With a mind that gives rise to the suffering of death and other such states, I resolve to cause all sentient beings to achieve the unsurpassed Dharma-bliss of the Tathāgata.

I resolve to cause all sentient beings to experience joy and happiness. Having given rise to this mind, I further teach them the Dharma so that they may gradually reach the stage of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-bhūmi*). That is to say, if I see sentient beings who are attached to their dwellings...
Regarding palaces and dwellings, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may thoroughly understand the self-nature of all phenomena and become free from all attachments.

If I see sentient beings who are attached to their parents, brothers, sisters, or siblings, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may gain entry into the pure assemblies of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
If I see sentient beings who are attached to their wives and children, I preach the Dharma for them.
I cause them to abandon the defilement of craving for birth and death and to give rise to great compassion, regarding all sentient beings with equanimity and non-duality.

If I see sentient beings dwelling in royal palaces, served by court ladies and attendants, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may assemble with the holy ones and enter the teaching of the Tathāgata.
If I see sentient beings who are stained by and attached to sensory objects, I preach the Dharma for them...

I shall cause them to enter the realm of the Tathāgata. If I see sentient beings who are full of anger and resentment, I shall preach the Dharma for them so that they may abide in the Tathāgata’s perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*).

If I see sentient beings whose minds are indolent, I shall preach the Dharma for them so that they may attain the pure perfection of vigor (*vīrya-pāramitā*). If I see sentient beings whose minds are distracted, I shall...

I preach the Dharma so that they may attain the Tathāgata’s dhyāna-pāramitā. If I see sentient beings entering the dense forest of views and obstructed by the darkness of ignorance, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may emerge from that thicket and darkness.
If I see sentient beings who lack wisdom, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may attain the prajñā-pāramitā. If I see sentient beings who are stained by and attached to the three...
Regarding the realms: for those beings I teach the Dharma so that they may transcend birth and death.
If I see beings whose aspirations are inferior, I teach them the Dharma so that they may fulfill their vow for the Bodhi of a Buddha.

If I see beings dwelling in practices for their own benefit, I teach them the Dharma so that they may give rise to the vow to benefit all sentient beings. If I see beings whose resolve and strength are feeble...
To those who are weak, I preach the Dharma so that they may attain the Bodhisattva’s perfection of power (*bala-pāramitā*).
If I see sentient beings with minds shrouded in the darkness of ignorance, I preach the Dharma so that they may attain the Bodhisattva’s perfection of wisdom (*jñāna-pāramitā*).
If I see sentient beings whose physical forms are incomplete, I preach the Dharma so that they may attain the Tathāgata’s pure form-body (*rūpa-kāya*). If I see sentient beings of ugly appearance...
"O base ones! For those who see that sentient beings have attained the unsurpassed, pure Dharma-body, I preach the Dharma so that they may likewise attain it.
If I see that sentient beings have coarse and evil physical forms, I preach the Dharma so that they may attain the subtle and wondrous form-body of a Tathāgata.

If I see that sentient beings are filled with much sorrow and affliction, I preach the Dharma so that they may attain the ultimate peace and happiness of a Tathāgata. If I see that sentient beings are impoverished..."
Suffering. For them, I preach the Dharma so that they may obtain the jewel-treasury of bodhisattva merit.
If I see sentient beings dwelling in gardens and groves, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may diligently seek the causes and conditions of the Buddha-dharma.
If I see sentient beings traveling on roads, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may advance toward the path of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*). If I see sentient beings in villages...
In the midst [of these realms], I preach the Dharma for them so that they may emerge from the triple world.
If I see sentient beings dwelling in the human realm, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may transcend the paths of the two vehicles and abide in the stage of the Tathāgata.
If I see sentient beings residing in cities and fortresses, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may dwell within the city of the Dharma King. If I see sentient beings abiding in the four...
In the corners, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may attain the wisdom of the equality of the three periods of time.
If I see sentient beings dwelling in various directions, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may attain the wisdom that perceives all phenomena.

If I see sentient beings whose conduct is dominated by craving, I preach the gate of the contemplation of impurity for them, so that they may abandon their attachment and defilement toward birth and death. If I see sentient beings...
To those whose conduct is dominated by anger, I teach the gate of the contemplation of great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), causing them to enter it and practice it with diligence.
If I see sentient beings whose conduct is dominated by delusion, I teach them the Dharma so that they may attain clear wisdom and contemplate the ocean of all phenomena (*dharmasāgara*).
If I see sentient beings whose conduct consists of equal parts of the afflictions, I teach them the Dharma so that they may enter the vows of the various vehicles (*yāna*).
Sāgara. If I see sentient beings who delight in the pleasures of birth and death, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may develop weary detachment.

If I see sentient beings who weary of the suffering of birth and death and are fit to be transformed and delivered by the Tathāgata, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may skillfully manifest rebirth.
If I see sentient beings who are attached to the five aggregates, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may attain...
I dwell in the realm of non-reliance. If I see sentient beings whose minds are inferior, I manifest for them the path of supreme adornment.
If I see sentient beings whose minds give rise to arrogance, I preach for them the patience of the equality of dharmas (*samatā-dharma-kṣānti*).
If I see sentient beings whose minds are deceitful and crooked, I preach for them the straightforward mind of a bodhisattva. Good son, by means of these...

I bestowed immeasurable Dharma-gifts, gathering in all sentient beings. Through various skillful means, I taught and tamed them, causing them to leave the evil realms and receive the joys of humans and devas, to be liberated from the bonds of the triple world, and to abide in omniscience.
At that time, I attained a vast ocean of the light of the Dharma of great joy; my mind was serene, at ease, peaceful, and delighted. Furthermore, son of good family, I constantly contemplate...
He observed the assemblies at the bodhimandas of all the bodhisattvas: those who cultivate various vows and practices; manifest various pure bodies;
possess various constant radiances; emit various rays of light; enter the gateway of omniscience through various skillful means;
enter various samādhis; manifest various supernatural transformations; produce oceans of various sounds; and are endowed with various adornments.
With their bodies, they enter various gates of the Tathāgatas; they travel to various oceans of lands; they behold various oceans of Buddhas;
they attain various oceans of eloquence; they illumine various realms of liberation; they obtain various oceans of the light of wisdom;
they enter various oceans of samādhis; they sport within various doors of liberation; and by means of various gates, they proceed toward omniscience.
They adorn the space of the dharma-realm with various ornaments, covering the entirety of space with clouds of diverse adornments.
They observe the various assemblies at sites of enlightenment, gathering from various worlds, entering various buddha-fields, and proceeding to various oceans of directions.
Having received various commands from various Tathāgatas, and accompanied by various Bodhisattvas from the presence of various Tathāgatas, they rained down clouds of various adornments;

they entered the various skillful means of the Tathāgatas, contemplated the various oceans of the Tathāgatas' teachings, entered the various oceans of wisdom, and sat upon various adorned seats. Good son, I observed this assembly at the site of enlightenment.
I understood that the Buddha’s spiritual power is immeasurable and boundless, and I gave rise to great joy.
Good son, I observed that the Tathāgata Vairocana manifests inconceivable, pure physical bodies in every thought-moment;
having seen this, I gave rise to great joy. Furthermore, I observed that in every thought-moment the Tathāgata emits great rays of light, filling the entire Dharma-realm.

Having seen this, he gave rise to great joy. Furthermore, he saw that from each and every pore of the Tathāgata, there issued forth in every moment oceans of light rays as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable Buddha-fields.

Each individual ray of light was accompanied by a retinue of light rays as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable Buddha-fields, pervading the entirety of all *dharmadhātus* and extinguishing all [suffering].

Having seen the suffering of all sentient beings, I give rise to great joy. Furthermore, son of good family, I observe that from the crown of the Tathāgata’s head and his two shoulders, there emerge in every thought-moment clouds of jewel-flame mountains as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, filling all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions.
Having seen this, I give rise to great joy. Furthermore, son of good family, I...

I contemplate each and every pore of the Tathāgata, from which, in every moment of thought, there issue clouds of fragrant light equal in number to the atoms of all Buddha-fields, filling all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions. Having seen this, I give rise to great joy.
Furthermore, son of good family, I contemplate each and every mark of the Tathāgata, from which, in every moment of thought, there issue [clouds] equal in number to the atoms of all Buddha-fields.
The clouds of the Tathāgata’s body, adorned with all marks, pervade all worlds throughout the ten directions.

Having seen this, they give rise to great joy. Furthermore, son of good family, I observe that from every single pore of the Tathāgata, in each and every thought-moment, there issue forth clouds of Buddha-transformations as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, manifesting the Tathāgata from his first resolution...
With a mind cultivating the *pāramitās* and fully adorning the path, they enter the bodhisattva path; having seen this, they give rise to great joy.

Furthermore, son of good family, I observe that from each and every pore of the Tathāgata, in every thought-moment, there emerge clouds of bodies of celestial kings, as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, along with the sovereign spiritual transformations of those celestial kings.
Pervading all the ten directions of the Dharma-realm, he manifests before those who are to be liberated by the body of a celestial king (*devendra*) and preaches the Dharma for them.

Having seen this, they give rise to great joy. Like clouds of celestial kings, there are likewise clouds of dragon kings (*nāgendra*), yakṣa kings (*yakṣendra*), gandharva kings (*gandharvendra*), asura kings (*asurendra*), garuḍa kings (*garuḍendra*), and kiṃnara kings (*kiṃnarendra*).

The clouds of bodies of the Mahoraga kings, the human kings, and the Brahma kings—there was not one among them who did not manifest in this manner and preach the Dharma in this manner from every single pore.

Having seen this, in every thought-moment I gave rise to great joy and great faith and delight, equal in measure to the *dharmadhātu* and to omniscience (*sarvajñā*). What I had never attained before, I have now for the first time attained. Previously...
That which was not yet realized is now for the first time realized; that which was not yet entered is now for the first time entered;

that which was not yet fulfilled is now for the first time fulfilled; that which was not yet seen is now for the first time seen; that which was not yet heard is now for the first time heard. Why is this?

Because they are able to thoroughly understand the characteristics of the *dharmadhātu*, and because they know that all phenomena possess but a single characteristic. They are thus able to [attain] equanimity.
Because they enter equally into the paths of the three periods of time, and because they are able to expound all boundless dharmas.
Good son, I have entered this Bodhisattva liberation-light ocean of the "Great Joyful Adornment Arising in Every Thought-moment. Furthermore, good son:
This liberation is boundless, for it universally enters the gates of all dharma-realms. This liberation is inexhaustible, for it equally gives rise to the mind of the nature of omniscience.
This liberation is limitless, for it enters the thoughts and perceptions of all sentient beings throughout the boundaries of the infinite.
This liberation is profoundly deep and tranquil, for it is the object of knowledge known by wisdom. This liberation is vast...
This liberation is great because it pervades the spheres of all Tathāgatas. This liberation is known by the unimpeded eye of wisdom of Bodhisattvas.
This liberation is bottomless, for it reaches the very source and foundation of the Dharma-realm.
This liberation is the Universal Gate, because within a single phenomenon one universally perceives all miraculous transformations. This liberation is ultimately...
It cannot be grasped, for all dharmas are equal and non-dual within the Dharmakāya. This liberation is ultimately without birth, because one has realized that all phenomena are like illusions.
This liberation is like a reflected image, for it is produced by the light of the vows of omniscience.
This liberation is like a magical transformation, for it arises from the sublime practices of the emanated Bodhisattvas. This...
Liberation is like the great earth, for it serves as the foundation for all sentient beings.
This liberation is like great water, for it can moisten all with great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*).
This liberation is like a great fire, for it dries up the waters of craving and attachment in sentient beings. This liberation is like a great wind, which causes all sentient beings...
Because it swiftly proceeds toward all-knowledge; because this liberation is like the great ocean, adorned with the various merits for the sake of all sentient beings;
because this liberation is like Mount Sumeru, from which emerges the ocean of the Dharma-treasures of all-knowledge;
and because this liberation is like a great city, adorned with all sublime Dharmas.
This liberation is like space, for it universally accommodates the spiritual power of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
This liberation is like a great cloud, for it universally rains down the rain of Dharma upon all sentient beings.
This liberation is like the pure sun, for it can shatter the darkness of ignorance within sentient beings. This liberation is like the full moon, for it brings fulfillment to the vast and great.
Because it is an ocean of merit. This liberation is like *tathatā* (suchness), for it is able to pervade all places.
This liberation is like one’s own reflection, for it is manifested from one’s own wholesome karma.
This liberation is like an echo, for it preaches the Dharma in accordance with what is appropriate. This liberation is like a reflected image.
Because it manifests in accordance with the minds of sentient beings; because this liberation is like the king of great trees, for it causes all the flowers of supernatural powers to bloom;
because this liberation is like a diamond, for from the very beginning it has been indestructible.
This liberation is like a wish-fulfilling jewel, for it gives rise to immeasurable powers of mastery.
This liberation is like the king of maṇi-jewels, the stainless treasury, for it manifests all the spiritual powers of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
This liberation is like the *nandadhvaja* (joy-banner) maṇi jewel, for it can equally produce the sounds of the Dharma wheels of all Buddhas.
Son of good family, I shall now speak this parable for you; you should contemplate it and enter into realization accordingly.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to the night goddess Śāntamati-sāgaravatī, "O Great Sage, how should one practice?"
"By practicing these, one attains this liberation. The night goddess said, "Noble son, a bodhisattva attains this liberation by practicing ten great treasuries of Dharma.
What are the ten? First, the practice of the great treasury of generosity, which completely satisfies the minds of all sentient beings according to their inclinations.
Second, the practice of the great treasury of pure ethical discipline, which universally enters the ocean of all buddhas' merits. Third..."
1. Cultivating the vast Dharma-treasury of patience (*kṣānti*), one is able to contemplate the nature of all phenomena (*dharmatā*) universally.
2. Cultivating the vast Dharma-treasury of diligence (*vīrya*), one proceeds toward omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) without ever turning back. 3.

Cultivating the vast Dharma-treasury of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), one is able to extinguish the feverish afflictions of all sentient beings. 4. Cultivating the vast Dharma-treasury of wisdom (*prajñā*), one is able to comprehend everything universally.
7. The vast treasury of the Dharma-sea of cultivating skillful means, which can universally bring all oceans of sentient beings to maturity; 8.
The vast treasury of cultivating all vows, extending throughout all oceans of Buddha-fields and sentient beings, practicing the bodhisattva path for as long as all future kalpas endure;
9. The vast treasury of cultivating all powers, manifesting all dharmas in every thought-moment.
The ocean of realms: in all Buddha-lands, they constantly and without rest attain equal and perfect enlightenment.
They cultivate the ten vast treasuries of pure wisdom, thereby attaining the Tathāgata’s wisdom that universally knows all phenomena of the three periods of time without obstruction.
Good son, if Bodhisattvas abide in these ten great treasuries of Dharma, they will be able to obtain such [qualities].
Liberation increases in purity; it is accumulated, made firm, stabilized, and brought to perfection.
Sudhana said, "Noble One, how long has it been since you first resolved your mind toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*? The night goddess replied:
"Good son, to the east of this Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean, beyond ten world-oceans, there is a world-ocean named All-Pure Radiance Jewel.
Within this world-ocean is a world-system named Light-Sound of the Vows of All Tathāgatas.
Within it is a world named Pure Radiance Golden Adornment, [adorned with] all fragrant gold."
Its substance is the diamond-mani king; its shape is like a multi-storied pavilion; it is bounded by clouds of various wondrous jewels;
it rests upon a sea of all kinds of precious necklaces and is covered above by clouds of exquisite palaces. It is a mixture of the pure and the impure.
Within this world-system, in ages long past, there was an eon named Universal Radiance Banner and a land named Universally Filled Wondrous Treasury. This was the site of enlightenment.
It was named *Sarvaratnanidhānasudracandraprabha*. There was a Buddha named *Anivartanadharmadhātunirghoṣa* who attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* there.
At that time, I was a bodhi-tree deity named *Puṇyasampannadīpaprabhaketu*, guarding the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*). I witnessed that Buddha attain equal and perfect awakening.
He manifested supernatural powers and resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that very moment, he attained a samādhi called "Universally Illuminating the Ocean of the Tathāgata’s Merits.

Within this site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), there subsequently appeared another Tathāgata in the world named Dharmadrumatejaḥparvata. At that time, my life came to an end and I was reborn therein as a bodhimaṇḍa.

O Night Goddess, named Light of Exquisite Merit and Wisdom, upon seeing that Tathāgata turn the wheel of the true Dharma and manifest great supernormal powers, I immediately attained a samādhi called "Universally Illuminating All Realms Free from Greed.
Subsequently, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata named King of the Sound of the Ocean of All Dharmas; at that time, I was a night goddess, and because of this...
I saw the Buddha, served him, and made offerings to him, whereby I immediately attained a samādhi named "The Ground that Grows All Wholesome Dharmas.
Subsequently, a Tathāgata appeared in the world named Ratnārcis-pradīpa-dhvaja-rāja. At that time, I was a night goddess;
because I saw that Buddha, served him, and made offerings to him, I immediately attained a samādhi named "Universal Manifestation of the Light of Supernatural Powers."
Megha said: "Subsequently, a Tathāgata appeared in the world named Guṇasumeruprabha. At that time, I was a night goddess;
because I was able to see that Buddha, I served and made offerings to him, and immediately attained a samādhi called 'Universally Illuminating the Ocean of All Buddhas.
Subsequently, another Tathāgata appeared in the world named Dharmameghasvararāja. At that time, my body..."
I was a night goddess. Because I was able to see the Buddha, serve him, and make offerings to him, I immediately attained a samādhi named "Lamp of the Ocean of All Dharmas.
Subsequently, a Tathāgata appeared in the world named King Illuminating with the Lamp of Wisdom. At that time, I was again a night goddess;
because I was able to see that Buddha, serve him, and make offerings to him, I immediately attained a samādhi named "Extinguishing All Multitudes."
The Lamp of Pure Radiance Born from Suffering. Next, a Tathāgata appeared in the world named Dharma-vīra-suvimala-śrī-ketu.

At that time, I was a night goddess; because I was able to see that Buddha, I served and made offerings to him, and immediately attained a samādhi called the "Radiant Treasury of the Tathāgatas of the Three Times. Next, a Tathāgata appeared in the world named Siṃha.

Dharmajñānapradīpa-vikrama. At that time, I was a night goddess; because I was able to see the Buddha, serve him, and make offerings to him, I immediately attained a samādhi named "The Wheel of Unobstructed Wisdom of All Worlds.
Subsequently, another Tathāgata appeared in the world named Jñānabalaśailendra-rāja. At that time, I was again a night goddess, and because I was able to see him...
I served and made offerings to those Buddhas, and immediately attained a samādhi named "Universally Illuminating the Faculties and Conducts of Sentient Beings Throughout the Three Times.

Good son, in the world-system called Pure Radiance Adorned with Gold, during the eon called Universal Radiance Banner, there appeared as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in a buddha-field. At that time, I was either a celestial king or...
He may become a dragon king, or a yakṣa king, or a gandharva king, or an asura king, or a garuḍa king, or a kiṃnara king, or a mahoraga king,
or a human king, or a brahmā king; he may take the body of a deva, or the body of a human, or the body of a man.
Sometimes taking the form of a woman, sometimes the form of a young boy, and sometimes the form of a young girl,
they all made various kinds of offerings to all those Tathāgatas and heard the various dharmas taught by those Buddhas.
Upon the end of their lives there, they were immediately reborn in this very world-system, where they practiced for as many eons as there are atoms in two Buddha-fields.
After practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, he passed away and was reborn in this Sahā world within the Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean.
There he encountered the Tathāgata Krakucchanda, whom he served and made offerings to, thereby attaining a samādhi named "Radiance Free from All Dust and Defilement.
Subsequently, he encountered the Tathāgata Kanakamuni, whom he served and made offerings to, thereby attaining a samādhi named...

He universally manifests all oceans of lands. Next, he encounters the Tathāgata Kāśyapa, whom he serves and makes offerings to, thereby attaining a samādhi named "Expounding the Ocean of the Speech and Sounds of All Sentient Beings.
Next, he encounters the Tathāgata Vairocana, who attains equal and perfect enlightenment at this very site of the Way;
in every thought-moment, the Buddha manifests great supernormal powers. At that time, I beheld him and immediately attained this [samādhi].

The liberation of "the adornment of vast great joy produced in every thought-moment. Having attained this liberation, one is able to enter into oceans of the establishment of the dharma-realm, numbering as many as the atoms in ten unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
Within those oceans of the establishment of the dharma-realm, one sees all the atoms present in every Buddha-field; within each and every atom, there are ten unspeakably [unspeakable... things.

In Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-fields, in each and every Buddha-field, there was the Tathāgata Vairocana seated at the site of enlightenment, attaining perfect awakening in every thought-moment and manifesting various miraculous transformations.
Each of these manifested transformations pervaded the entire ocean of the Dharma-realm; he also saw his own body present in all of them.
He went to the abodes of all the Tathāgatas and heard the sublime Dharma they preached.
Furthermore, he beheld from every single pore of all those Buddhas oceans of emanations that manifested supernatural powers;

throughout the ocean of all dharma-realms, the ocean of all world-systems, the lineage of all worlds, and within every world therein, they turned the wheel of the True Dharma according to the inclinations of sentient beings.
Cakra: "I have attained the power of the swift dhāraṇī; I receive, uphold, and contemplate all words and meanings.
With clear wisdom, I universally enter the treasury of all pure dharmas. With sovereign wisdom, I universally traverse the ocean of all profound dharmas.
With pervasive wisdom, I universally know the vast meanings of the three periods of time. With equalizing wisdom, I universally penetrate all..."
The Buddha’s Dharma is without differentiation. Thus he awakens to and understands all dharma-gates; within each and every dharma-gate, he awakens to and understands clouds of all sūtras;
within each and every cloud of sūtras, he awakens to and understands oceans of all dharmas;
within each and every ocean of dharmas, he awakens to and understands all dharma-categories; and within each and every dharma-category, he awakens to and understands all dharmas.
Cloud: Within each and every Dharma-cloud, one awakens to and understands all streams of phenomena. Within each and every stream of phenomena, there arise all oceans of great joy.
From each and every ocean of great joy, all stages are produced. From each and every stage, all oceans of samādhi are produced.
Within each and every ocean of samādhi, one attains all oceans of seeing Buddhas. Within each and every ocean of seeing Buddhas...
They attain the ocean of light of all-knowledge. Each individual ocean of wisdom-light universally illumines the three periods of time and pervades the ten directions.
They know the ocean of past practices of immeasurable Tathāgatas; they know the ocean of all the former lives of immeasurable Tathāgatas;
they know the ocean of the difficult renunciations and acts of giving of immeasurable Tathāgatas; they know the ocean of the pure wheels of precepts of immeasurable Tathāgatas. They know...
He knows the immeasurable ocean of the pure forbearance of the Tathāgatas; he knows the immeasurable ocean of the vast diligence of the Tathāgatas;
he knows the immeasurable ocean of the profound meditative concentration of the Tathāgatas; he knows the immeasurable ocean of the *prajñāpāramitā* of the Tathāgatas.
They know the ocean of the Tathāgatas’ infinite skillful means-pāramitās; they know the ocean of the Tathāgatas’ infinite vow-pāramitās;
they know the ocean of the Tathāgatas’ infinite power-pāramitās; they know the ocean of the Tathāgatas’ infinite wisdom-pāramitās;
they know the infinite ways in which the Tathāgatas formerly transcended the bodhisattva stages; they know the infinite ways in which the Tathāgatas formerly dwelt.
In the Bodhisattva-bhūmi, throughout oceans of immeasurable eons, they manifest supernormal powers. They know the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ past entry into the bodhisattva stages;
they know the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ past cultivation of the bodhisattva stages; they know the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ past purification of the bodhisattva stages;
they know the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ past contemplation of the bodhisattva stages; they know the immeasurable Tathāgatas...
In the past, when they were bodhisattvas, they constantly beheld all Buddhas.
They knew that immeasurable Tathāgatas, in their former lives as bodhisattvas, had completely seen oceans of Buddhas and oceans of eons while dwelling together.

They knew that immeasurable Tathāgatas, in their former lives as bodhisattvas, had manifested throughout oceans of lands with infinite bodies. They knew that immeasurable Tathāgatas, in their former lives as bodhisattvas, had cultivated [the path] pervading the entire dharma-realm.
The Vast Conduct: knowing how immeasurable Tathāgatas, when they were formerly bodhisattvas, manifested various gates of skillful means to discipline and bring all sentient beings to maturity;
knowing how immeasurable Tathāgatas emit great radiance that universally illumines all oceans of lands throughout the ten directions;
and knowing how immeasurable Tathāgatas manifest great supernormal powers to appear everywhere.
Before all sentient beings, he knows the vast ground of wisdom of immeasurable Tathāgatas; he knows the immeasurable Tathāgatas turning the wheel of the true Dharma;
he knows the immeasurable Tathāgatas manifesting oceans of marks; he knows the immeasurable Tathāgatas manifesting oceans of bodies;
and he knows the oceans of the great power of those Tathāgatas from their first generation of the mind of enlightenment until the extinction of the Dharma.
I know and see all this in every moment of thought. Good son, you asked me: "How long has it been since you first resolved to attain enlightenment?

Good son, in the past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in two Buddha-fields, in the world-system called Pure Light Adorned with Gold, I was a bodhi-tree goddess. There, I heard the Dharma of Non-retrogression...
The Tathāgata Dharmadhātusvararāja taught the Dharma, causing [beings] to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
For as many eons as there are atoms in two Buddha-fields, they cultivated the bodhisattva practices;
only thereafter were they born within this Sahā world during the Bhadrakalpa, from the time of Krakucchanda Buddha until Śākyamuni Buddha, and this...
All the Buddhas who will appear throughout all future kalpas, I shall likewise approach and make offerings to;

just as I make offerings to all future Buddhas within this world during the Bhadrakalpa, so too shall I approach and make offerings to all future Buddhas in all worlds and throughout all kalpas. Well done!
"Good man, that world Adorned with Pure Radiant Gold still exists today; the appearance of Buddhas therein continues without interruption.
You should single-mindedly cultivate this gate of great heroic vigor of a bodhisattva.
Then, the Night Goddess Silent Ocean-Voice, wishing to restate the meaning of this liberation, spoke these verses for the youth Sudhana:
"Good Wealth, listen as I describe this gate of pure liberation; having heard it, give rise to joy and practice diligently until its ultimate fulfillment.
In the past, throughout oceans of eons, I gave birth to a heart of great faith and delight, as pure as space.
Constantly contemplating all-knowledge, I [saw] the Buddhas of the three periods of time."
All gave rise to hearts of faith and joy, together with their assemblies; they all vowed to always remain close to me.
In the past, I once saw a Buddha making offerings for the sake of sentient beings;
having heard the pure Dharma, his heart was filled with great joy. He always honored his parents, revering and making offerings to them.
Thus, without rest or weariness, I have entered this gate of liberation;
I compassionately rescue all those who are old, sick, poor, or lacking in sensory faculties, Causing them all to attain peace and security.
From the terrors of water, fire, kings, and thieves, And from all fears within the great ocean— These various practices I cultivated in the past.
To rescue those sentient beings whose afflictions are ever-blazing, who are entangled and shrouded by karmic obstructions,
and who have fallen into various perilous paths— I shall rescue those sentient beings from all the immeasurable torments of suffering in the evil realms,
and from birth, old age, sickness, death, and the like; I shall utterly extinguish them all.
"May I, throughout all future kalpas, universally act for the sake of all living beings to extinguish the suffering of birth and death and attain the ultimate bliss of Buddhahood.
Good son, I know only this liberation called 'The Vast Array of Excellence Born Moment by Moment. As for those [others]..."
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas enter deeply into the ocean of all dharma-realms; they fully know the number of all kalpas and universally behold the formation and destruction of all lands.
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
Good son, within this assembly of the Tathāgata at the site of enlightenment, there is a night goddess named Guardian of All Cities and Increaser.
“Dīrghatapasvī, go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
At that time, the youth Sudhana, with single-minded attention, observed the body of the night goddess Śāntasvararutasāgaravatī and spoke these verses:
Following the instruction of a virtuous friend, I have come to the abode of the celestial deity.
There I see the deity seated upon a jeweled throne, his physical form boundless; he is not one who clings to appearances or characteristics.
Those of inferior intellect and shallow understanding who reckon that all phenomena exist—neither gods nor humans in this world can know the sphere of the Venerable One.
Though observed for immeasurable eons, it cannot be measured; because its physical marks are boundless, it is far removed from the five aggregates.
It does not abide in any location, having forever severed worldly doubt.
It manifests the power of mastery, neither grasping at internal nor external phenomena, being unmoving and unimpeded.
With the pure eye of wisdom, one beholds the Buddha’s supernormal powers; The body is the treasury of the True Dharma, and the mind is unimpeded knowledge.
Having attained the illumination of wisdom, one further illumines the minds of all sentient beings;
One perceives that the accumulation of boundless karma adorns all worlds, And realizes that these worlds are entirely of the mind.
Manifesting bodies equal in number to all sentient beings, knowing that the world is entirely like a dream;
seeing all Buddhas as reflections and all phenomena as echoes, they cause beings to be free from attachment.

For the sake of sentient beings throughout the three periods of time, they manifest their bodies in every thought-moment, yet their minds dwell nowhere as they preach the Dharma pervasively throughout the ten directions.
The boundless oceans of lands, the oceans of Buddhas, and the oceans of sentient beings— All are contained within a single mote of dust.
This is the power of this Honored One’s liberation.
When the youth Sudhana had spoken these verses, he prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and gazed upon him with profound reverence.
[He] looked up, took his leave, and departed.
Below this is the fifth night goddess, Samudrareṇu-ghoṣa-vijitā. She is associated with the Ground Difficult to Conquer (Sudurjayā).

"Difficult to Conquer" means that because the activities of the two wisdoms—of the ultimate and the conventional—are mutually contradictory, it is extremely difficult to bring them into correspondence. Sudhana has already received [this teaching].

Having understood and dwelt upon the previous instructions of his spiritual friend, he proceeded to the abode of the night goddess Silent Ocean Sound. Upon seeing her, he paid his respects and inquired after her well-being.

At that time, the night goddess praised Sudhana and formally bestowed upon him the Dharma-realm, namely, the Bodhisattva liberation door called "The Arising in Every Thought-Moment of Vast and Great Joyful Adornments. By means of this, the Bodhisattvas of this stage traverse...

Benefiting sentient beings in accordance with worldly conventions, he unifies the provisional and the ultimate. Because he transforms beings through contemplation so that their aspirations are fulfilled, he gives rise to joy;

because he contemplates the supreme functions of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, he experiences great delight. Thus, his transformations proceed without interruption, which is why it is called "arising in every thought-moment.
This is the name and essence of this dharma-gate. Upon hearing the name of this liberation, Sudhana came to understand its profound depth and vastness.
Therefore, he asks: "What is the activity of this liberation? This question concerns the functional activity that arises. Next, he asks: "In what sphere does it operate?
This question concerns the sphere of operation, which is precisely the sphere of liberation. Furthermore, he asks: "By what means does it arise? This question concerns the means by which it arises.
Next, he asks: "What is the contemplation that is able to observe? This question concerns the wisdom of contemplation. There is...
Regarding these four questions, the Night Goddess first answers the first by stating what kind of skillful means she initiates:
"I give rise to a mind of pure, impartial aspiration," and so forth. There are twenty kinds of such minds that serve as the initiating skillful means;

specifically, she takes the mind of the dual cultivation of compassion and wisdom as the means capable of initiation. The former ten [types of mind] initiate the superior-seeking mind for great wisdom, while the latter...
"I resolve to cause all sentient beings to transcend the ten kinds of mental states, such as sorrow and affliction.
This is the great compassionate mind for the sake of those below. These aforementioned twenty kinds of minds comprise thirteen and a half lines of scripture. Next, it says:
"Having generated these minds, he further teaches the Dharma so that they may gradually reach the stage of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-bhūmi*)," and so forth. This answers what is to be done.

The "Activity" (karma) refers precisely to the activity of transforming and delivering sentient beings. Below, the matter of transforming and delivering sentient beings is explained in detail through thirty-seven sections, divided into three parts.
The first part consists of sixteen lines of scripture concerning the vision of sentient beings who delight in and are attached to the lower realms;
it enumerates fifteen sections to clarify how one transforms and delivers sentient beings according to their needs through the ten perfections (pāramitās). The first five sections are as follows:
The first two [verses] clarify the perfections of giving and ethical discipline; the subsequent eight clarify the [remaining] eight perfections.

Next, from "If one sees sentient beings whose physical marks are incomplete" below, there are eleven and a half lines of scripture that enumerate twelve sections, clarifying how to transform sentient beings who lack merit so that they may attain the causal and resultant merits of Buddhahood and perceive the primary truth (*paramārtha*). Next, "if one sees sentient beings in whom greedy conduct predominates... [and so forth].

The following nine lines and a half of the sūtra enumerate ten gates, clarifying that one merely uses the gate of counteractive measures (*pratipakṣa*) to destroy the delusive obstructions of sentient beings.
This is intended to show that all aforementioned means of benefiting beings take the preceding twenty mental states as their initiating expedients;
thus, one is able to accomplish these activities of benefiting beings. Next, "I [use] these immeasurable gifts of Dharma (*dharma-dāna*) to gather in all..."
The section from "Sentient beings [enter] the three lower practices" concludes the intent of the transformation; seeing that things bring about benefit, they rejoice greatly.
This above has already answered the two questions regarding activity and skillful means, while within the conclusion it also explains the name "liberation.
Below, from "Furthermore, good son, I constantly observe," the answer to the question regarding observation begins. This consists of two sections; the first is "constantly observing."
In the section following "Examining All Bodhisattvas," there are ten lines and a half of sutra text. First, it describes observing the realm of the bodhisattvas;

next, from "I observe this assembly in the place of enlightenment and know the Buddha’s spiritual power" onwards, there are twenty-two lines of sutra text that specifically reveal the observation of the Buddha’s realm.
There are ten gates within what is observed, each of which gives rise to great joy. Because of this...
Because he has attained liberation, he gains the name "One of Vast Great Joy. Next, having seen this, great joy arises in every thought-moment;
the following six lines and a half of scripture summarize what was previously observed, all of which are designated as the nature of the *dharmadhātu*.

By means of the great wisdom capable of contemplation, one accords with the essence and characteristics of the *dharmadhātu*. Therefore, the joy and other qualities that arise are equal to all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*).
Furthermore, O son of good family, this "boundless liberation" answers the question regarding the objective sphere (*viṣaya*).

Above was the subject of contemplation; here, this objective sphere is the object of contemplation. There are two aspects to this objective sphere. If categorized according to the gate of entering the *dharmadhātu*:
This refers to the object of contemplation. If one gives rise to omniscience through the realization that "mind-only" is the ultimate limit of all objects, there are twenty-six lines of scripture.
The first seven and a half lines list ten categories of dharmas explained by way of direct teaching (*dharmadeśanā*).

Following the phrase "like a shadow," the subsequent nineteen lines of scripture list twenty-two categories explained by way of analogy (*upamāna*). At the end, the conclusion and exhortation state: "You should contemplate and accordingly awaken."

[The section on] "Entering. Having already answered the questions posed above, [the text] now exhorts practice. Next, at that time, the youth Sudhana addressed the Night Goddess Silent Sound (Śāntasvarā), asking:
"O Great Sage, how does one practice to attain this liberation? This question concerns the cause of liberation.
The Night Goddess answers that the cause consists in fully practicing the ten perfections (*daśapāramitā*). This is set forth in thirteen lines of scripture, each of which...
"It is called the Great Dharma-Treasury. This reveals that within each and every *pāramitā*, all myriad practices (*sahasra-caryā*) are contained.

Sudhana said, "Noble One, how long has it been since you first resolved your mind [for enlightenment]? This question concerns the duration of his initial resolve. Below, the causes and conditions for this resolve are fully described, stating:
"Within the ocean of worlds to the east of this Flower Treasury World System (*Kusumatalagarbhavyūha-lokadhātusea*), there is a world-lineage (*lokadhātu-jāti*)."
Within this world-system, there is a world named Pure Radiance Adorned with Gold.
In that world, in a remote past age, there was an eon named Universal Light Banner. Within that eon, there was a land named Universally Filled Wondrous Treasury.
In that land, there was a site of enlightenment named Wondrous Moonlight of All Jewel Treasuries. At that time,
There was a Buddha named Dharma-realm Non-retrogression Tathāgata who attained perfect enlightenment at this site of awakening.
At that time, I was a bodhi-tree deity guarding the site of awakening.
Seeing that Buddha resolve upon the mind of enlightenment, I immediately attained a samādhi called "Universally Illuminating the Ocean of the Tathāgata’s Merits. This is...
At the very beginning, when I first saw the Buddha and gave rise to the aspiration for enlightenment (*bodhicitta*), I immediately attained a samādhi;

this is the direct response to the question regarding the initial arousal of the mind. From that time onward, within this very site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), nine Buddhas appeared in succession in the world.
In the presence of each and every Buddha, I served and made offerings to them, heard their teachings, and in each case attained a specific kind of samādhi.
Since first generating this resolve, there have been fifty-two sūtras concerning his non-retrogressive practice that recount past events;
therein it says: "In this world-system called Pure Radiance Adorned with Gold, during the eon called Universal Radiant Banner."
There have been as many Tathāgatas appearing in the world as there are atoms in a Buddha-field; I have served them all.
These are merely nine Buddhas cited from among those as numerous as the atoms of a field.
Since the Buddhas whom I have served are already inconceivable, how could the samādhis I have attained possibly be conceived?
However, what has been described above refers exclusively to the world-system of Golden Adornment (*Suvarṇālaṃkāra*). There, he served Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field;
therefore, it is said that "having passed away from here, he was reborn in this very same world-system.

Having practiced the bodhisattva path for kalpas as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, this concluding statement points specifically to his conduct within the single world-system of Golden Adornment.
Furthermore, the following section describes practicing the bodhisattva path in this Sahā world.
It states that after his life there ends, he is reborn in this Sahā world within the Flower-Adorned World-Ocean.

Since the former [location] was merely a secondary land to the east of the Flower Treasury (Puṣpa-garbha), it is now specifically stated that he is "reborn in the Sahā world within the Flower Treasury Ocean. Thus, regarding his birth...
In this Sahā world, during the Bhadrakalpa, they have already encountered the three past Buddhas, Konāgamana and the others;
they served and made offerings to them all, heard their teachings, and each attained samādhi. Now, they have met my own teacher, Vairocana.
Having attained equal and perfect enlightenment and manifested great supernormal powers, I have obtained the liberation door named "The Birth of Vast and Great Joy Adornment.
This shows that while the previous passage through many Buddhas was the cultivation of causes, it is now that the fruit of liberation is accomplished;
only upon reaching this point is the name and essence of liberation fully revealed. The six lines of scripture above describe the present.
This explains the causes and conditions for attaining liberation. Below, the functional activity of liberation is explained in detail. It says:

"Having attained this liberation, one is able to enter the ocean of the established dharma-realms within as many Buddha-lands as there are atoms in ten unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields," and so forth.
This collectively reveals that the great function of liberation is boundless. There are thirty-six lines of scripture leading up to the passage: "I, at..."

In every thought-moment, they fully know and perceive it. Within this, there is revealed the great function of the infinitely profound and subtle *dharmadhātu*, layer upon layer and inexhaustibly inexhaustible, thereby manifesting the deep roots of this liberation; thus, its application is vast.
Following this, he concludes by saying: "Good son, as for your question regarding how long it has been since I first resolved my mind toward enlightenment, it is as I have explained above."
In the world-system Suvarṇālaṃkāra, beginning from the first arousal of the mind of enlightenment, he practiced the bodhisattva conduct for as many eons as there are atoms in two buddha-fields.
Only thereafter was he born within the Bhadrakalpa in this Sahā world, where he encountered three past Buddhas and finally my own Teacher;
from that point onward, throughout future eons, he has continued to practice the bodhisattva conduct.
All the Buddhas who exist therein, I have likewise served, approached, and made offerings to.

Because my resolve has been such that it does not regress throughout these long eons, I exhort Sudhana, saying: "You should single-mindedly cultivate this gate of great heroic vigor of the Bodhisattvas.
At that time, the night goddess Silent Sound Ocean further proclaimed the meaning of this liberation and spoke in verse:
There are ten verses spoken. The first verse exhorts one to practice; the next eight verses correctly clarify the past practices;
and the final verse concludes the scope of these practices. Having spoken these verses, he then humbly acknowledges his own limitations while extolling the excellence of others, saying:
"I know only this liberation door of the vast and joyful adornment that arises in every thought-moment. As for the Bodhisattvas who have deeply entered..."
They fully know all the enumerations of kalpas throughout the ocean of all dharma realms, and universally behold the formation and destruction of all lands.
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct? Pointing to a subsequent friend, she said:
"In this site of enlightenment, there is a night goddess named *Sarvanagararakṣāprabhāvavivardhanī*. You should go and ask her."
"I shall explain it for you. At that time, the youth Sudhana observed the night goddess Silent Ocean Sound with single-minded attention and spoke in verse.
He uttered ten stanzas praising the supreme benefits of the Dharma-door. Having spoken these verses, he gazed at her with earnest reverence, took his leave, and departed.
At that time, the youth Sudhana followed the instructions of the night goddess Silent Ocean Sound;
he contemplated and examined the dharma-gate she had taught, not forgetting a single word or phrase, regarding her immeasurable profound resolve and immeasurable nature of phenomena.

With all skillful means, supernatural powers, and wisdom, her mindfulness and contemplation continued in uninterrupted succession; her mind vast and expansive, she attained realization and dwelt therein.

She proceeded to the place where the night goddess who protects all cities was located, and saw that goddess seated upon a lion throne made of mani-jewel kings of universal precious light, surrounded by countless other night goddesses. She manifested—
The body of the physical form of all sentient beings; appearing as a body that universally faces all sentient beings;

appearing as a body unstained by any world; appearing as a body equal in number to all sentient beings; appearing as a body that transcends all worlds; appearing as a body that brings all sentient beings to maturity;
appearing as a body that swiftly reaches all ten directions; appearing as a body that universally encompasses all.
He manifested bodies throughout the ten directions: the ultimate body of the Tathāgata’s essential nature, and the ultimate body for the subduing of sentient beings.
Upon seeing this, Sudhana leaped for joy and prostrated at his feet, circumambulating him countless times.
Standing before him with palms joined, he spoke these words: "Noble One, I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet..."
"I do not yet know how a bodhisattva benefits sentient beings while practicing the bodhisattva path;
how they gather in sentient beings through the supreme gathering; how they accord with the teachings of all Buddhas; and how they draw near to the station of the Dharma King.
I only pray that you will take pity on me and explain this for me. Then that night goddess said to Sudhana, "Noble son, for the sake of protecting and rescuing..."
For the sake of all sentient beings; for the sake of adorning and purifying all Buddha-fields; for the sake of making offerings to all Tathāgatas;
because you wish to abide through all kalpas to rescue sentient beings; because you wish to protect the lineage of all Buddhas;
because you wish to universally enter the ten directions to cultivate all practices; because you wish to universally enter all dharmas.
Because you have entered the ocean of gates; because you desire to pervade all things with a mind of equanimity; because you desire to universally receive the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas;
because you desire to universally rain down the rain of Dharma according to the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings.
[He] asked about the gates of practice cultivated by the bodhisattvas. "Good son, I have attained the profound, sovereign, and wondrous voice of a bodhisattva."
They are liberated; they are great Dharma masters who are free from all obstructions, for they are skillfully able to reveal the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas.
They possess the power of great vows and great compassion, causing all sentient beings to abide in the bodhicitta.
They are able to perform all deeds that benefit sentient beings, accumulating roots of goodness without ceasing, and act as a tamer for all sentient beings.
He is the Teacher who guides all sentient beings so that they may abide in the path of *sarvajñatā* (omniscience).
He is the sun of pure Dharma for all the world, universally illuminating the world to cause the roots of goodness to arise.
His mind is impartial toward all worlds, universally causing sentient beings to increase in wholesome dharmas. His mind is pure regarding all objective spheres, eliminating and extinguishing...
Because of all unwholesome karmas; because of the vow to benefit all sentient beings by constantly manifesting their bodies universally in all lands;
because of manifesting all past events and causal conditions to cause all sentient beings to abide in wholesome conduct;
and because of constantly serving all spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) to cause sentient beings to abide in the Buddha’s teaching. O Son of the Buddha!
I bestow these dharmas as a gift of Dharma upon sentient beings, causing them to give rise to pure qualities (*śukladharma*) and seek all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*).

Their minds become firm and solid like the Vajra-Nārāyaṇa treasury; they are well able to discern the power of the Buddha and the power of Māra; they constantly draw near to virtuous friends (*kalyāṇamitra*);
they shatter the mountain of all karmic and afflictive obstructions; and they gather the dharmas that assist the path to all-knowledge.

The mind never abandons the ground of omniscience. Good son, when I benefit all sentient beings by means of such light of pure dharmas, gathering roots of goodness and the factors conducive to the path, I perform ten kinds of observations of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*).
What are these ten? They are: first, I know that the dharma-realm is immeasurable, because I have attained the vast light of wisdom. I...
I know the dharma-realm is boundless, for I see all that is known and seen by all Buddhas.
I know the dharma-realm is limitless, for I universally enter all Buddha-lands to reverently make offerings to all Tathāgatas.
I know the dharma-realm is shoreless, for I manifest the practice of bodhisattva conduct throughout the entire ocean of the dharma-realm. I know the dharma-realm...

I know that the realm is uninterrupted, for it enters into the Tathāgata’s uninterrupted wisdom; I know that the dharma-realm is of a single nature, for the Tathāgata’s single voice is such that no sentient being fails to understand it;
I know that the nature of the dharma-realm is pure, for I realize the Tathāgata’s vow to universally deliver all sentient beings;
I know that the dharma-realm pervades all sentient beings, for Samantabhadra’s wondrous practices completely encompass them all.
Because it is all-pervasive. I know the Dharma-realm because it is well-adorned by the sublime conduct of Samantabhadra, the single adornment.
I know the Dharma-realm because it is indestructible; the roots of goodness of omniscience fill the Dharma-realm and are themselves indestructible. Good son!

I performed these ten kinds of observations of the dharma-realm, accumulated all roots of goodness, perfected the factors conducive to enlightenment, understood the vast majesty and virtue of all Buddhas, and deeply entered the inconceivable realm of the Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, noble son, through such right mindfulness and reflection, I attained the ten kinds of great majestic dhāraṇī-wheels of the Tathāgata. What are these ten?
These are: the dhāraṇī-wheel of universally entering all phenomena; the dhāraṇī-wheel of universally upholding all phenomena;
the dhāraṇī-wheel of universally expounding all phenomena; and the dhāraṇī-wheel of universally recollecting all Buddhas of the ten directions.
The dhāraṇī-wheel that universally proclaims the names of all Buddhas; the dhāraṇī-wheel that universally enters the ocean of vows of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
the dhāraṇī-wheel that universally enters the ocean of all vehicles; the dhāraṇī-wheel that universally enters the ocean of the karma of all sentient beings;
the dhāraṇī-wheel that swiftly transforms all karma; and the swift generation of all-knowledge.
The Dhāraṇī Wheels. Good son, these ten dhāraṇī wheels have ten thousand dhāraṇī wheels as their retinue, and they constantly expound the sublime Dharma for the sake of sentient beings.
Good son, I may expound the Dharma of hearing-wisdom (*śrutamayī-prajñā*) for some sentient beings;
I may expound the Dharma of reflection-wisdom (*cintāmayī-prajñā*) for others; or I may expound the Dharma of cultivation-wisdom (*bhāvanāmayī-prajñā*) for others.
For some sentient beings, he teaches that there is one dharma; for others, he teaches that all dharmas exist.
For some, he teaches the dharma of the name-sea of a single Tathāgata; for others, he teaches the dharma of the name-seas of all Tathāgatas.
For some, he teaches the dharma of a single world-ocean; for others, he teaches the dharma of all world-oceans. Or he may teach the prophecy of a single Buddha.
The ocean-like Dharma; or for some, he expounds the ocean-like Dharma of the prophecies bestowed by all Buddhas;

or for some, he expounds the ocean-like Dharma of the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of a single Tathāgata; or for some, he expounds the ocean-like Dharma of the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas;
or for some, he expounds the ocean-like Dharma of the wheel of Dharma of a single Tathāgata; or for some, he expounds the ocean-like Dharma of the wheel of Dharma of all Tathāgatas; or for some...
He may preach the Dharma of a single Tathāgata sūtra; or he may preach the Dharma of the sūtras of all Tathāgatas.
Or he may preach the Dharma of the assembly of a single Tathāgata; or he may preach the Dharma of the assemblies of all Tathāgatas.
Or he may preach the Dharma of the ocean of the mind of a single sarvajñatā; or he may preach the Dharma of the oceans of the minds of all sarvajñatās. Or...
I preach the Dharma of liberation through the Single Vehicle for some, or I preach the Dharma of liberation through all vehicles for others.
Noble son, I preach such inexpressible gateways of the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings. Noble son, I have entered the ocean-like gateway of the Tathāgata’s non-differentiated Dharma-realm;
I preach the unsurpassed Dharma, universally gathering in all sentient beings, and shall remain thus throughout all future kalpas.
The Conduct of Samantabhadra. "Good son, I have accomplished this profound, sovereign, and wondrous-sounding liberation.
In every thought-moment, I increase all gates of liberation; in every thought-moment, I fill the entire Dharma-realm.
Then, the youth Sudhana said to the night goddess: "How marvelous, O goddess! This gate of liberation is so rare and extraordinary. Noble one..."

"How long has it been since you attained this realization? The night goddess replied, "Noble son, in the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in a world-system, there was an eon named Stainless Radiance.

There was a world named Cloud of Dharmadhātu Merits, which had as its substance an ocean of mani-jewel kings that manifested the karma of all sentient beings; it was shaped like a lotus and rested upon four [pillars]."

Within the networks of Mount Sumeru made of fragrant mani-jewels, as numerous as the atoms of the world-system, there is the adornment of lotus flowers that produce the sounds of the original vows of all Tathāgatas;
these are accompanied by a retinue of lotus flowers as numerous as the atoms within Mount Sumeru.
It was interspersed with fragrant maṇi jewels as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru. There were four-continent worlds (cāturdvīpaka) as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru;
in each four-continent world, there were hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of unspeakably unspeakable cities.
Good son, in that world there was a four-continent world named Wondrous Banner (Cāmaradhvaja), and within it was a king.

It was named Universal Jewel Flower Light. Not far from there was a site of enlightenment called the Palace of the Dharma King Universal Manifestation, wherein Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru appeared.
The first of those Buddhas was named Dharma Ocean Thunder Sound Radiance King. When that Buddha appeared in the world, there was a universal monarch named Pure Sun Radiance.

In the presence of that Buddha, he received and upheld the *Sarvadharma-sāgara-āvarta-sūtra*. After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, that king renounced the household life to protect and uphold the True Dharma.
When the Dharma was on the verge of extinction, there arose a thousand different schools and a thousand varieties of doctrinal teachings.
In the vicinity of the final eon, when the obstacles of karma and afflictions are heavy, many wicked bhikṣus will engage in much strife and contention.
Delighting in and clinging to sensory objects, they will not seek merit; instead, they will delight in discoursing on kings, thieves, women, nations, oceans, and all manner of worldly talk.
At that time, a king-like bhikṣu will say to them: "How strange! How tragic! The Buddha, throughout immeasurable [aeons]..."
"O you who have gathered here from oceans of great kalpas, why do you together seek to destroy this torch of Dharma?

Having spoken thus, he ascended into the air to a height of seven *tāla* trees. From his body issued immeasurable clouds of flames of various colors, emitting vast nets of light in manifold hues, causing immeasurable sentient beings to eliminate the heat of their afflictions and causing immeasurable sentient beings to give rise to [the resolve for awakening].
Through these causes and conditions, the teaching of that Tathāgata flourished once again for sixty-five thousand years.
At that time, there was a bhikṣuṇī named Dharmacakra-vibhūti-prabhā, who was the daughter of this king.

Surrounded by a retinue of hundreds of thousands of bhikṣuṇīs, she heard the words of her father, the king, and witnessed his supernormal powers; she then gave rise to the bodhicitta, never to regress.
He regressed and attained a samādhi named "Lamp of All Buddha Teachings. Furthermore, he attained this profound, sovereign, and wondrous-sounding liberation.
Having attained it, his body and mind became supple and soft, and he immediately beheld with his own eyes all the spiritual powers of the Tathāgata Dharma-Sea Thunder-Voice Radiance King.
"Good son, what do you think? At that time, the Wheel-Turning Sage King..."
When the Tathāgata turned the wheel of the true Dharma, and those who caused the Dharma to flourish during the final age after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa—who could they have been other than these?
The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra is he now; the bhikṣuṇī Dharmacakrapravartinābhāsa was none other than myself.
At that time, I protected the Buddha-dharma and enabled one hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs to [attain] anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
They attain non-retrogression from enlightenment. Furthermore, they cause them to attain the samādhi of directly beholding all Buddhas.
Furthermore, they cause them to attain the *vajra-light dhāraṇī* of the wheel of Dharma of all Buddhas.
