Entering the prison, he witnessed all manner of sufferings endured by the offenders. Compassion arose in the Prince’s heart, and desiring to rescue and pardon them, he immediately addressed the King, saying, "The suffering and torment of the offenders within the prison are unbearable; I pray that Your Majesty will grant them clemency.
The King then assembled five hundred ministers to deliberate upon the matter. All the ministers unanimously declared it was impossible. At that time, the Prince was filled with sorrow...
His heart was deeply moved; he wished to sacrifice his own body to take the place of the suffering of the imprisoned multitude.
At that time, the ministers together addressed the king, saying, "The Crown Prince acts contrary to the law. If you do not punish him, Your Majesty’s precious throne will not endure for long.
Upon hearing this, the king was filled with a towering rage and desired to execute the prince. When the queen learned of this, she wailed in grief and lamentation, disfiguring her appearance.
He was subdued. He went to rescue the crown prince. The king commanded the prince, "If you rescue this criminal, I shall surely put you to death.
The prince’s compassionate heart was firm and resolute; he was determined to save him and was willing to accept execution himself. The king would certainly not grant him clemency.
At that time, the queen interceded for the prince, requesting a grace of half a month, so that he might practice giving before his execution. The king likewise...
It was granted. At that time, to the north of the capital city, there was a great park named Sūryaprabha (Sunlight).
The Prince went there and established a great assembly for giving, providing all manner of necessities; whatever was requested, nothing was not fully supplied.
This passage, consisting of thirty-one lines of scripture, recounts in detail the beginning of the Night Goddess’s initial generation of the mind of enlightenment (*cittotpāda*) in a former life.
The first part concerns the past life story (*pūrvayoga*) of the Night Goddess when she had not yet renounced the world;

the second part recounts how that Buddha personally saved the Prince. After half a month had passed and the date for his execution was approaching, the Buddha Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganapradīparāja arrived at that assembly accompanied by the eight classes of beings. When the Prince saw him from afar, his heart was filled with great joy.

The Buddha was delighted. He had a seat prepared and sat upon it. For them, he preached a sūtra titled *The Universal Illumination Wheel of Causes*, enabling all sentient beings to understand it according to their respective capacities.
They were distanced from dust and freed from defilement, attaining the purity of the Dharma-eye.
At that time, Prince Subduer immediately attained the Bodhisattva liberation of teaching and transforming sentient beings to cause them to give rise to roots of goodness.
Section. The twenty-two lines of scripture above this describe the practices cultivated by the Night Goddess in her former life as a householder;
this is the direct answer to the question regarding the duration since she first resolved upon enlightenment (*bodhicitta*). Below, the past and present are identified:
"That prince was none other than my own self; those five hundred ministers were the present Devadatta and his four companions."
The hundred followers who sided with him were none other than the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa, such as Krakucchanda and the rest.
The King Prasenajit of that time was none other than the great master of debate, the Nirgrantha Śāṭhyāyana, of the present day.
All these individuals mentioned above shall each attain Buddhahood in the future, though their names will differ. There are two concluding paragraphs summarizing this assembly.
The *Dvādaśamukha-sūtra*. The preceding section narrates the night goddess’s conduct while she was a householder; the following section narrates her conduct after she left the household life.
It says: "O Son of the Buddha, at that time, after I had saved those whose transgressions were to be purified, my parents permitted me to abandon my kingdom, wife, and children.
I then went forth from home to study the Way under the Buddha Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganapradīparāja."
For five hundred years, he purely cultivated the Brahma-faring (brahmacarya). He immediately attained one million dharani-doors and other such Dharma-gates.

The conclusion states: "He understood them all clearly. There are eleven lines of scripture. Next, it clarifies his subsequent rebirth, his meeting with a Buddha, and his cultivation of causes, saying:
"At that time, after my life ended, I was once again born into that royal family as a wheel-turning [monarch]."
O King, within the single eon known as *Sūryaprabha* in the world-system *Ratnaprabhā*, he successively encountered ten thousand Buddhas;
to mention them briefly, there were eight such Buddhas. Subsequently, in the second eon named *Sūryaprabha*, sixty billion Buddhas appeared in succession, all of whom he served and attended.
At the site of each and every Buddha, he further attained immeasurable liberations (*vimokṣa*).

[Up to this point] is the section on skillful means (*upāya*). The above passage recounts the Buddhas he took as teachers since his renunciation of the world; it consists of thirty lines of scripture.
It chronicles which Buddhas he served and what kind of bodies they assumed, noting that none of these encounters were ever in vain.

This is why [this teaching] is so profound and difficult to explain, for it is not a realm that can be measured by the intellect or consciousness. At that time, the Lord who Protects All Sentient Beings...
O Night Goddess, wishing to further proclaim the meaning of this liberation, he spoke in verse:

"Since you have asked about this inconceivable dharma of liberation with a heart of joy, faith, and delight, I, relying on the power of the Tathāgata’s protective mindfulness, shall proclaim it for you;
you should listen and receive it. There are thirty-four verses. The first verse permits the teaching; the following two verses [elaborate upon]...
The ancient Buddhas appeared in the world. The next one and a half verses praise the governance and transformation of the former king.
The section beginning with "The crown prince" praises the night goddess’s cultivation of causes. The first nine and a half verses praise her past life as a householder;

the next verse praises her renunciation and attainment of the Dharma; the following two verses praise ten thousand Buddhas; and thereafter, below the phrase "as many as the atoms of a Buddha-field," there are ten [verses].

Seven verses summarize the attainment of the Dharma regarding time and place. Because liberation is profound, vast, and difficult to know, these verses are repeated here to demonstrate the sense of earnestness.
Having fully answered the causes and conditions of the gateway to the Dharma of liberation, he then humbly acknowledges his own limitations while extolling the excellence [of others], saying:
"I know only this gateway to liberation for teaching and transforming sentient beings so that they may give rise to roots of goodness."

Thus it is. As for those bodhisattvas who transcend all worlds and manifest bodies in all realms of existence, even unto their universal entry into the ocean of all forms of speech—how could I possibly know or describe them? Then, pointing to a companion behind him, he said:
"In this Jambudvīpa, there is a grove named Lumbinī. In that grove, there is a deity named Guṇakāraṇḍavyūhā."
"You may go and ask him; he will explain it for you. Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, joined his palms in reverence, gazed up at him, and took his leave to depart.
Essential Summary of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha,
Volumes 73 and 74. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda, a śramaṇa from the Kingdom of Khotan.
Commentary by the Śramaṇa Chengguan of Qingliangshan Dàhuá-yán Monastery;
Excerpts by the Śramaṇa Hanshan Deqing of Fáyún Monastery on Kuāngshān, clarifying the meaning.
Chapter Thirty-nine, Part Fifteen: Entering the Dharmadhātu.
At that time, after the youth Sudhana had attained the bodhisattva liberation from the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā,
he recollected, cultivated, mastered, and increased it. Proceeding by stages,
he arrived at the Lumbinī grove and searched everywhere for the goddess Viśeṣamati, whom he saw there amidst the adornments of all kinds of jewel trees.
Within the pavilion, he sat upon a lion throne of precious lotuses, surrounded with reverence by twenty billion nayutas of devas.
He was preaching the *Sūtra on the Ocean of Bodhisattva Births*, causing them all to be born into the family of the Tathāgata and to increase the great ocean of a bodhisattva’s merit.
Having seen this, Sudhana prostrated at his feet, stood before him with palms joined, and said:

He said, "O Great Sage, I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should cultivate the bodhisattva practices to be born into the family of the Tathāgata and become a great light for the world.
That deity replied, "Good son, there are ten kinds of treasuries of birth for bodhisattvas. If a bodhisattva accomplishes these dharmas, then..."

Born into the family of the Tathāgatas, they cause the roots of goodness of a bodhisattva to increase in every thought-moment. Without weariness, without indolence, without aversion, and without retreat, they are uninterrupted and unerring.
Free from all delusions, they do not give rise to thoughts of cowardice, inferiority, affliction, or regret.
They advance toward omniscience, enter the gates of the Dharma-realm, resolve upon the vast mind, increase the perfections, and accomplish the unsurpassed enlightenment of all Buddhas.
Having abandoned the worldly realms and entered the stage of the Tathāgata, they attain supreme supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
The teachings of all Buddhas are ever present before them, and they accord with the objective realm of the true meaning of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*). What are these ten?

First, the treasury of birth through the vow to constantly make offerings to all Buddhas; second, the treasury of birth through the arousal of the bodhicitta; third, the contemplation of all dharma-gates.
1. The treasury of birth through diligent practice; 2. The treasury of birth through universally illuminating the three periods of time with a profound and pure mind;

3. The treasury of birth through impartial radiance; 4. The treasury of birth through being born into the family of the Tathāgatas; 5. The treasury of birth through the radiance of the Buddha’s power; 6.
The treasury of birth through contemplating the gateway of universal wisdom; 7. The treasury of birth through universally manifesting adornments.
The Treasury of Rebirth through Rigorous Acceptance. Tenth is the Treasury of Rebirth upon Entering the Stage of the Tathāgata.
Good son, what is called the Treasury of Rebirth through the Vow to Constantly Make Offerings to All Buddhas? Good son, when a bodhisattva first resolves their mind, they make this vow:
"I shall respect, revere, and make offerings to all Buddhas; I shall never grow weary of seeing the Buddhas. Regarding all...
He constantly gives rise to love and joy for the Buddhas; he always arouses deep faith and cultivates all merits without ever ceasing.
This is called the "Womb of Rebirth" where a Bodhisattva first gathers roots of goodness for the sake of omniscience.
What is meant by the "Womb of Rebirth" through the arousal of the bodhicitta? Good son, this Bodhisattva arouses the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

That is to say: giving rise to the mind of great compassion in order to rescue and protect all sentient beings; giving rise to the mind of making offerings to the Buddha in order to serve him to the ultimate end;
giving rise to the mind of universally seeking the true Dharma without any stinginess; giving rise to the mind of vast aspiration in order to seek all-knowledge;
giving rise to the immeasurable mind of loving-kindness in order to universally gather in all sentient beings; and giving rise to the mind of never abandoning anyone.

The minds of sentient beings: because they are clad in the firm armor of the vow to seek all-knowledge; because they give rise to a mind free from flattery and deception, thereby attaining knowledge as it truly is;

because they give rise to a mind that acts according to their words, cultivating the bodhisattva path; because they give rise to a mind that does not deceive the Buddhas, guarding the great vows of all Buddhas;
and because they give rise to the mind of the vow for all-knowledge, transforming sentient beings until the end of the future.
Because of this rest, the bodhisattva, by virtue of such merits of the bodhicitta as are equal in number to the atoms within a buddha-field, is born into the family of the Tathāgata.

This is the second treasury of birth for a bodhisattva. What is called the treasury of birth through diligent practice in the gate of contemplating all dharmas? Son of good family, this bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to the contemplation of all...
The ocean-heart of the Dharma-gates; the mind that gives rise to the path of perfecting omniscience through dedication; the mind that gives rise to right mindfulness free from error or negligence;
the mind that gives rise to the purity of the ocean of all bodhisattva samādhis; the mind that gives rise to the cultivation and accomplishment of all bodhisattva merits;
the mind that gives rise to the adornment of all bodhisattva paths; and the great diligence that gives rise to the quest for omniscience.
To practice all meritorious virtues with a mind like the blazing fires at the end of an eon that never ceases;
to give rise to the mind of practicing the conduct of Samantabhadra to teach and transform all sentient beings;

and to give rise to the true mind of skillfully learning all dignified deportments, cultivating the merits of a bodhisattva, relinquishing all possessions, and abiding in non-possession—this is the third treasury of birth for a bodhisattva.
What is called the "Treasury of Rebirth Illuminating the Three Times with a Profound and Pure Mind"?

Good son, this bodhisattva possesses a pure and superior mind (*adhyāśaya*) and attains the light of the Tathāgata’s enlightenment. Entering the ocean of a bodhisattva’s skillful means (*upāya*), their mind is as firm and solid as a vajra.
Turning their back on all rebirths within the realms of existence, they accomplish all the self-natures of the Buddhas.

Abiding in power, they cultivate sublime practices and possess the faculties of a bodhisattva. Their minds are clear and pure, their vow-power is unshakable, and they are constantly protected and remembered by all Buddhas.
They shatter all mountains of obstacles and serve as a place of reliance for all sentient beings.
This is the fourth treasury of the bodhisattva’s birth. What is meant by "birth through the light of equality"?
"Good son, this bodhisattva is fully endowed with all practices and universally transforms sentient beings. He is able to relinquish everything he possesses.
Abiding in the realm of the Buddha’s ultimate pure precepts, he is fully endowed with the dharma of patience and achieves the light of the dharmas of patience of all Buddhas.
Through great diligence, he advances toward omniscience and reaches the other shore. He cultivates and practices the various meditative concentrations..."
The Samādhi of the Universal Gate. With pure wisdom perfected, one illuminates all phenomena with the brilliance of the sun of wisdom.
Attaining the unobstructed eye, one beholds the ocean of all Buddhas and awakens to and enters the true nature of all dharmas. All those in the world who see this rejoice;
they are well able to practice the Dharma-gate of reality as it is. This is the fifth treasury of the Bodhisattva’s birth. What is meant by "birth"?
The Matrix of Birth in the Family of the Tathāgatas. Good son, this bodhisattva is born into the family of the Tathāgatas and dwells in accordance with all Buddhas.
He accomplishes all profound dharma-gates and possesses the pure great vows of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
He attains the same roots of goodness as all Buddhas and shares a single essential nature with all Tathāgatas. He is endowed with supramundane conduct and pure, wholesome dharmas.
They dwell securely in the dharma-gate of vast merit. Entering into various samādhis, they behold the spiritual power of the Buddhas.
According to those who require transformation, they purify all sentient beings. Their responses to questions are inexhaustible in eloquence. This is the sixth treasury of birth for Bodhisattvas.
What is called the treasury of birth of the light of the Buddha’s powers? Good son, this Bodhisattva enters deeply into the Buddha...
They travel through all Buddha-fields with power, their minds never regressing. They serve and attend upon the assemblies of Bodhisattvas without weariness or fatigue.
They understand that all phenomena arise like illusions; they know all worlds to be like things seen in a dream; they perceive all forms and appearances as being like light and shadows;
they recognize all manifestations of supernatural powers as being like transformations; and they understand all modes of birth to be entirely like...
The teachings of all Buddhas that they manifest are like echoes in a valley; they reveal the Dharma-realm so that all may reach ultimate realization.
This is the seventh treasury of birth of a bodhisattva. What is called the treasury of birth through contemplating the gateway to universal wisdom?
Noble son, this bodhisattva dwells in the stage of youthful truth and contemplates all-knowledge, expounding each individual gateway of wisdom throughout the exhaustion of immeasurable eons.
They practice all that is undertaken by bodhisattvas; they attain mastery of mind within the profound samādhis of all bodhisattvas;
in every thought-moment, they appear before the Tathāgatas in the worlds of the ten directions; and regarding differentiated objects, they enter non-differentiated meditative concentration.
To possess the wisdom that perceives distinctions within the undifferentiated Dharma; to know that there is no objective realm within immeasurable objects;
to enter immeasurable realms from within a limited realm; to penetrate the vast and boundless nature of phenomena (dharmatā);
and to know that all worlds are merely provisional designations, all of which arise from the consciousness-mind—this is the eighth treasury of birth for Bodhisattvas. What do you say?
"What is meant by the 'Treasury of Universal Manifestation of Adorned Rebirths'? Good son, this bodhisattva is able to adorn immeasurable buddha-fields in various ways;
they are universally able to manifest the bodies of all sentient beings as well as the bodies of all Buddhas, and have attained fearlessness."
They manifest the pure Dharma, circulating throughout the Dharma-realm without obstruction. According to the inclinations of beings' minds, they cause them all to know and see;
they manifest various practices for attaining Bodhi, causing them to give rise to the path of unimpeded omniscience.
Such deeds are performed without missing their proper time, while they constantly abide in the samādhi of Vairocana’s treasury of wisdom. This is called Bodhi.
The Ninth Treasury of Rebirth of the Bodhisattva. What is called the Treasury of Rebirth upon Entering the Stage of the Tathāgata?
Good son, this bodhisattva receives the dharma of consecration from all the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time and universally knows the sequence of all realms.
That is to say, he knows the sequence of the deaths and births of all sentient beings throughout their past and future limits, as well as all aspects of the bodhi...
He knows the sequence of the Bodhisattva’s practice; the sequence of the mental activities of all sentient beings; the sequence of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time attaining Buddhahood;

and the sequence of skillful means in preaching the Dharma. He also knows the sequence of names and the order of all kalpas—whether of formation or destruction—throughout the past, present, and future limits.
According to what each sentient being should be transformed and delivered, he manifests the attainment of enlightenment for them.
The adornment of the path’s merit, the teaching of the Dharma through supernormal powers, and the taming of beings through skillful means—this is the tenth treasury of the bodhisattva’s birth.

O Son of the Buddha, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates, increases, perfects, and accomplishes these ten dharmas, they will be able to manifest all manner of adornments within a single adornment; such is the adornment of all things.
They guide, instruct, and awaken all sentient beings throughout the lands, without ceasing until the end of all future kalpas.
They expound the ocean of all Buddha-dharmas, with their various realms and various modes of maturation.
Transmitting immeasurable dharmas from one to another, they manifest the inconceivable sovereign power of the Buddhas, filling all of space and the Dharma-realm. Regarding all...
They turn the wheel of Dharma within the ocean of the mental activities of sentient beings. They manifest the attainment of Buddhahood in all worlds without interruption.
They expound all dharmas with ineffable, pure sounds and voices. Abiding in immeasurable places, they attain unimpeded penetration.
Adorning the site of enlightenment with all dharmas, they [act] according to the differences in the inclinations and understandings of sentient beings.
He has manifested as a Buddha and revealed the immeasurable, profound treasury of the Dharma, teaching and bringing all worlds to maturity.
At that time, the forest deity of Lumbinī, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, surveyed the ten directions through the Buddha’s spiritual power and spoke these verses:
With a supreme, stainless, and pure mind, never weary of beholding all Buddhas,
they vow to constantly make offerings throughout the future; this is the treasury of birth for those of clear wisdom,
wherein they appear among all sentient beings and all Buddhas within the lands of the three periods of time.
May all beings vow to deliver them and constantly attend upon this inconceivable one;
This is the treasury of the birth of those who hear the Dharma without weariness and delight in contemplation, Who are universally unimpeded throughout the three periods of time,
And whose body and mind are pure like space— this is the treasury of the birth of those renowned for their fame.
His mind dwells perpetually within the ocean of great compassion, as firm as a diamond or a mountain of jewels;
having thoroughly mastered the gateway to all modes of omniscience, this most excellent one possesses the treasury of rebirth.
His great loving-kindness universally covers all beings, and his sublime conduct constantly increases the ocean of the perfections.
Illuminating all classes of beings with the light of the Dharma— this is the treasury of birth of those who are courageous,
who thoroughly understand the nature of phenomena with unimpeded minds; born into the family of the Buddhas of the three periods of time,
they universally enter the ocean of the dharma-realm of the ten directions— this is the treasury of birth of those of brilliant wisdom.
The Dharma-body is pure and the mind is unimpeded; Universally visiting all lands throughout the ten directions, There is no power of any Buddha that is not accomplished.
This inconceivable treasury of birth, Having entered deep wisdom, is already sovereign; It is also ultimate within all samādhis.
The gateway for contemplating all-knowledge as it truly is; this treasury of the birth of the True Body purifies all Buddha-lands.
Diligently practicing the methods for universally transforming sentient beings, he manifests the sovereign power of the Tathāgata.
This treasury of the birth of the one of Great Name— The treasury of the birth of the one of Great Name.
Having long practiced for omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), they are swiftly able to enter the stage of the Tathāgata;
understanding that the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) is entirely unimpeded—these sons of the Buddhas possess this treasury of birth.
Good son, when bodhisattvas are endowed with these ten dharmas, they are born into the family of the Tathāgatas and become pure for all the world.
"Radiance. Good son, since immeasurable eons ago, I have attained this liberation door of sovereign birth.
Sudhana said, 'Noble one, what is the scope of this liberation door? He replied, 'Good son, I first made this vow:
"May I draw near to all Bodhisattvas at the time they manifest their births. I vowed to enter the Vairocana..."

The Tathāgata Vairocana’s ocean of immeasurable births, through the power of his former vows, was born in this world within the Lumbinī Grove in Jambudvīpa, single-mindedly mindful of when the Bodhisattva would descend to be born.
After a hundred years had passed, the World-Honored One indeed descended from Tuṣita Heaven and was born here. At that time, ten kinds of signs appeared within this grove. What are they?
Tenth: First, the ground within this garden suddenly becomes level of its own accord; all pits, hollows, mounds, and hills completely disappear.
Second, the ground is made of diamond and adorned with various jewels, free from tiles, rubble, thorns, and stumps.
Third, rows of precious *tāla* trees stand in circumference, their roots firmly planted down to the water’s edge. Fourth, they produce manifold fragrances.
The sprouts manifest treasuries of manifold fragrances; precious incense forms trees that provide lush shade and reflection. All these fragrances surpass those of the heavens.
Fifth, various exquisite flower garlands and precious ornaments are arranged in rows and distributed everywhere, filling the space.
Sixth, all the trees within the garden naturally blossom with *maṇi* jewel flowers. Seventh, all...
Within the ponds, lotuses sprang up spontaneously; they emerged from the ground and spread across the surface of the water.

Eighth, at that time, all the kings of the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and all others dwelling in the desire and form realms of this Sahā world came together to assemble in this grove, joining their palms in reverence.
9. Furthermore, all the celestial maidens in this world, down to the *mahoraga* maidens, were filled with joy;
each holding various articles of offering, they stood respectfully before the *piplakṣa* tree.
Tenth, from the navels of all Buddhas of the ten directions, light rays were emitted, called the "Lamp of Sovereignty over the Birth of Bodhisattvas.

These illuminated this grove everywhere. Within each ray of light, there appeared all the miraculous manifestations of the Buddhas' births and all the meritorious qualities of the births of all bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, various voices and sounds of the Buddhas issued forth. This is...
There were ten kinds of auspicious omens in the grove. When these signs appeared, the celestial kings and others immediately knew that a Bodhisattva was about to descend to be born.

Seeing these omens, I rejoiced immeasurably. Son of good family, when Lady Māyā departed from the city of Kapilavastu and entered this grove, ten further kinds of radiant auspicious signs appeared, causing all sentient beings to obtain [benefit].
The Light of the Dharma. What are the ten? They are: the light of the treasury of all jewel-flowers; the light of the treasury of precious incense;

the light that issues forth the true and wondrous sounds from the blossoming of precious lotuses; the light of the bodhisattvas of the ten directions who have first resolved their minds on enlightenment;

the light of the bodhisattvas who have attained entry into the various stages (*bhūmi*) and manifest spiritual transformations; and the light of the bodhisattvas who cultivate the perfections (*pāramitā*) to completion.
The light of perfected wisdom; the light of the wisdom of all bodhisattvas’ great vows; the light of the wisdom of all bodhisattvas’ skillful means for teaching and transforming sentient beings;
the light of the wisdom of all bodhisattvas realizing the true reality of the dharma-realm;

and the light of all bodhisattvas attaining the sovereign power of a Buddha, being born, renouncing the world, and attaining perfect enlightenment—these ten lights universally illuminate immeasurable worlds.

The Minds of Sentient Beings. "Good son, when Lady Māyā sat beneath the Pāṭala tree, ten kinds of divine transformations were further manifested as the Bodhisattva was about to be born. What are these ten?
Good son, at the time when the Bodhisattva was about to be born, the sons and daughters of the gods from all the heavens of the desire realm, as well as all those of the form realm..."

The devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and their retinues all gathered like clouds for the sake of making offerings. The majesty and virtue of Lady Māyā were exceptionally sublime;
from every pore of her body she emitted radiance that universally illuminated the trichiliocosm without obstruction.
All obstructions were removed, and all radiance was made manifest. He extinguished the afflictions of all sentient beings and the sufferings of the evil realms;
this was the first supernatural transformation of the Bodhisattva as he was about to be born.
Furthermore, noble son, at that time, within the womb of Lady Māyā, all the forms and images of the three thousandfold world system appeared in their entirety—those hundreds of millions...
Within Jambudvīpa, there were various capitals and cities, each with its own gardens and groves of differing names;
in all of them dwelt Lady Māyā, surrounded by hosts of devas, who manifested the inconceivable signs of supernatural power portending the Bodhisattva’s imminent birth.
This was the second miraculous manifestation of the Bodhisattva as he was about to be born. Furthermore, [it was] excellent...

O son of noble family, within every pore of Lady Māyā appeared all the Buddhas whom the Tathāgata had reverently honored and made offerings to while practicing the bodhisattva path in the past, as well as the sounds of those Buddhas preaching the Dharma.
It was, for example, like the images of the sun, moon, stars, clouds, and thunder appearing in a bright mirror or in water. Lady Māyā—
The pores of Queen Māyā’s body were likewise thus; they were able to manifest the Tathāgata’s past causes and conditions.

This was the third miraculous manifestation of the Bodhisattva as he was about to be born. Furthermore, noble son, within each and every pore of Queen Māyā’s body, there appeared the worlds, cities, and towns where the Tathāgata had resided while practicing the bodhisattva path in the past.
In villages, mountain forests, rivers, and oceans; throughout the kalpas of sentient beings; upon encountering a Buddha’s appearance in the world; entering pure lands;
according to their births and the length of their lifespans; and relying on spiritual friends to practice wholesome dharmas—in every land and in every place of birth, Māyādevī is always their mother.
All such things as these are contained within a single pore, without exception.
All these were manifested. This was the fourth supernormal transformation of the Bodhisattva as he was about to be born.

Furthermore, noble son, within each and every pore of Lady Māyā appeared clearly and distinctly all the colors, features, physical forms, clothing, food and drink, and experiences of pleasure and pain associated with the places where the Tathāgata had been born during his past cultivation of the bodhisattva path.
This was clearly discerned. This constitutes the fifth miraculous manifestation of the Bodhisattva as he was about to be born.

Furthermore, noble son, from every single pore of Queen Māyā’s body, there appeared all those things the World-Honored One had renounced in the past while practicing the perfection of giving—his head, eyes, ears, nose, lips, tongue, teeth, and gums;
his body, hands, feet, blood, flesh, tendons, and bones; and [the bodies of] men and women.

He also saw his wives, concubines, cities, palaces, clothing, necklaces, gold, silver, and precious treasures—all such internal and external objects—as well as the physical appearance, voices, and locations of those who received them;
this was the sixth supernormal transformation of the Bodhisattva just prior to his birth. Furthermore, noble son, when Lady Māyā entered this grove, its trees...

He universally manifests all the Buddhas of the past as they enter their mothers' wombs, including the lands, groves, garments, flower garlands, ointments, powdered incense, banners, silken streamers, flags, and canopies; all manner of adornments made of various jewels;
and the exquisite sounds of music, song, and chant, so that all sentient beings may everywhere see and hear them. This is the Bodhisattva’s imminent birth.
The seventh supernatural manifestation occurred at the time of birth. Furthermore, noble son, when Queen Māyā entered this grove,
there issued forth from her body the palace towers and pavilions made of the king of *maṇi* jewels where the Bodhisattva dwells—
surpassing all those of the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others.
The dwelling place of the King of Men was covered above with jeweled nets, universally draped with exquisite fragrances, and adorned with various treasures.
It was pure both inside and out, each section distinct and not intermingled, completely filling the Lumbinī Grove.
This was the eighth miraculous manifestation when the Bodhisattva was about to be born. Furthermore, noble son, Queen Māyā entered this [grove]...
At that time, from his body there emerged bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of buddha-fields.

The physical forms, features, marks, radiance, deportment, majestic bearing, spiritual powers, and retinues of all those bodhisattvas were entirely equal to those of the Bodhisattva Vairocana, without any difference. They all simultaneously offered praise.
They praised the Tathāgata. This was the ninth miraculous manifestation when the Bodhisattva was about to be born.

Furthermore, noble son, at the time when Queen Māyā was about to give birth to the Bodhisattva, suddenly a great lotus flower named Sarvaratnavyūhagarbha emerged before her from the Diamond Foundation (vajrapratiṣṭhāna). It had a diamond stem and filaments made of various jewels. Just as...
The King of Mind-Jewels serves as its terrace. It has as many petals as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields, all of which are composed of mani-jewels.
Jeweled nets and jeweled canopies cover it from above. All the celestial kings together uphold it;
all the dragon kings pour down rain of incense; and all the yakṣa kings respectfully surround it, scattering various heavenly flowers.
All the gandharva kings produced subtle and wondrous sounds, singing praises of the Bodhisattva’s past meritorious deeds of making offerings to the Buddhas.
All the asura kings cast aside their arrogant minds and prostrated themselves in reverent salutation.
All the garuḍa kings hung down jeweled silken banners that filled the void of space. All the kiṃnara kings gazed upon him with joy.

They sang praises and extolled the virtues of the Bodhisattva. All the kings of the mahoragas were filled with joy, singing and praising him, while they universally rained down clouds of all manner of jewel-adornments. This was the tenth miraculous manifestation when the Bodhisattva was about to be born.
Son of good family, after these ten kinds of signs had been displayed in the Lumbinī Grove, he then...
The birth of the Bodhisattva’s body was like the appearance of a pure solar disc in the void of space; like the emergence of auspicious clouds from the summit of a high mountain;
like the flashing of lightning amidst dense clouds; like the kindling of a great torch in the darkness of night.
At that time, the radiance of the Bodhisattva’s physical marks as he was born from his mother’s side was likewise so. Good son, the Bodhisattva at that time—
Although at that time he manifested his initial birth, he had already fully realized that all phenomena are like dreams and illusions,
like shadows and reflections, neither coming nor going, neither arising nor ceasing. Good son,
when I saw the Buddha manifest various miraculous transformations upon his initial birth in the Lumbinī Grove within Jambudvīpa of these four continents, I also saw—
The Tathāgata manifested various miraculous transformations at his initial birth within the Lumbinī Grove in Jambudvīpa, among the ten billion sets of four continents within the trichiliocosm.
He also saw immeasurable Buddha-fields within every single atom of the trichiliocosm, and he saw hundreds of Buddha-worlds, thousands of Buddha-worlds, and even up to ten...
Throughout every world, within each and every atom, there are immeasurable Buddha-fields.
Within all such Buddha-fields, Tathāgatas manifest birth and various miraculous transformations. In this manner, they continue constantly and without interruption from moment to moment.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to that goddess: "O Great Goddess, how long has it been since you attained this liberation?"
He replied, "Good son, in the distant past, beyond kalpas as numerous as the atoms in a billion buddha-fields, and even more than that number, there was a world named Universal Jewel.
The kalpa was named Joyful Delight. Within it, eighty nayutas of buddhas appeared.
The first of those buddhas was named Sovereign Merit Banner, fully endowed with the ten titles. In that world..."
Within it is a set of four continents named Wondrous Light Adornment.
In Jambudvīpa among those four continents, there is a royal capital named Sumeru Adornment Banner. Therein dwells a king named Jewel Flame Eye, whose queen is named Joyful Light.
Noble son, just as Queen Māyā was for Vairocana in this world, [so too was she for him].
The mother of the Tathāgata was likewise so; in that world, Lady Joyful Light (*Priyaprabhā*) was the mother of the first Buddha.
Good son, when Lady Joyful Light was about to give birth to the Bodhisattva, she went with twenty billion *nayuta* of female attendants to the Golden Flower Garden (*Suvarṇapuṣpa-udyāna*).
Within the garden was a pavilion named Peak of Wondrous Jewels (*Ratnakūṭa*), and beside it...
There was a tree named Sarvārthasiddha. Lady Priyadarśanā grasped a branch of that tree and gave birth to the Bodhisattva.
The hosts of deva kings each held fragrant water and together bathed him. At that time, there was a wet nurse named Viśuddhaprabhā who stood in attendance by his side.
Once he had been bathed, the hosts of deva kings handed him to the wet nurse; the wet nurse received him with reverence and felt great joy.
He rejoiced and immediately attained the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Universal Eye. Having attained this samādhi, he saw throughout the ten directions immeasurable Buddhas.
He further attained the Bodhisattva liberation of sovereign manifestation of birth in all places, which is as swift and unimpeded as the initial consciousness at conception.
By virtue of attaining this liberation, he beheld all Buddhas through the power of their original vows.
Mastery over birth is likewise so. Good son, what do you think? Was that wet nurse anyone else?

It was I myself. From that time onward, in every thought-moment, I have constantly seen Vairocana Buddha manifesting the ocean of births of bodhisattvas and his sovereign spiritual powers for the sake of taming sentient beings, just as I see Vairocana now.

By the power of the original vows of the Vairocana Buddha Vehicle, in every thought-moment, within the atoms of this trichiliocosm and even throughout all worlds in the ten directions, he manifests the miraculous transformations of a Bodhisattva’s birth.
Seeing that all Buddhas are likewise so, I reverently serve and make offerings to them all, listen to the Dharma they teach, and practice according to those teachings. At that time—
The forest goddess of Lumbinī, wishing to restate the meaning of this liberation, received the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions,
and spoke in verse: “O Son of the Buddha,
regarding that which you have asked— the profound realm of all Buddhas— you should now listen and receive it.”
I shall explain its causes and conditions: Past eons as numerous as the atoms in billions of lands, There was an eon named Joyful Eighty-Nayuta, In which a Tathāgata appeared in the world.
The first Tathāgata was named Sovereign Banner of Virtue; While I was in the Golden Flower Garden, I beheld him on the day of his birth.
At that time, I served as his nurse; my wisdom was exceedingly sharp and keen. The devas bestowed upon me the Bodhisattva’s golden body;
I then quickly took it up in my hands. I gazed intently, yet could not see the crown of his head;
his bodily marks were all perfectly complete, each one infinite and boundless—a stainless and pure body.
Adorned with the primary and secondary marks, like a statue of exquisite jewels, Upon seeing them, one rejoices within oneself;
contemplating those merits, The ocean of manifold blessings rapidly increases.
Seeing these miraculous feats, one gives rise to the great bodhicitta, Single-mindedly seeking the virtues of a Buddha, And further expanding all the great vows.
Purifying all lands and eliminating the three evil realms, I universally made offerings to countless Buddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
Practicing my original vows, I rescued and liberated sentient beings from suffering.
In the presence of those Buddhas, I heard the Dharma and attained liberation, as numerous as the atoms within billions of lands.
Through practice for immeasurable eons, I have made offerings to all the Buddhas who appeared during those eons;

I have upheld their true Dharma and purified this ocean of liberation. To the Honored Ones of Ten Powers, as numerous as the atoms within billions of lands, who passed in the past—I have fully maintained their wheels of Dharma and further illuminated this liberation.
In a single moment, I behold within the atoms of this world-system every ocean of lands purified by a Tathāgata;
within each land there is a Buddha, manifesting his birth amidst a garden,
each displaying inconceivable and vast powers of spiritual transformation, or appearing in an inconceivable manner.
Bodhisattvas from billions of lands, dwelling atop celestial palaces, are about to realize the Buddha-enlightenment;
within immeasurable oceans of lands, all the Buddhas manifest their births, surrounded by assemblies preaching the Dharma—all these I see.
In a single thought-moment, I see billions of lands and Bodhisattvas as numerous as atoms.
Leaving home and proceeding to the site of enlightenment, they manifest the realm of the Buddhas.
I see within the atoms of the lands immeasurable Buddhas attaining the Way, each manifesting various skillful means to deliver suffering sentient beings.
Within every single atom, all Buddhas turn the wheel of Dharma, doing so entirely with inexhaustible voices.
Universally raining down the Dharma of ambrosia, In number equal to the atoms within billions of lands;
Within each atom of every land, I see the Tathāgata, Manifesting his entry into parinirvāṇa.
Thus, in immeasurable lands, the Tathāgatas manifest their birth; I likewise manifest my own bodies everywhere, Appearing before them to offer worship.
In inconceivable oceans of lands, with their infinite varieties of destinies, I appear before them all and rain down the great rain of Dharma. O Son of the Buddha, I know this door of liberation;
even in immeasurable billions of eons, its praise could not be fully exhausted.
"Good son, I only know this liberation of the Bodhisattva’s mastery in manifesting birth throughout all places for immeasurable eons.
As for those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who are able to take a single thought-moment as the treasury of all eons and contemplate all dharmas,
they manifest birth through skillful means to universally make offerings to all Buddhas."
They have attained ultimate penetration into all Buddha-dharmas. They manifest birth in all places and sit upon lotus thrones before all Buddhas.
Knowing the time when sentient beings are ready to be delivered, they manifest birth through skillful means to subdue them.
In all lands, he manifests various spiritual transformations, appearing before all like reflections.
How could I possibly know or describe his meritorious conduct? Son of good family, in this city of Kapilavastu there is a woman of the Śākya clan named Gopā.
Go to her and ask: "How does a bodhisattva teach and transform sentient beings within the cycle of birth and death?"
Then the youth Sudhana prostrated at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with deep reverence, took his leave, and departed.

From here below is the ninth [stage], the Lumbinī Grove Goddess, who entrusts [the teaching] to the Stage of Excellent Wisdom (*Sādhumatī-bhūmi*). As for the Stage of Excellent Wisdom, it refers to the attainment of...
Regarding the subtle fourfold unhindered eloquence (*pratisaṃvid*), it is because he is able to skillfully preach the Dharma throughout the ten directions.
This grove is the place where Buddhas are born; it symbolizes that upon reaching the ninth stage, one shall receive office and be born into the family of the Buddhas.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, having heard the aforementioned gate of liberation, recollected, cultivated, mastered, and increased it; following the instructions, he proceeded in search [of his next teacher].

In the Lumbinī Grove, at the abode of the goddess Subhūṣitā, he saw her seated upon a lion throne within a pavilion adorned with all kinds of jewels, preaching the *Sūtra on the Ocean of Birth* for the sake of the assembly of devas, causing them all to be born into the family of the Tathāgata.
Having seen this, Sudhana paid his respects, declared his resolve, and inquired about being born into the family of the Tathāgata. That goddess—
He then bestowed upon him the Dharma-realm, responding: "Good son, there are ten kinds of treasuries of birth for bodhisattvas.
If a bodhisattva accomplishes these ten dharmas, they shall be born into the family of the Tathāgata. This directly answers his question.
First, there are five lines and a half of scripture that praise the excellence of this dharma; next, it inquires: "What are the ten? Next—
Their names are listed as follows: first, the treasury of birth through the vow to constantly make offerings to all Buddhas;
second, the treasury of birth through the arousal of the bodhicitta; third, the treasury of birth through the diligent cultivation of the contemplation of all dharma-gates;
fourth, the treasury of birth through the universal illumination of the three periods of time with a profound and pure mind; fifth, the treasury of equal radiance.
The Treasury of Birth. Sixth, the treasury of birth by being born into the family of the Tathāgatas. Seventh, the treasury of birth through the light of the Buddha’s power.
Eighth, the treasury of birth by contemplating the gateway of universal wisdom. Ninth, the treasury of birth by universally manifesting adornments.
Tenth is the treasury of taking birth upon entering the stage of the Tathāgata. These ten names of the treasuries of taking birth encompass the meaning of the causes and effects of the six stages:
first corresponds to the ten levels of faith; second is the ten abidings; third is the general path of application;
fourth is the first stage (*bhūmi*); fifth extends from the second stage to the seventh; the sixth and seventh gates both refer to the eighth stage; and the eighth is...
The ninth stage corresponds to the tenth stage; the tenth is equal to the stage of Equal Enlightenment (Samyaksambodhi) and entry into the stage of the Tathāgata.
Although the commentary assigns these vertically to six distinct positions, in reality they are perfectly interfused, encompassing the beginning and the end as a whole.

Therefore, the previous praise stated that by accomplishing this Dharma, one is born into the family of the Tathāgata; this meaning clearly demonstrates the mutual penetration of cause and fruit. Next, the prose section first explains each term individually.

The ten sections together with the prose summary comprise sixty-eight lines of sūtra. Together with the subsequent verses of the *saṃgīti*, there are ten stanzas that collectively explain the meaning of this dharma-gate.
Below, the text cites and establishes its name, saying: "A bodhisattva who possesses these ten dharmas is born into the family of the Tathāgata and becomes a pure light for all worlds.
This cites and answers the meaning of the question. Next, the dharma-gate is established.
Regarding this name: "I have, since immeasurable kalpas past, attained the gate of liberation of sovereign birth.

This refers back to the aforementioned dharma to establish the title. As for "sovereign birth," it means that one manifests according to the capacity and resonance [of beings], being free from all obstruction.
Next, Sudhana asks: "Noble One, what is the sphere of this gate of liberation? This is the question.
This is the realm of liberation. The following answer reveals the functional activity of this Dharma gate:
"Good son, I previously made a vow, vowing that whenever any bodhisattvas manifest birth, I would always be able to draw near them.
I vowed to enter the immeasurable ocean of births of the Tathāgata Vairocana; by the power of that former vow, I have been born here in Jambudvīpa."
In the center of the Lumbinī Garden, he focused his mind on when the Bodhisattva would descend to be born. This clarifies that [the birth] was received in accordance with a vow.
Since this garden first came into being, a hundred years have passed; now, as a result, the World-Honored One has descended from Tuṣita Heaven to be born here.
Before his birth, I beheld ten kinds of auspicious omens previously appearing within this grove. There were ten...
The *Six-Section Sutra on Auspicious Signs* describes these portents and concludes by stating:
"When these auspicious signs appear, the various devas immediately know that a Bodhisattva is about to descend to be born. As I observe these signs, my joy is immeasurable.
Next, it describes how ten kinds of auspicious signs appeared when Queen Māyā departed from the city of Kapilavastu and entered this grove before the Bodhisattva’s birth.
Regarding the signs: there are eight folios and a half of sūtra text describing the auspicious omens of Māyā entering the forest.
Next, when Lady Māyā was about to give birth to the Bodhisattva beneath a Pīpal tree, ten kinds of supernatural transformations further manifested.

Regarding those ten kinds of miraculous transformations: First, when the Bodhisattva was about to be born, the devas of the desire and form realms, the eight classes of spirits, and others all gathered in the grove and prepared offerings.
Second, within the womb of Lady Māyā, all the forms and images of the trichiliocosm appeared;
in each of the billions of Jambudvīpas, there were gardens and groves, and each one of them...
There was a lady who, amidst the auspicious signs of the Bodhisattva’s imminent birth,
had all the pores of her three attendants manifest the deeds of the Tathāgata’s past offerings to Buddhas and hearing of the Dharma. In every single pore of the fourth lady’s body,
there appeared all the places where the Tathāgata had dwelt while practicing his former austerities, as well as the kalpas in which he encountered the appearance of Buddhas in the world.
5. She calculates the length of lifespans and the knowledge upon which they depend for practicing wholesome dharmas;

in every place of birth, Queen Māyā is always her mother. Within each and every pore of Queen Māyā, she manifests the physical characteristics, appearances, and experiences of suffering and pleasure in all the places where the Tathāgata was born during his past practices. 6. Māyā...

7. From all the pores of his body, there appeared the accounts of the Tathāgata’s past practices, such as his giving away his head, eyes, marrow, brain, body, blood, flesh, kingdoms, cities, wives, and concubines. 8.
When Queen Māyā entered this grove, the entire forest universally manifested the splendors of past Buddhas entering their mothers’ wombs. Queen Māyā...
When people enter this garden, there emerge from their bodies the palaces and other dwellings where Bodhisattvas reside.
Ninth, when Queen Māyā enters this garden, her body emits as many Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in ten unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, all simultaneously offering praise.
Tenth, when Queen Māyā was about to give birth to the Bodhisattva, suddenly—
Before him, from the adamantine foundation, a great lotus flower emerged, adorned with various jewels and held by the Heavenly Kings;
the eight classes of divine beings each presented offerings. This was a premonitory omen appearing before the Bodhisattva’s descent into birth.
Fifty lines of scripture recount these events in detail, leading down to the actual account of his birth.
After these signs had appeared in the Lumbinī Grove, the Bodhisattva was then born from his mother’s side.
His physical form was like the appearance of a pure solar disc in the empty sky, or like auspicious clouds emerging from the summit of a high mountain;
the radiance of his bodily marks was likewise so. When I beheld the Buddha here in this Jambudvīpa...
When he was born in the Lumbinī Garden, he also saw himself manifesting his initial birth within the Jambudvīpa of each of the ten billion four-continent worlds inside the trichiliocosm;

furthermore, he saw himself manifesting various supernatural transformations of birth within every single atom and every single world-system throughout all worlds in the ten directions, continuing uninterruptedly from moment to moment. There are ten [aspects to this].

One line and a half of the sūtra describe the matter of manifesting births in all places. The preceding section answers the question regarding the realm of liberation, revealing its functional activity (*karmayoga*).
The following section asks about the duration since the resolve for enlightenment was first generated. Sudhana said to that goddess:
"Great Goddess, how long has it been since you attained this liberation? She replied: "In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in a billion buddha-fields..."
After that number of kalpas, there was a world named Universal Jewels (Sarvaratna) and a kalpa named Joyful Delight (Rati).
In that world, there were four continents; within Jambudvīpa, there was a royal capital named Sumeru-Adorned Banner (Sumeru-vyūha-dhvaja).
In that world, there was a king named Ratnajvālākṣa (Jewel-Flame-Eye). The king’s queen was named Priyaprabhā (Joyous Light).
Just as Queen Māyā was the mother of Vairocana in this world, so too was Queen Priyaprabhā the mother of the first Buddha in that world. Noble son, when Queen Priyaprabhā was about to...
At the time of the Bodhisattva’s birth, they went to that flower garden. Within the garden was a tree named Sarvadada (All-Giver).
The Bodhisattva was born as the Joyful Light grasped a branch of that tree. At that time, there was a nurse named Vimalaprabhā (Pure Light) who stood by his side.
The devas bestowed her upon the nurse, who received him with reverence and felt great joy; she immediately attained [the realization of] Bodhi.
The Samādhi of Universal Vision. This is the liberation of being born with sovereign mastery in all places, universally beholding the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions.
Because one has attained this liberation, one sees all Buddhas taking birth with sovereign mastery through the power of their original vows.
Good son, as for that wet-nurse, do you think she was anyone else? It was my very self. [She] did not meet her husband.
"Person" (jina) refers to the present lady, who is none other than the mother of the Buddha in the past.
From that time onward, I have constantly perceived Vairocana Buddha in every thought-moment, manifesting the sovereign spiritual powers of the ocean-like births of Bodhisattvas.
Above this are twenty-one lines of scripture, which describe the causes and conditions for attaining liberation in the past, thereby revealing the root of the Dharma.
Deeply, the goddess of Lumbinī further proclaimed its meaning and spoke in verse; there were twenty-three stanzas praising the causes and conditions of the past.
Then, humbling herself and deferring to the superior, she said: "I know only this much:
that the Bodhisattva, throughout immeasurable eons and in all places, manifests the mastery of taking birth through liberation. As for the various [realizations] of the Bodhisattvas..."
“Sākyamuni takes a single thought-moment as the treasury of all kalpas;

even to the point of manifesting births in all realms of existence and performing the various miraculous feats for the sake of taming sentient beings—how could I possibly know this? He then pointed to his later companion and said:
‘In this city of Kapilavastu, there is a woman of the Śākya clan named Gopā. You should go and ask her; she will explain it to you. At that time...”
The youth Sudhana gazed up at him, paid his respects, took his leave, and departed.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda, a śramaṇa from the Kingdom of Khotan;
with commentary on the meaning by the śramaṇa Chengguan of Dafangguangshan Huayan Monastery at Mount Qingliang;

Entering the Dharma Realm, Chapter Thirty-nine, Part Sixteen.
At that time, the youth Sudhana, facing the city of Kapilavastu, contemplated and practiced the liberation of taking birth;
he increased and expanded his mindfulness without abandoning it, gradually traveling until he reached the Universal Manifestation of the Dharma Realm Assembly of Bodhisattvas.

In the Hall of Radiance, there was a deity named Vigatāśoka-guṇa, who, together with ten thousand palace-lord deities, came forth to welcome Sudhana, saying: "Welcome, O noble man! You possess great wisdom and great valor."
They are able to cultivate the inconceivable sovereign liberation of a bodhisattva; their minds never abandon vast vows;
they skillfully observe the spheres of all phenomena; they dwell securely within the city of Dharma; and they enter into immeasurable gates of expedient means.

They accomplish the great ocean of the Tathāgata’s merits; they attain sublime eloquence to skillfully discipline sentient beings; they obtain the body of noble wisdom and constantly practice in accordance with it;
they know the differences in the mental activities of all sentient beings, causing them to rejoice and advance toward the path of the Buddha.
I observe that you, O noble one, cultivate all sublime practices with a mind never for a moment lax; your deportment and conduct are entirely pure.

Before long, you shall attain the supreme three karmas of the Tathāgatas—pure and adorned—and you shall adorn your body with the primary and secondary marks, and embellish your mind with the wisdom of the ten powers as you traverse the worlds. Thus do I observe you, O noble one.
With a courageous diligence that is peerless, you shall before long behold all Buddhas of the three periods of time and receive their teachings.
Before long, you shall attain the bliss of all bodhisattva dhyānas, liberations, and samādhis.
Before long, you shall enter the profound liberation of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas. Why is this?

Because by seeing, drawing near to, making offerings to, listening to, receiving the teachings of, and recollecting and practicing according to the instructions of a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), you will be untiring and non-retrogressive; free from sorrow and regret; and without obstacles.
Neither Māra nor his followers will be able to create difficulties for you, for before long you shall attain the unsurpassed fruit. Well done!
The youth Vasumitra said, "Noble One, may I attain all that you have just described.

Noble One, my wish is that all sentient beings may be stilled from all fevers of affliction, be freed from all evil karma, give rise to all forms of peace and happiness, and cultivate all pure practices. Noble One, [I pray for this].
All sentient beings give rise to various afflictions, commit various evil deeds, and fall into various evil realms.
Whether in body or mind, they constantly undergo agonizing suffering. When the Bodhisattva sees this, distress arises in his heart. Noble One, it is like a man who has only one son;
his love and affection for him are profound. Suddenly seeing that person’s limbs and body being severed by another, his heart is pierced with such intense pain that he cannot [bear it].

Peace unto you. It is likewise with the bodhisattva-mahāsattva. Seeing sentient beings fall into the three evil realms due to their afflictions and karma, and undergo various sufferings, his mind is filled with great distress and sorrow.

If he sees sentient beings give rise to the three kinds of wholesome karma—of body, speech, and mind—and are born in the realms of gods or humans to experience physical and mental bliss, the bodhisattva at that time gives rise to great joy. Why is this?
For this reason, a bodhisattva does not seek omniscience for their own sake; they do not crave the pleasures and desires of saṃsāra;
they do not follow the force of the inversions of perception, the inversions of view, the inversions of mind, or the various fetters, latent tendencies, cravings, and views;

they do not give rise to various notions of pleasure regarding sentient beings; nor do they relish or become attached to the bliss of the meditative absorptions (dhyāna). They are free from obstacles, weariness, or regression.
Abiding within the cycle of birth and death, they perceive only sentient beings undergoing immeasurable and manifold sufferings throughout the various realms of existence.
They give rise to great compassion and, through the power of their great vows, universally embrace all beings. By the power of this compassionate vow, they cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva.
To sever the afflictions of all sentient beings; to seek the omniscient wisdom of the Tathāgatas;
to make offerings to all Buddhas and Tathāgatas; to adorn and purify all vast buddha-fields;

and to thoroughly cleanse the inclinations, desires, and all mental and physical activities of all sentient beings—therein, they never experience weariness or fatigue within the cycle of birth and death. O Noble One!
Furthermore, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas act as adornments for all sentient beings, so as to cause them to be born among gods and humans in states of wealth and nobility;
they act as parents, establishing them in the bodhicitta; they act as nurturers, bringing them to fulfillment in the bodhisattva path;
they act as guardians, ensuring they remain far removed from the three evil realms; and they act as mariners, enabling them to attain...
It is for the purpose of crossing the ocean of birth and death; it is to serve as a refuge that causes one to abandon all fears of demons and afflictions;
it is to bring about the ultimate goal so that one may forever attain the bliss of cool serenity; it is to serve as a ferry that leads one into the ocean of all Buddhas;
it is to serve as a guide that brings one to the island of the jewels of all dharmas; and it is to cause the lotus of the mind—the merits of all Buddhas—to blossom beautifully.
Because they are ornaments that constantly radiate the light of merit and wisdom; because they are delightful, for whatever they do is entirely dignified and majestic;
because they are venerable, having distanced themselves from all evil karma; because they are Samantabhadra, possessing a body endowed with all dignity and majesty;
because they are great luminaries, constantly radiating the pure light of wisdom; and because they are great clouds, constantly raining down...
Because it is the nectar-like Dharma of all things, when the noble Bodhisattva thus cultivates these practices,
he causes all sentient beings to give rise to love and joy, becoming fully endowed with the bliss of the Dharma. At that time, as the youth Sudhana was about to ascend the Dharma Hall,
the goddess Viśoka and the host of deities offered him exquisite celestial flower garlands, unguents, and powdered incense, surpassing those of all the heavens.
They scattered various jeweled ornaments over Sudhana and spoke these verses:
"You have now appeared in the world As a great lamp of light for the world.
For the sake of all sentient beings, you diligently seek Unsurpassed enlightenment; In immeasurable billions of kalpas, It would be difficult even to behold you."
The Sun of Merit now rises, extinguishing all the darkness of the world.
Seeing all sentient beings shrouded by the delusions of perversion, you have given rise to the mind of great compassion;
seeking to realize the Teacherless Way, you have sought the Bodhi of the Buddhas with a pure mind, serving spiritual friends.
Not begrudging your own body or life, you are without dependence or attachment in all worlds;
your mind is universally unimpeded and pure as space. You have cultivated the practices for awakening until your merits are entirely perfected;
emitting the great light of wisdom, you shine universally upon all worlds.
You do not leave the world, nor do you cling to it; you move through the world without obstruction, like the wind traveling through space.
Just as when a great conflagration arises, nothing can extinguish it, so too is the fire of your diligence in practicing the path to enlightenment— it is courageous and of great vigor.
Firm and immovable, a lion of adamantine wisdom, you roam without fear throughout the entire realm of phenomena;
to all the oceans of lands that exist, you are able to travel and approach them to attend upon spiritual friends.
At that time, after the goddess Aśokaśrī had spoken these verses, she followed Sudhana out of her love for the Dharma, never leaving him.

Then, the youth Sudhana entered the Hall of Universal Manifestation of the Light of the Dharma Realm and searched everywhere for that Śākya girl, seeing her within the hall seated upon a lion throne of precious lotuses. Eighty thousand...
He was surrounded by four thousand court ladies. Among these ladies, there were none who were not born from royal lineages;

they had all cultivated the practices of a bodhisattva in the past and planted roots of goodness together. Having universally gathered in sentient beings through generosity and kind speech, they were already able to clearly perceive the realm of omniscience.
They had collectively cultivated and accumulated the practices for the awakening of a Buddha and constantly dwelt in right concentration.
He constantly dwells in great compassion, universally gathering all sentient beings as if they were his only child. Fully endowed with a heart of loving-kindness, his retinue is pure.

Having already accomplished the inconceivable skillful means of a bodhisattva in the past, he has attained non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and is fully possessed of the various *pāramitās* of a bodhisattva. Free from...
Free from all attachments, they take no pleasure in birth and death; though they traverse the various realms of existence, their minds are ever pure.

Constantly and diligently observing the path to omniscience, they leave behind the net of hindrances and veils, transcending all points of attachment. From the Dharma-body, they manifest transformation bodies, giving rise to the power of a Bodhisattva through the practice of Samantabhadra.
The sun of wisdom and the lamp of insight are both fully perfected. At that time, the youth Sudhana...
The son went to where the Śākya maiden Gopā was, prostrated at her feet, and stood with palms joined, saying: "Noble Lady,
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva, while within birth and death,
remains unstained by the afflictions of birth and death, and realizes the self-nature of phenomena."
While abiding in their true nature, they do not dwell in the stages of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; they fulfill the Buddha-dharmas while practicing the bodhisattva path.
Abiding in the bodhisattva stages, they enter the realm of the Buddhas; transcending the world, they take birth within the world.
Having accomplished the dharma-body, they manifest infinite and diverse form-bodies; having realized the signless dharma, they manifest for the sake of sentient beings.
Regarding all marks: though knowing that dharmas are ineffable, they extensively expound all dharmas for the sake of sentient beings;

though knowing that sentient beings are empty, they never abandon the work of transforming sentient beings; though knowing that all Buddhas are neither born nor extinguished, they diligently make offerings without ever turning back;
and though knowing that all dharmas have no karma and no retribution, they cultivate various virtuous deeds without ever ceasing.
Then the daughter of Gopa said to Sudhana: "Excellent, excellent, noble son!
That you are now able to ask about such practices of the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas—that one who cultivates all the vows and conduct of Samantabhadra should ask in this way—is truly worthy."
Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon it well. I shall, by the spiritual power of the Buddha, proclaim it for you.
Noble son, if bodhisattvas accomplish ten dharmas, they will be able to perfect the bodhisattva practice of the universal wisdom-light of Indra’s net.
What are these ten? They are: by relying on spiritual friends, one attains vast and supreme...
Because of liberation; because of attaining pure desire and joy; because of gathering all merit and wisdom; because of hearing the Dharma from all Buddhas;
because the mind never abandons the Buddhas of the three periods of time; because of being identical to the practices of all Bodhisattvas;

because of being protected and remembered by all Tathāgatas; because the sublime vows of great compassion are entirely pure; and because one is able to universally sever [afflictions] through the power of wisdom.

Because of all births and deaths—this constitutes the ten. If bodhisattvas accomplish these dharmas, they will be able to fulfill the bodhisattva practice of the light of universal wisdom of Indra’s net.

O Son of the Buddha, if a bodhisattva draws near to spiritual friends, they will be able to practice with diligence without regression, cultivating the emergence of inexhaustible Buddha-dharmas. O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhi...
The Bodhisattva serves the spiritual friend through ten kinds of dharmas. What are these ten? They are: being without regard for one’s own body or life;
having no mind of greedy seeking for worldly objects of enjoyment; knowing that the nature of all dharmas is equal and never abandoning the vow for omniscience;
observing the true reality of the entire dharma-realm; and constantly relinquishing [attachment] with the mind.
Regarding the ocean of all that exists: knowing that phenomena are like space, one’s mind has no basis;
one accomplishes all the great vows of a bodhisattva and is constantly able to manifest all oceans of lands, purely cultivating the unimpeded wheel of wisdom of a bodhisattva.
O Son of the Buddha, you should serve all spiritual friends with this Dharma, never opposing them. At that time, Śākyagupta—
The goddess, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, relied upon the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke in verse:
"To benefit all living beings, the Bodhisattva With right mindfulness personally attends the spiritual friend;
Revering them as the Buddha with a tireless mind, This is the conduct in the world known as the Indra-net conduct."
His resolute conviction is as vast as space; all that exists throughout the three times—lands, sentient beings, and Buddhas—is likewise so.
This is the practice of universal wisdom-light, whose aspiration is like the sky, without limit; he has forever severed afflictions and is free from all defilement.
The merit cultivated by all Buddhas—this practice is performed in the world by the Bodhisattva Śarīrameghacārin.
He cultivates omniscience and an inconceivable ocean of merit;
he purifies his body of all virtues and wisdom. This practice is performed in the world as an undefiled conduct.

Those who listen to and receive the Dharma from all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, without ever feeling satiated, are able to give rise to the lamp of wisdom of the true mark (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*). This practice shines universally throughout the world;
in a single thought-moment, they are able to enter into the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions.

With a mind that never forsakes the Tathāgatas, This practice of great vows directed toward Bodhi can enter the assemblies of all Buddhas; The ocean of samādhis of all Bodhisattvas, the ocean of vows,
and the ocean of skillful means— This practice in the world is like the conduct of Indra’s net.
Sustained by the empowerment of all Buddhas, throughout boundless kalpas until the end of the future,
they practice the path of Samantabhadra everywhere; these are the deeds of the Bodhisattva’s emanations,
who, seeing sentient beings undergoing great suffering, give rise to great compassion and manifest in the world.
Manifesting the light of the Dharma to dispel the darkness—this is the course of the Bodhisattva’s sun of wisdom.

Seeing all sentient beings within the various realms of existence, he turns the infinite wheels of Dharma for them, so that they may forever sever the stream of birth and death; this is the practice of the Universal Worthy (Samantabhadra).
The Bodhisattva practices these skillful means, manifesting bodies in accordance with the minds of sentient beings;
throughout all realms of existence, they transform and deliver immeasurable conscious beings.
By the power of great compassion and skillful means, they manifest their forms everywhere throughout the world.
"According to their understanding and inclinations, I preach the Dharma to them, causing all to advance toward the path of Bodhi.
When Śākyaghoṣa had spoken this verse, he addressed the youth Sudhana, saying:
"Noble son, I have attained the liberation door called 'The Ocean of Samādhis for Contemplating All Bodhisattvas. " Sudhana said: "O Great Sage, this..."

"What is the scope of this gate of liberation? He replied, "Noble son, having entered this liberation, I know all sentient beings within as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field of this Sahā world—how they die here and are born there among the various realms of existence;

how they perform good and evil deeds and undergo their respective karmic fruits; and whether they seek liberation or do not seek liberation, whether they are fixed in the right [path], or fixed in the wrong."
I fully know and see all such accumulated wholesome and unwholesome dharmas: those that are concentrated and those that are unconcentrated; those with afflictions and those without afflictions;
those possessing wholesome roots and those lacking wholesome roots; wholesome roots subsumed by unwholesome roots, and unwholesome roots subsumed by wholesome roots.
Furthermore, I know the names of all the Buddhas who appeared during that eon.

I have fully understood them all in their proper sequence. I have fully understood how that Buddha, the World-Honored One, from his first aspiration and through his skillful means, sought all-knowledge;
how he gave rise to the ocean of all great vows; how he made offerings to all Buddhas and cultivated the bodhisattva practices;
how he attained equal and perfect enlightenment and turned the wondrous wheel of Dharma; and how he manifested great supernormal powers to transform and deliver sentient beings. I also know...
Regarding the distinctions among the assemblies of those Buddhas: within those assemblies, there are sentient beings who attain liberation by relying on the Śrāvaka vehicle.
I fully know all the roots of goodness they cultivated in the past, as well as the various forms of wisdom they have attained.
There are also sentient beings who attain liberation by relying on the Pratyekabuddha vehicle. As for those...
I fully know all the roots of goodness of the pratyekabuddhas, as well as the enlightenment they attain, their tranquility, liberation, supernormal powers, transformations,
their ripening of sentient beings, and their entry into nirvana. I also know the assemblies of bodhisattvas of those Buddhas—
how those bodhisattvas, from their first generation of the mind of awakening, cultivated roots of goodness and gave rise to immeasurable great vows and practices until they attained accomplishment.
They fulfill all the *pāramitās*. They adorn the path of the bodhisattva in various ways. By means of their power of mastery, they enter the bodhisattva stages (*bodhisattvabhūmi*).

Abiding in the bodhisattva stages, they contemplate the bodhisattva stages, purify the bodhisattva stages, and [contemplate] the characteristics of the bodhisattva stages, the wisdom of the bodhisattva stages, the wisdom of the bodhisattva’s integration, the wisdom of the bodhisattva’s teaching and transforming of sentient beings, and the wisdom of the bodhisattva’s establishment. The bodhisattva...
The sphere of vast conduct; the spiritual powers of bodhisattvas; the ocean of bodhisattva samādhis; the skillful means of bodhisattvas;
the oceans of samādhis entered by bodhisattvas in every thought-moment; the light of omniscience attained; the clouds of lightning-flashes of omniscience obtained;
the patience regarding the true nature of reality realized; the mastery of omniscience attained; and the oceans of buddha-fields wherein they dwell.
I fully know the ocean of dharmas they enter; the ocean of sentient beings they know; the skillful means in which they abide; the vows they have made; and the spiritual powers they manifest.
Good son, I fully know all the oceans of kalpas throughout the future in this Sahā world, continuing without interruption from one to another.
Just as I know the Sahā world, so too do I know the [worlds] of the Sahā world-system.
He also knows the worlds as numerous as the atoms within a single world-system; he also knows all the worlds within the Sahā world-system;
he also knows all the worlds contained within the atoms of the Sahā world-system;
he also knows the worlds situated in the ten directions without interval outside the Sahā world-system; and he also knows the worlds comprised within the world-classes of the Sahā world-system.
He knows the worlds comprised within the infinite world-systems of the ten directions in this Flower Bank Ocean of World-Systems of the World-Honored One Vairocana;
