it is the dwelling place of those who, in a single thought-moment, travel to all lands; it is the dwelling place of those who manifest their bodies before all sentient beings.
It is the dwelling place of those whose minds constantly benefit all worlds; it is the dwelling place of those who are able to reach every location;

it is the dwelling place of those who, though having already transcended all worlds, constantly manifest their bodies therein for the sake of transforming sentient beings; it is the dwelling place of those who are unattached to any land.
This is the dwelling place of those who travel to all lands for the sake of making offerings to all Buddhas;
it is the dwelling place of those who, without moving from their original location, can universally visit all Buddha-fields and adorn them;
it is the dwelling place of those who draw near to all Buddhas yet do not give rise to the notion of "Buddha"; it is the dwelling place of those who rely upon all spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
It is the dwelling place of those who do not give rise to the notion of a "spiritual friend" (kalyāṇamitra).

It is the dwelling place of those who abide in all the palaces of Māra yet are not attached to the realms of desire. It is the dwelling place of those who have forever abandoned all mental conceptions.
It is the dwelling place of those who, although manifesting their bodies among all sentient beings, do not give rise to the distinction between self and other.

It is the dwelling place of those who possess the perception of non-duality; it is the dwelling place of those who can universally enter all worlds while maintaining no perception of differentiation within the dharma-realm;
it is the dwelling place of those who vow to abide through all future eons while maintaining no perception of length or brevity regarding those eons;
it is the dwelling place of those who manifest their bodies everywhere without departing from the tip of a single hair.
This is the dwelling place of those who dwell in all worlds; it is the dwelling place of those who can expound the Dharma that is difficult to encounter;

it is the dwelling place of those who abide in the Dharma that is difficult to know, the profound Dharma, the non-dual Dharma, the signless Dharma, the Dharma without antidotes, the Dharma of non-apprehension, and the Dharma free from conceptual proliferation; it is the dwelling place of those who abide in great loving-kindness and great compassion.
This is the dwelling place of those who have already transcended all wisdom of the two vehicles,
who have already surpassed all realms of Māra, who are already unstained by worldly dharmas, who have already reached the *pāramitā* attained by Bodhisattvas,
and who dwell in the dwelling place of the Tathāgatas. Although they are detached from all marks (*lakṣaṇa*), they nevertheless do not enter the stage of the Śrāvakas.
The state of correctness (*samyaktva*) is the dwelling place of those who, although they have realized that all phenomena are unborn, do not abide even in the nature of non-arising.
It is the place where one contemplates impurity without realizing the dharma of freedom from greed, yet does not remain associated with desire;

where one cultivates loving-kindness without realizing the dharma of freedom from hatred, yet does not remain associated with the defilement of anger; and where one contemplates dependent origination...
This is the dwelling place of those who have not realized the state free from delusion, yet are not accompanied by the confusion of delusion;

who, though abiding in the four dhyānas, are not reborn according to those meditative states; who, though practicing the four immeasurables for the sake of transforming sentient beings, are not reborn in the realm of form;
and who, though cultivating the four formless absorptions out of great compassion, do not abide in the formless realm.
This is the dwelling place of those who, though diligently practicing *śamatha* and *vipaśyanā*, do not realize liberation for the sake of transforming sentient beings;
who, though practicing equanimity (*upekṣā*), do not abandon the work of transforming sentient beings; who, though contemplating emptiness (*śūnyatā*), do not give rise to the view of emptiness;
who, though practicing the signless (*animitta*), constantly transform sentient beings attached to signs; and who, though practicing the wishless (*apraṇihita*)...
This is the dwelling place of those who do not abandon the practices and vows of enlightenment.
Although they have attained mastery over all karma and afflictions, they manifest conformity to all karma and afflictions for the sake of transforming sentient beings.

Although they are free from birth and death, they manifest the acceptance of birth and death for the sake of transforming sentient beings. Although they have already transcended all realms of existence, they [remain] for the sake of transforming sentient beings...
Therefore, he demonstrates the dwelling place of those who enter the various realms of existence. Although he practices loving-kindness (*maitrī*), he feels no attachment toward sentient beings;
although he practices compassion (*karuṇā*), he has no grasping toward sentient beings;

although he practices sympathetic joy (*muditā*), his mind is constantly filled with pity as he contemplates suffering beings; and although he practices equanimity (*upekṣā*), he does not abandon the benefit [of others].

This is the dwelling place of those who attend to other matters. Although they practice the nine successive meditative attainments (*navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), they do not weary of taking birth in the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*).
Although they know that all phenomena are without arising or ceasing, they do not realize the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).

Although they enter the three gates of liberation (*trivimokṣamukha*), they do not grasp at the liberation of the śrāvakas. Although they contemplate the four noble truths (*catvāry āryasatyāni*), they do not abide in the Lesser Vehicle.
Riding upon the fruits of the noble ones, though they contemplate the profound dependent origination, they do not abide in ultimate quiescence;

though they cultivate the Eightfold Noble Path, they do not seek permanent transcendence from the world; though they have surpassed the stage of ordinary beings, they do not fall into the stages of the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas;
though they contemplate the five aggregates of clinging, they do not bring those aggregates to final extinction; and though they have transcended the four Māras...
He discerns all māras; though he does not cling to the six sense bases, he does not utterly extinguish them.
Though he dwells in true suchness (*tathatā*), he does not fall into the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*). Though he teaches all vehicles (*yāna*), he does not abandon the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*).
This great celestial palace is the dwelling place of those who abide in all such merits. At that time, the youth Sudhana...
And he spoke these verses:
"Thus, Maitreya, the Honored One, whose great compassion and pure wisdom Benefit the world,
the eldest son of the Buddhas on the stage of consecration, Has entered the dwelling place that is the realm of the Tathāgatas."

All these sons of the Buddhas of great renown, having entered the gate of liberation of the Mahāyāna, travel through the dharma-realm with minds free from attachment. This is the dwelling place of those who are peerless:
generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, skillful means, vows, power, and supernormal knowledges.
Such is the dwelling place of those who are fully endowed with all the perfections of the Mahāyāna;
their wisdom is as vast as space, universally knowing all phenomena of the three times,
unimpeded, independent, and without grasping— the dwelling place of those who have realized the nature of all existence.
Skillfully able to understand all phenomena— Without intrinsic nature, without arising, and without dependence;
Like a bird flying through the sky, attaining mastery— This is the dwelling place of the Great Wise One.
Having realized the true nature of the three poisons, He discerns that they arise falsely through causes and conditions.
Nor do they seek liberation out of weariness with that [saṃsāra]; this is the dwelling place of those who are tranquil:

the three doors of liberation and the eightfold noble path. They are able to observe all the aggregates, bases, elements, and dependent origination, yet they do not proceed toward mere quiescence; this is the dwelling place of those who are skillful.

The lands of the ten directions and all sentient beings— With unimpeded wisdom, he observes them all and realizes their nature is empty, without discrimination. This is the dwelling place of the one in tranquil extinction;
He practices throughout the entire dharma-realm without obstruction, Yet the nature of his practice cannot be found.
Like the wind moving through space, there is nowhere it travels; this is the dwelling place of those who are without dependence.

Seeing everywhere the multitudes of beings in the evil realms, who undergo various agonies and have no refuge, he emits the great light of compassion that completely extinguishes them all; this is the dwelling place of those who are filled with pity.
Seeing all sentient beings have lost the right path—like those born blind treading a perilous road—he leads them into the city of liberation; this is the dwelling place of the Great Guide.
Seeing all sentient beings caught in the net of Māra, constantly oppressed by birth, old age, sickness, and death.
Causing them to be liberated and find solace— this is the dwelling place of the courageous and valiant.

Seeing all sentient beings afflicted by the disease of delusion, he gives rise to a heart of vast compassion and eliminates it entirely with the medicine of wisdom— this is the dwelling place of the Great King of Physicians.
Seeing all living beings drowning in the ocean of existence, Sunk and oppressed by sorrow, undergoing manifold sufferings, He rescues them all with the ship of the Dharma;
This is the dwelling place of the One Who Crosses Well.
Seeing all beings within the ocean of delusion, He is able to give rise to the wondrous jewel-mind of Bodhicitta.
Entering therein, they rescue and deliver all; this is the dwelling place of the skillful fisherman.
With eyes of great vows and compassion, he constantly surveys all sentient beings and draws them out from the ocean of existence;
this is the dwelling place of the Golden-Winged King (Garuda).
Just as the sun and moon dwell in the void, There is no part of the entire world they do not illuminate;
The light of wisdom is likewise so. This is the dwelling place of those who illumine the world:
For the sake of transforming even a single sentient being, Bodhisattvas remain throughout all future eons, as infinite as space.
As it is for one person, so it is for all; this Saviour dwells in a single land-field to transform sentient beings, without ceasing throughout all future kalpas,
and in every land-field it is likewise— this is the dwelling place of the One of Firm Resolve.
The Dharma taught by all Buddhas of the ten directions, He receives in a single sitting and exhausts it all;
Thus shall it be throughout all future eons. This is the dwelling place of those with the ocean of wisdom:
They travel everywhere through all oceans of worlds, Universally entering all oceans of sites of enlightenment.
Making offerings to the ocean of all Tathāgatas— this is the dwelling place of those who practice;
practicing the ocean of all sublime conducts, and giving rise to an ocean of boundless great vows,
thus passing through oceans of many kalpas— this is the dwelling place of those possessed of merit.
Upon the tip of a single hair, immeasurable lands, Buddhas, sentient beings, and eons cannot be described;
thus he clearly perceives them all without exception—this is the dwelling place of the unimpeded eye.
In a single thought-moment, he universally encompasses boundless eons, as well as the lands, the Buddhas, and the sentient beings therein.
With unimpeded wisdom, he knows all things correctly; this is the dwelling place of that virtuous person.

Even if the lands of the ten directions were ground into dust, and all the great oceans were measured by drops from a single hair, such would be the number of vows made by the Bodhisattva—this is the dwelling place of that one who is unimpeded.
Accomplishing the gates of dhāraṇī and samādhi, With great vows, various dhyānas, and liberations,
Each abiding for boundless eons— This is the dwelling place of the true sons of the Buddha.
Immeasurable and boundless sons of the Buddha Preach the Dharma in various ways to deliver sentient beings.
It is also said that all the various worldly arts and crafts are the dwelling place of this practitioner;

they achieve the skillful means and wisdom of supernatural powers. Practicing the wondrous Dharma-gate of illusion, they manifest births throughout the five destinies in the ten directions; this is the dwelling place of those who are unimpeded.
From the very first moment of generating the mind of enlightenment, the Bodhisattva fully practices all deeds;
his emanations are infinite, pervading the entire Dharma-realm. This is the dwelling place of one possessed of such spiritual power:
in a single thought-moment, he accomplishes the path to Bodhi and universally performs boundless works of wisdom.
Worldly thoughts and anxieties all become deranged; this is the dwelling place of those whose measure is unfathomable.
Having accomplished spiritual powers without obstruction, they travel through the realm of phenomena without exception;
yet their minds have never attained anything. This is the dwelling place of those with pure wisdom.
The Bodhisattva practices unimpeded wisdom, Entering all lands without attachment;
With non-dual knowledge, they illuminate everywhere— This is the dwelling place of those who realize selflessness.
Understanding that all phenomena have no basis, Their original nature is quiescent, like empty space.
Constantly practicing within such a sphere of experience is the dwelling place of those free from defilement;
seeing everywhere that sentient beings undergo various sufferings, they give rise to a heart of great compassion and wisdom,
vowing to always benefit all worlds— this is the dwelling place of those who possess pity and mercy.
The Buddha-son dwelling here appears before all sentient beings, Like the bright orb of the moon, universally dispelling the darkness of birth and death.
The Buddha-son dwelling here universally accords with the minds of sentient beings, Manifesting infinite bodies that fill the lands of the ten directions. The Buddha-son dwelling here...
Wandering through all worlds to the abodes of all Tathāgatas, The sons of the Buddha dwell here for immeasurable and incalculable eons, contemplating the teachings of all Buddhas.
For immeasurable and incalculable eons their minds never grow weary; Dwelling here, the sons of the Buddha enter samādhi in every thought-moment.

Each and every gate of samādhi Reveals the realm of all Buddhas. When the sons of the Buddha dwell herein, they fully know all lands, Immeasurable and innumerable eons, The names of sentient beings and the names of Buddhas.
When the sons of the Buddha dwell herein, They encompass all eons in a single thought-moment, Simply following the minds of sentient beings.

Yet they are free from conceptual discrimination; Abiding here, the sons of the Buddha Cultivate all samādhis within each moment of thought, Thoroughly understanding the phenomena of the three periods of time.
Abiding here, the sons of the Buddha Sit with their bodies unmoving in the full lotus posture, Universally manifesting throughout all lands And amidst all realms of existence.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here drink from the ocean of all Buddha-dharmas; they enter deeply into the ocean of wisdom and are fully endowed with the ocean of merit.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here know completely the number of all lands, the number of eons, and the number of sentient beings;
the same is true for the number of Buddhas' names. The Buddha-sons dwelling here...
In a single thought, they are able to comprehend entirely the formation and destruction of all lands throughout the three periods of time.
Abiding here, the sons of the Buddha universally know the practices and vows of the Buddhas;

abiding here, the sons of the Buddha see within a single mote of dust the various practices performed by Bodhisattvas, as well as the faculties, dispositions, and desires of sentient beings. Abiding here, the sons of the Buddha behold [all this] within a single atom.
In immeasurable lands and sites of enlightenment, Sentient beings and all kalpas— As within a single atom, so it is within all atoms;
All varieties are fully present, Everywhere without obstruction.
The Son of the Buddha dwelling here Universally contemplates all phenomena: Sentient beings, lands, and worlds.

Without arising and without anything existing, they contemplate the equality of sentient beings, the equality of phenomena, the equality of Tathāgatas, the equality of buddha-fields, and the equality of all vows; the three times are entirely equal.
Abiding herein, the sons of the Buddha transform and guide all multitudes of living beings, making offerings to all Tathāgatas and contemplating the nature of all phenomena.
Throughout immeasurable thousands of millions of eons, The practices of their vows and wisdom have been cultivated;

So vast and immeasurable, they cannot be fully extolled. To those great heroes who act without obstruction And abide within this [state], I join my palms in reverent salutation— To the eldest sons of all Buddhas.
"To the Noble Maitreya of Holy Virtue, I now offer worship and homage; may he deign to turn his compassionate attention toward me.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, having praised all the bodhisattvas within the Great Pavilion of Vairocana’s Adorned Treasury with such immeasurable dharmas of extolling and praising bodhisattvas, bowed his body.
With palms joined in reverence, they prostrated themselves. With single-minded devotion, they wished to behold Maitreya Bodhisattva and draw near to make offerings.
Then they saw Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva approaching from another direction, accompanied by immeasurable devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and gandharvas.
Asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoraga kings, Śakra, Brahmā, and the World-Protectors,
along with their immeasurable retinues from their respective places of birth, and a multitude of brahmins and countless hundreds of thousands of other beings,
surrounded him from before and behind as they came together toward the Great Tower of the Treasury of Adornments. Upon seeing them, Sudhana leaped for joy.

Leaping up, he prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground. At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva observed Sudhana, pointed him out to the great assembly, and praising his merit, spoke these verses:
Behold you, Sudhana, whose wisdom and mind are pure; You have come to my presence to seek the practice for enlightenment.
Welcome, O one perfected in compassion! Welcome, O one of pure pity!
Welcome, O one with eyes of tranquility! You who practice without weariness, Welcome, O one of pure intention!
Welcome, you of vast and noble mind; welcome, you whose faculties do not regress. Welcome, you who practice without weariness;

welcome, you of unshakable conduct. You who constantly seek out virtuous friends, who thoroughly understand all phenomena, and who subdue all living beings—welcome, you who walk the sublime path; welcome, you who abide in merit.
Welcome, you who have set out for the fruit of Buddhahood, Never experiencing weariness. Welcome, whose very essence is virtue;
Welcome, nourished by the Dharma. Welcome, whose conduct is boundless, Difficult for the world to perceive.
Welcome, free from delusion, Untainted by worldly conditions— Gain and loss, defamation and praise, and the like.
Completely free from discrimination, you come to bestow peace and happiness;
With minds made supple, capable of being transformed, all deceit, flattery, anger, and pride are utterly extinguished. Welcome, true sons of the Buddha!
You go everywhere throughout the ten directions, Increasing all merits, supple and free from weariness.
Welcome, you who possess the wisdom of the three times, Who thoroughly know all phenomena,
And universally produce a treasury of merit through tireless cultivation. Mañjuśrī, Guṇamegha, and all other sons of the Buddhas,
Have caused you to come to my presence, To show you the realm of non-obstruction, Where you may fully practice the bodhisattva path.

Universally gathering all living beings— such a person of vast capacity has now come to my presence to seek the pure realm of all Tathāgatas. Having come to my presence to inquire about these vast vows,
they ask about the various deeds and practices accomplished by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
Since you wish to practice and study all things, you have come to my presence;
since you seek the subtle Dharma from a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) and wish to receive the bodhisattva conduct, you have come to my presence.
You must keep in mind the spiritual friend who is praised by all Buddhas, for they shall cause you to attain enlightenment.
And have come to my presence; you have remembered me as a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra).
You have given birth to me like a father and mother, and nurtured me like a wet-nurse.

You have increased my factors of enlightenment (bodhipakṣa), like a physician healing all ailments, like the heavens sprinkling nectar, like the sun revealing the right path, and like the moon turning the pure wheel.
Unshakable as a mountain, Without increase or decrease like the ocean, Like a boatman who has come to ferry others across, he has arrived at my side.
Behold this spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra): He is like a great and valiant general, Like a great caravan leader, And like a great guide, Who is able to raise the banner of the True Dharma.
It can manifest the virtues of the Buddhas; It can extinguish all evil realms; It can open the gates to the happy destinies;
It can reveal the bodies of all Buddhas; It can guard the treasuries of all Buddhas; It can uphold the teachings of all Buddhas.
Therefore, I pray that you will look upon me with favor. Desiring to fulfill pure wisdom, And desiring to possess a well-proportioned body, [I seek this].
Desiring to be born into a noble family, you have come to my presence. You all should observe this person who has drawn near to a spiritual friend;
following what he practices and studies, you should all act in accordance with it.
By virtue of past causes and conditions of merit, Mañjuśrī has caused him to resolve upon the mind [of awakening]; follow him in harmony, without opposition.
Practicing without weariness, one abandons parents, relatives, palaces, and all wealth;
with humility, one seeks out spiritual friends. Thus purifying the mind and forever leaving behind the worldly body, one shall be born in a Buddha-land and receive all supreme fruits of retribution.
Sudhana beholds sentient beings suffering from birth, old age, sickness, and death; for their sake, he gives rise to great compassion and diligently cultivates the unsurpassed path.
Sudhana beholds sentient beings constantly transmigrating through the five realms of existence;
seeking adamantine wisdom, he shall shatter the wheel of all those sufferings. Sudhana beholds sentient beings...
The field of the mind is exceedingly wild and defiled; To remove the thorns of the three poisons, One seeks exclusively the plow of sharp wisdom.
Sentient beings dwell in the darkness of delusion, Blind and obscured, having lost the right path.
Sudhana acts as their guide, Showing them the place of peace and security: The armor of patience, the vehicle of liberation, And wisdom as the sharp sword.
Able, within the three realms of existence, to destroy the thieves of all afflictions;
Sudhana, the master of the Dharma-ship, universally rescues all sentient beings, Causing them to cross the ocean of saṃsāra and swiftly reach the pure jewel-island.
Sudhana, the sun of perfect enlightenment, with the wheel of great vows and the light of wisdom, Traverses everywhere through the void of the Dharma-realm.

Universally illuminating the dwellings of the deluded masses, The moon of the perfect awakening of Sudhana, With the white dharmas all fully perfected, The cool light of compassionate concentration Shines equally upon the minds of sentient beings.
Sudhana’s ocean of noble wisdom Abides in reliance upon the straightforward mind; His bodhisattva practices gradually deepen, Giving birth to the myriad jewels of the Dharma.
The Great-Minded Dragon Sudhana ascends into the void of the Dharma-realm; He raises clouds and pours down sweet rain, bringing all fruits to fruition.
Sudhana kindles the lamp of Dharma: Faith is the wick, compassion the oil, mindfulness the vessel, and merit the light.
It extinguishes the darkness of the three poisons and awakens the *kalala* of the mind.
Compassion is its womb, loving-kindness its flesh, and the factors of enlightenment its limbs and joints.
It grows from the *tathāgatagarbha*, increasing the treasury of merit, the treasury of pure wisdom, the treasury of skillful means, and giving birth to the treasury of great vows.
Such is this magnificent adornment that protects and delivers all living beings.
Among all devas and humans, it is difficult to hear and difficult to see.
The roots of such a tree of wisdom are so deep they cannot be moved; the ocean of manifold practices increases, universally shading all living beings.
If you wish to give rise to all virtues, if you wish to inquire about all dharmas, and if you wish to sever all doubts—
Seeking exclusively for spiritual friends, Desiring to shatter the demons of delusion, Desiring to remove the stains of all views,
And desiring to untie the bonds of sentient beings— Seeking exclusively for spiritual friends, One should extinguish all evil realms, Reveal the path to humans and devas,
Cause them to cultivate meritorious deeds, And swiftly enter the city of Nirvana.
One should cross over the perils of various views; one should recognize the net of various views; one should dry up the waters of craving and desire;

one should show the path of the three realms. One should become a refuge for the world, a light for the world, and a teacher of the three realms, showing them the place of liberation, and likewise causing the world to do so.

Universally free from all conceptual attachments, Universally awakened from the spittle of afflictions, Universally emerged from the mire of craving and desire, You shall thoroughly understand all various dharmas, And you shall purify all various buddha-fields. All shall reach ultimate fulfillment;
Your mind is greatly joyful, Your conduct is exceedingly gentle and supple, And your mind is most pure.
Whatever merits you wish to cultivate shall all be brought to full completion; before long, you shall behold the Buddhas and thoroughly penetrate all dharmas.
You shall adorn and purify oceans of buddha-fields and achieve great enlightenment;
you shall fulfill the ocean of all practices, know the ocean of all dharmas, and deliver the ocean of sentient beings.
Cultivating all practices in this way, one shall reach the shore of merit;
one shall give birth to all virtuous qualities and become equal to the sons of the Buddha.
With such a resolute mind, one shall sever all delusions, purify all karma, subdue all māras, and fulfill these aspirations.
You shall give birth to the path of wondrous wisdom; You shall open the path of the True Dharma. Before long, you shall abandon the paths of afflictions, karma, and all sufferings.

The wheel of all sentient beings, Sunk in the wheel of various existences— You shall turn the Wheel of Dharma, Causing them to sever the wheel of suffering. You shall uphold the lineage of the Buddhas.
You shall purify the seed of the Dharma; you shall gather the seed of the Saṃgha. You shall pervade all three times;
you shall sever the net of all cravings; you shall tear asunder the net of all views;
you shall rescue the net of all sufferings; you shall fulfill this net of vows; you shall deliver the realm of sentient beings; and you shall purify the realm of the buddha-fields.
One should gather the realm of wisdom; one should perfect this realm of mind.
One should cause sentient beings to rejoice, cause bodhisattvas to rejoice, and cause all Buddhas to rejoice. One should achieve this joy;
one should see all realms of existence, see all buddha-fields, and see all phenomena.
When I become this Buddha, I shall emit light that destroys darkness; I shall emit light that soothes heat; I shall emit light that extinguishes evil.
I shall wash away the sufferings of the three realms of existence; I shall open the gate to the celestial realms;
I shall open the gate to the Buddha-way; I shall show the gate of liberation, causing all sentient beings to enter it universally.
One should demonstrate the true path and sever the paths of evil. Thus, through diligent practice, one accomplishes the path to Bodhi.

One should cultivate an ocean of merit and cross the ocean of the three realms of existence, causing the entire ocean of sentient beings to emerge from the ocean of manifold sufferings. One should act thus for the ocean of sentient beings.
Exhaust the ocean of afflictions, Cause the ocean of all practices to be cultivated, And swiftly enter the ocean of great wisdom.
You shall increase the ocean of wisdom; You shall cultivate the ocean of practice; The ocean of the great vows of all Buddhas— You shall fulfill them all.
You shall enter the ocean of lands; You shall contemplate the ocean of sentient beings.
You should, by the power of wisdom, drink universally from the ocean of all dharmas;
you should behold the clouds of all Buddhas, arouse clouds of offerings, and listen to the clouds of the wondrous Dharma.

You should raise these clouds of vows, wander universally through the chambers of the three realms of existence, universally destroy the chambers of all delusions, and universally enter the chamber of the Tathāgata.
One should practice this path: universally entering the gates of samādhi, universally roaming through the gates of liberation, and universally abiding in the gates of supernormal powers;
traversing throughout the entire dharma-realm, appearing before all sentient beings and facing all Buddhas.
Like the light of the sun and moon, one shall accomplish such power.
Your conduct shall be free from agitation; Your conduct shall be free from attachment. Like a bird moving through the sky, you shall accomplish this wondrous function;
Like Indra’s net, the network of realms abides thus— You should go to them all, Unimpeded like the wind, And enter the Dharma-realm.
You travel throughout all worlds, Universally beholding the Buddhas of the three times.
With a heart of great joy, you have already attained And shall further attain all dharma-gates. You should give rise to great exultation;
Without greed and without weariness, You are a vessel of merit, Able to follow the teachings of all Buddhas.
Those able to cultivate the bodhisattva practices can behold such wonders;
such sons of the Buddhas are difficult to encounter even in billions of eons, let alone behold their merits.
Having cultivated these various sublime paths, you have been born among humans and have gained great benefit from all virtues; you have been able to see Mañjuśrī and the others.
Possessing immeasurable merits, you have already departed from all evil realms; Having emerged from all places of peril, you have transcended all suffering and affliction.
Excellent! Do not be indolent; having left the stage of ordinary beings, You now dwell upon the stage of a bodhisattva.
You shall fulfill the stage of wisdom and swiftly enter the stage of the Tathāgata.
The conduct of Bodhisattvas is like the ocean; The wisdom of the Buddhas is equal to space.

Your aspiration is likewise so— You should give rise to great joy. With your faculties untiring, And your resolve ever firm, By attending upon spiritual friends, All shall soon be fully accomplished. Such are the various practices of Bodhisattvas.
All act to harmonize sentient beings, universally practicing all Dharma-gates. Be careful not to give rise to doubt;
you possess inconceivable merit as well as true faith. Therefore, on this day, you are able to see these sons of the Buddhas.
Seeing these sons of the Buddhas, you shall all obtain vast and great benefit.
Each and every one of these great vows is faithfully accepted by all.
You are able to cultivate the bodhisattva practices within the three realms of existence; therefore, O sons of the Buddha, I show you this gate of liberation.
It is not for those who are not vessels of the Dharma to dwell together with the sons of the Buddha, even if it were for immeasurable eons.
Its realm is beyond comprehension; that you see these bodhisattvas and have been able to hear such a Dharma is something extremely rare in the world.
You should give rise to great joy and celebration: the Buddhas protect and mind you, and the bodhisattvas take you into their care.
Since you are able to practice in accordance with their teachings, it is well that you dwell in this life.

Having already been born into the family of Bodhisattvas, having already perfected the virtues of a Bodhisattva, and having grown within the lineage of the Tathāgatas, you shall soon ascend to the stage of consecration. Before long, you shall attain equality with all the sons of the Buddhas;
seeing sentient beings afflicted by suffering, you shall establish them all in a state of peace and security, just as one plants seeds according to their kind.
You shall surely obtain such a fruit; I now congratulate and comfort you. You ought to be greatly joyful!
Though immeasurable bodhisattvas have practiced the Way for immeasurable kalpas, they were unable to accomplish this conduct;
now you have attained it all through the power of firm progress in faith and joy. Thus has Sudhana accomplished this conduct.
If one possesses a heart of reverence and admiration, one should likewise train in this way:
All meritorious deeds arise from aspiration and desire; Sudhana has already understood this.
Always delighting in diligent cultivation, like a dragon spreading dense clouds, He will surely pour down a great rain; Thus does the Bodhisattva give rise to the wisdom of aspiration.
If you have a virtuous friend who decisively causes you to practice all deeds and shows you the conduct of Samantabhadra, you should serve them well;
be careful not to give rise to doubt. For immeasurable eons you have recklessly cast away your body out of desire;
now, for the sake of seeking enlightenment, this casting away is truly virtuous.
Throughout immeasurable eons, you have endured the sufferings of birth and death; you have never served the Buddhas nor heard of such a practice.

Now that you have obtained a human body, encountered a Buddha and a spiritual friend, and have been able to hear and receive this bodhisattva practice—why do you not rejoice? Even though you have met with the appearance of a Buddha in the world.
Even if one encounters a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), if their mind is not pure, they will not hear such a Dharma.
However, if one has faith, joy, and respect for a spiritual friend, and is free from delusion and weariness, then one hears such a Dharma.
If there are those who hear this Dharma and give rise to a heart of aspiration, [they shall attain it].
One should know that such a person has already attained vast benefit;
with such purity of mind, they will always remain near the Buddhas and also near the Bodhisattvas. They will certainly achieve enlightenment.
If one enters this Dharma-gate, they will possess all merits and be forever separated from the various evil realms.
Not experiencing any suffering, before long they shall cast off this body and be reborn in a Buddha-land,
where they constantly behold the Buddhas of the ten directions as well as all the Bodhisattvas. Through the power of past causes,
present pure understanding, and service to virtuous friends, their various merits increase like lotuses born from water.
Delight in spiritual friends; diligently make offerings to all Buddhas;
listen to the Dharma with single-minded focus and always practice without weariness. You are a true vessel for the Dharma;
you shall possess all dharmas, you shall cultivate all paths, and you shall fulfill all vows. By means of your mind of faith and understanding...
And because you are able to pay homage to me, before long you shall enter universally into the assemblies of all Buddhas.
Excellent, true son of the Buddha! You who revere all Buddhas, before long you will be endowed with all practices and reach the shore of the Buddha’s merits.
You should now go to the presence of Mañjuśrī, the one of great wisdom.
"He shall cause you to attain the profound and wondrous conduct of Samantabhadra.
At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva Mahāsattva stood before the assembly and praised the great treasury of merit of Sudhana.
Having heard this, Sudhana was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; the hairs on his body all stood on end, and he rose up with tears of grief choking his voice and joined his palms.
With palms joined in reverence, he gazed up at him and circumambulated him countless times.
By the power of Mañjuśrī’s mental resolve, various flower garlands and diverse wonderful jewels suddenly filled his hands without his even realizing it.
Delighted, Sudhana immediately scattered them as an offering over the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya. Then, Maitreya Bodhisattva placed his hand upon Sudhana’s head.
He spoke in verse:
"Excellent, excellent, true son of the Buddha! Universally exerting all your faculties without weariness, Before long you shall be endowed with all virtues, Just like Mañjuśrī and myself."
Then the youth Sudhana replied in verse:
"I recall that spiritual benefactors Are difficult to encounter even in hundreds of millions of eons.
Now that I have been able to draw near them all And come into the presence of your honor, It is because of Mañjuśrī That I behold those who are so difficult to see."
That Honored One of Great Merit—may he swiftly return so that we may behold him again.
This concludes the third major section, which clarifies how Maitreya alone embodies the characteristics of the causes for attaining virtue.

That is to say, having already integrated conditions and entered into reality, he subsumes all prior virtues as the cause for attaining Buddhahood; being certain to become a Buddha, he thus relies upon one [individual].
He is born in the stage of the "Place of Rebirth" (*upapatti-sthāna*), serving as the final thought-moment (*paścima-citta*) prior to equal enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*).
This is why Maitreya’s pavilion is named the "Vairocana-Adorned Treasury. Because this stage is difficult to enter, it was previously necessary to provide extensive warnings and exhortations;

here, one should first give rise to various superior states of mind (*viśiṣṭa-citta*) when seeking instruction. Thus, after Sudhana had received the teachings of his previous spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), he went to seek counsel from Maitreya.
First, one separately generates superior mindfulness: repenting of the past and cultivating for the future. Thus it is said:
"Recalling for oneself that in the past one did not practice reverence, one immediately resolves to act with diligence," and so forth.

There are twenty-three and a half lines of scripture that examine the past faults in detail to apply their antidotes, and observe present suffering to spur oneself on against future suffering. One should contemplate and investigate in this manner.
It is so. All of this is brought about by faithfully receiving the instructions of a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*). This is a profound understanding of the exhortations of Devasena and Guṇākara.
When one meets them later, one should respectfully inquire; when one first meets them, one should rely upon their guidance.
Initially, the youth Sudhana, with such reverent observation and the power of his vows, contemplates such realms of immeasurable wisdom.
Regarding the realm: before the Great Pavilion of Vairocana’s Adorned Treasury, one briefly collects the mind and contemplates with observation.
By means of the power of great vows and profound faith and understanding, one enters the gate of the equality of the wisdom-body that pervades all places.

This initial entry into meditative concentration serves to express reverence. The Commentary states: "Collecting the mind" indicates entering into concentration; "contemplating and observing" refers to being settled in concentration.

Regarding the preparatory practice (*prayoga*): faith and aspiration are the causes of meditative concentration (*samādhi*). Below, the names and characteristics of the concentrations are explained in detail.

As for the fact that Sudhana, before seeing Maitreya, first sees the pavilion and immediately enters this concentration: the intent is to reveal that the realm of profound stages and double negation (*chongxuan*) cannot be perceived by a distracted mind;
therefore, he enters concentration to observe it. This is because he integrates the practices of all preceding stages [into this state].

Having accomplished this samādhi, it serves as the cause for entering the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*). Next, there are eight lines of further scripture stating that he universally manifests his body before all Tathāgatas;
this specifically reveals the functional activity of the samādhi. That is to say, the union of concentration and wisdom—the clarity of wisdom-concentration—is its sublime function.
Therefore, he is able to universally manifest bodies throughout the ten dharma-realms, arraying clouds of bodies [before them].
The Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*). Next, "equal to the boundless measure of empty space," etc., clarifies the true source of the Dharma-nature (*dharmatā*) to which [the practitioner] accords.
Within this single state of meditative concentration, all that Sudhana has realized upon his initial encounter with the Dharma-realm is fully revealed.

Next, "furthermore, he definitively knows all retributions" and below clarify the profound contemplation that accords with the Dharma-realm; these clarify the three contemplations that accord with the Dharma-realm.

The "Single Mind" section consists of fourteen lines of scripture, divided into three parts. First, from "Furthermore, with certainty" (*khalu punar*) down to the end of the fifth line, the remainder of the scripture clarifies that phenomena arise from conditions;

this is the contemplation of the provisional (*prajñapti-darśana*). Next, from "Free from the view of annihilation" (*uccheda-dṛṣṭi*) up to the limit of signlessness (*animitta-koṭi*), there are five lines of the remainder of the scripture;
the clear wisdom here accords with the absence of intrinsic nature (*niḥsvabhāva*); this is the contemplation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-darśana*). Next, the knowledge of the one...
All phenomena are like seeds producing sprouts; because they flow forth from skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), three lines of verse from another sutra summarize them into the Middle Way.

This then specifically clarifies the previously established characteristics. When the youth Sudhana enters such wisdom, two lines of verse from the *Sūtra on the Flowing Forth of Inconceivable Roots of Goodness* describe how his body and mind become cool, refreshing, and joyful. These two lines conclude the summary.
Furthermore, he rose from the ground and, with single-minded devotion, gazed up at [the Buddha] and circumambulated him countless times. As the light emerged, he paid homage and offered praise.
First, he circumambulated with physical reverence; next, he spoke these words with mental reverence:
"This great pavilion is the dwelling place of those who have realized emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. [The following sixty-two lines of the sutra are then cited.]
The "one who is able to dwell" refers to virtue. This praises the multi-storied pavilion (kūṭāgāra) in which he dwells;
because the first phrase fully manifests this, the term "this great multi-storied pavilion" runs through all the subsequent lines. The commentary divides this into ten sections.

In general, what is praised here concerns the virtue of practicing both the provisional and the ultimate, as well as principle and phenomena, in tandem. After Śrīmati had already spoken in prose, she further offered praise in verse. At that time, the youth Sudhana...
The son then spoke in verse. Within these verses praising the Middle Way, there are fifty-five stanzas. The first thirty-four stanzas are in seven-syllable lines;

they enumerate virtues while extolling the locus [of the teaching]. From the twenty-first stanza onward, the lines consist of five syllables; they point to specific loci while elucidating its excellence.
"Having come here now to offer worship and pay homage, I pray that you will look upon me with compassion; let this suffice.
Above, he beheld the *parivṛti* (the environment); below, he beheld the *puruṣakāra* (the primary being).
At that time, after the youth Sudhana had praised the Great Pavilion of Vairocana’s Adorned Treasury with such eulogies and hymns, he then saw Maitreya Bodhisattva emerge from another [direction].

Regarding the statement that Maitreya comes from another place: when Sudhana first visited Meghashri, they met on a separate peak, which symbolizes not abiding in the fixed positions and arising from essence to function.
Now, seeing that Maitreya—the culmination of the causal stage—comes from another place, it symbolizes the gathering of function back into essence.
This intends to reveal that throughout the five stages of cause and effect, there is nothing that does not [return to the source].
Flowing from this Dharma-realm, now that the cause has been exhausted and the fruit fulfilled, there is nowhere to which one does not return to this Dharma-realm;
thus, Maitreya came surrounded by immeasurable celestial retinues of the eight classes and countless sentient beings.
Upon seeing him, Sudhana leaped for joy and prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground. Hardly had he performed this gesture of reverence before he had yet begun to inquire.

Maitreya Bodhisattva did not wait for further questioning; having already observed from afar that Sudhana’s merits were complete, he simply pointed him out to the great assembly, extolled his virtues, and spoke these verses in praise: "Behold the conduct of Sudhana."
"With a mind purified by wisdom, you have come to me for the sake of seeking Bodhi.
Hereafter, one hundred and thirteen verses are spoken in extenso to praise the virtues of Sudhana. At the end, a single verse briefly indicates the subsequent spiritual friend, saying:
"You should go to the presence of Mañjuśrī of Great Wisdom; he shall cause you to attain Samantabhadra."
This is the wondrous practice. However, Maitreya did not wait for Sudhana to further inquire about the Dharma-gate;
rather, having finished praising him with verses, he immediately pointed out the next spiritual friend.

This intention signifies that at the ultimate stage, words are forgotten, and one should realize the wisdom-practice of the Dharma-realm in order to enter the ocean of the fruit of Sublime Enlightenment. Thus, Maitreya praised Sudhana in this manner.
Because of the power of Mañjuśrī’s mental resolve, a multitude of necklaces, flowers, and wondrous jewels suddenly filled his hands.
This symbolizes that when one perfectly accords with the awakened fruit, inconceivable function arises spontaneously;
it is realized through the forgetting of conditions. Therefore, Sudhana again scattered flowers over Maitreya. This symbolizes the non-duality of cause and fruit.
Thus, Maitreya again spoke a verse in praise of Sudhana, and Sudhana likewise replied with a verse.
This is merely the account of their initial meeting; the questions regarding the Dharma are contained in the subsequent text.
Essential Outline of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha,
Volumes 77 and 78. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda, a śramaṇa from the Kingdom of Khotan.
Commentary by the Śramaṇa Chengguan of Qingliangshan Dahuayan Monastery;
Extracted and Annotated by the Śramaṇa Deqing of Huishan Fayun Monastery.
Chapter Thirty-nine, Part Nineteen: Entering the Dharma Realm.
At that time, the youth Sudhana joined his palms in reverence and addressed Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva once more, saying:
"O Great Sage, I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct, nor how a bodhisattva should cultivate the bodhisattva path. O Great Sage, all Tathāgatas..."
The Venerable One was granted the prophecy that in one lifetime he would attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
If, in one lifetime, he were to attain unsurpassed enlightenment, then he would have already transcended all the stages where Bodhisattvas dwell;
he would have already surpassed all the Bodhisattva stages of "leaving birth" (*niyāma*); he would have already perfected all the *pāramitās*; and he would have already deeply...
They have entered all gates of patience; they have already fulfilled all bodhisattva stages;
they have already sported within all doors of liberation; they have already accomplished all dharmas of samādhi;
they have already attained mastery in all bodhisattva practices; they have already realized all dhāraṇīs and eloquence; and they have already [perfected] all bodhisattvas...
Having attained mastery within mastery, one has already accumulated all the factors conducive to enlightenment for bodhisattvas;
one has already sported in wisdom and skillful means; one has already brought forth the knowledge of great supernormal powers;
one has already accomplished all rules of training; one has already perfected all sublime conduct; and one has already fulfilled all great vows. Thus, one has already...
Having received the predictions of all Buddhas, they have already fully understood the gateways of all vehicles;
they have already become worthy of being protected and remembered by all Tathāgatas; they have already been able to expound the bodhi of all Buddhas;
they have already been able to uphold the treasury of all Buddha-dharmas; they have already been able to uphold the secret treasury of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; they have already...
One who is able to be the foremost among all the assemblies of bodhisattvas has already become a great heroic general capable of destroying the army of the māra of afflictions;
has already become a great guide capable of leading others out of the wilderness of birth and death;
has already become a great king of physicians capable of treating the grave illnesses of all delusions; and has already become the most supreme among all sentient beings.
Having already attained mastery among all world-lords, one has thereby become the foremost among all noble ones;
having already become the most preeminent among all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, one has thereby become a helmsman within the ocean of birth and death;
and one has thereby been able to cast the net for the subduing of all sentient beings. Thus...
Having already been able to observe the faculties of all sentient beings, one has thereby already been able to encompass the realm of all sentient beings;
one has thereby already been able to protect the assembly of all bodhisattvas; one has thereby already been able to discuss all matters concerning bodhisattvas;
one has thereby already been able to go to the abodes of all Tathāgatas; one has thereby already been able to dwell in the assemblies of all Tathāgatas; one has thereby already been able—
Manifesting before all sentient beings, one is already able to remain unstained by all worldly dharmas;
one is already able to transcend all realms of Māra; one is already able to dwell securely in the realm of all Buddhas;
one is already able to reach the unimpeded state of all Bodhisattvas; one is already able to diligently make offerings to all Buddhas.

Having attained the same essential nature as all Buddhas, having bound the silken ribbon of the sublime Dharma, having received the Buddha’s consecration, having abided in omniscience, having been able to universally produce all Buddha-dharmas, and having been able to swiftly tread upon the station of omniscience—O Great Sage, how should a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct?
How should they cultivate the bodhisattva path? In accordance with what they have cultivated...
One will swiftly learn to fully realize all Buddha-dharmas; be able to deliver and liberate all sentient beings one contemplates;
universally fulfill all great vows that have been made; universally bring to ultimate completion all practices that have been initiated;
universally comfort all devas and humans; not fail oneself; not sever the Three Jewels; not render the lineage of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in vain; and be able to uphold [the Dharma].
"Please explain for us all such matters as these, which are the eye of the Dharma of all Buddhas.
At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva surveyed the entire assembly at the site of enlightenment, pointed toward Sudhana, and spoke these words:
"O virtuous ones, do you see this son of a householder who is now inquiring of me regarding the various merits of the bodhisattva practices?"
"O virtuous ones, this son of a householder is courageous and diligent; his aspirations are unadulterated, his profound resolve is firm, and he never regresses.

Possessing superior hope, he is like one whose hair is on fire—never finding satisfaction—and he delights in approaching and making offerings to spiritual friends, seeking them out everywhere to serve and request the Dharma from them. O virtuous ones, in the past, this son of a householder..."
Having received the instructions of Mañjuśrī in the City of Blessings (Puṇyavatī), he traveled southward in succession to seek spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra).
After passing through one hundred and ten spiritual friends, he finally came to my place, never for a moment giving rise to a thought of weariness or indolence.
"O virtuous ones, this son of a householder is truly rare. He is intent upon the Great Vehicle and mounted upon great wisdom;
he has aroused great valor and donned the armor of great compassion. With a mind of great loving-kindness, he rescues and protects sentient beings.

He initiates the practice of the perfection of great diligence, acts as a great caravan leader to protect all beings, and serves as a great Dharma-ship to cross over the ocean of existence. He dwells...
In the Great Path, he gathers the great Dharma-treasures and cultivates all the vast dharmas that assist the path.
Such a person is difficult to hear of, difficult to see, and difficult to approach, dwell with, or practice alongside. Why is this?
Because this son of a householder has resolved his mind to rescue and protect all sentient beings, causing all sentient beings to be liberated from all sufferings and to transcend them.

They leave behind all evil realms; they depart from all perils and difficulties; they shatter the darkness of ignorance; they emerge from the wilderness of birth and death; they stifle all discursive talk of the various destinies and transcend the realm of Māra;
they do not cling to worldly dharmas; they emerge from the mire of desire; they sever the yoke of greed; they untie the bonds of views; and they demolish the dwelling of marks.
He cuts off the path of delusion, topples the banner of pride, pulls out the arrows of confusion, removes the veil of sleep, tears asunder the net of craving, extinguishes ignorance,
crosses over the stream of existence, leaves behind flattery and illusion, purifies the stains of the mind, severs folly and doubt, and brings forth liberation from birth and death. O virtuous ones,
this son of a householder has constructed a great Dharma-ship for those being swept away by the four floods, and he has established a great [raft] for those submerged in the mud of false views.
He is a bridge of Dharma for those shrouded in the darkness of ignorance and delusion, lighting the lamp of great wisdom for them.

He reveals the Noble Path for those wandering through the wilderness of birth and death. He prepares the medicinal elixir of Dharma for those afflicted by the grave illness of the afflictions (*kleśa*).

He gives the nectar of immortality to those suffering the pains of birth, old age, and death, causing them to find peace and security. And for those who have entered the fires of greed, hatred, and delusion, he pours upon them the water of meditative concentration (*samādhi*).
It makes water cool and refreshing. It consoles and comforts those with much sorrow and affliction. It instructs and exhorts those bound in the prison of existence so that they may emerge.

It opens with the sword of wisdom those who have entered the net of views. It shows the gates of liberation to those dwelling in the cities of the realms. It guides those in perilous difficulties to places of safety.
It bestows the dharma of fearlessness upon those who dread the thieves of the fetters. And it grants compassion to those fallen into the evil destinies.
For those whose hands grasp the aggregates that cause harm, he shows the city of Nirvāṇa; for those entwined by the serpents of the elements, he liberates them through the Noble Path;
for those attached to the empty village of the six sense bases, he draws them out with the light of wisdom; for those dwelling in false salvation, he causes them to enter true salvation;

for those who associate with evil friends, he points out virtuous friends; for those who delight in mundane dharmas, he instructs them in the Noble Dharma; and for those attached to birth and death...
He causes them to enter the city of omniscience. O noble ones, this son of a householder constantly protects sentient beings through such practices;
he never ceases to resolve upon bodhicitta, and he is never weary in seeking the path of the Mahāyāna.

They drink the waters of all dharmas without ever becoming weary or satisfied; they constantly and diligently accumulate the practices that assist the path; they always delight in purifying all dharma-gates;
they cultivate the conduct of a bodhisattva without forsaking diligence; and they fulfill all vows through skillful means in virtuous practice.
One views spiritual friends with insatiable devotion; one serves spiritual friends without physical weariness or indolence;
and having heard all the instructions of spiritual friends, one always delights in practicing them in accordance with them, never contravening them.
O virtuous ones, if there are sentient beings who can resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, this is truly rare. Furthermore, once they have resolved their minds [upon it]...
To be able to thus apply diligent skillful means to gather all Buddha-dharmas is doubly rare.
Furthermore, one can thus seek the bodhisattva path; furthermore, one can thus purify the bodhisattva conduct; furthermore, one can thus serve spiritual friends;
furthermore, one can thus act as if one’s head were on fire; furthermore, one can thus comply with the instructions of spiritual friends; furthermore, one can thus remain steadfast.
He firmly practices the path; furthermore, he is able to thus gather the factors conducive to enlightenment (*bodhipakṣa-dharma*);
he is able to thus not seek any fame, profit, or sustenance; he is able to thus not abandon the singular, pure mind of a bodhisattva;

and he is able to thus take no pleasure in the household life, have no attachment to sensual desires, and feel no longing for parents, relatives, or acquaintances, but instead delights only in seeking awakening.
Together with their companions, they are furthermore able to disregard their own bodies and lives, wishing only to diligently cultivate the path to omniscience.

You should know that this is successively even more difficult to attain. O virtuous ones, other bodhisattvas must pass through immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of kalpas before they can fulfill the vows and practices of a bodhisattva, and before they can draw near to the Buddhas.
Bodhi. Within a single lifetime, this son of a householder will be able to purify Buddha-fields; he will be able to transform sentient beings;
he will be able to penetrate the dharma-realm with wisdom; he will be able to accomplish all the pāramitās;
he will be able to expand all practices; he will be able to fulfill all great vows; and he will be able to transcend all māras.
...one will then be able to serve all virtuous friends, purify the path of all Bodhisattvas, and fulfill the practices of Samantabhadra.

At that time, after Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva had thus praised the various merits of the youth Sudhana and inspired immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings to resolve upon Bodhicitta, he addressed Sudhana:

Vasu said: "Excellent, excellent, noble son! It is for the benefit of all the world, for the protection of all sentient beings, and for the diligent pursuit of all Buddha-dharmas that you have resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Noble son, you have obtained a sublime gain; you have well attained a human body; you dwell well in this life."
I declare to you: you have encountered the appearance of a Tathāgata most auspiciously; you have beheld the great spiritual friend Mañjuśrī most auspiciously.
Your body is a vessel of goodness, moistened by all roots of merit, and sustained by the pure dharmas.
All their desires have been completely purified; they are protected and remembered by all the Buddhas, and they are embraced by virtuous friends.
Why is this? Good son, the bodhicitta is like a seed, for it can give rise to all the qualities of a Buddha.
The bodhicitta is like a fertile field, for it can cause the pure virtues of sentient beings to grow.
Because of the Dharma, the bodhicitta is like the great earth, for it can support all worlds.
The bodhicitta is like pure water, for it can wash away the stains of all afflictions.
The bodhicitta is like a great wind, for it is unimpeded throughout the world. The bodhicitta is like a blazing fire, for it can burn...
Because it is the firewood for all views, the bodhicitta is like the pure sun, for it universally illumines all worlds.
The bodhicitta is like the full moon, for all pure and white dharmas are therein perfected.
The bodhicitta is like a bright lamp, for it can emit the various radiances of the Dharma. The bodhicitta is like...
The pure eye, because it universally perceives all places of safety and peril. The bodhicitta is like a great highway, because it causes all to enter the city of great wisdom.
The bodhicitta is like a correct ferry, because it enables one to leave behind all erroneous dharmas.
The bodhicitta is like a great vehicle, because it is universally able to transport all bodhisattvas.
The mind is like a gateway, for it opens up and reveals all bodhisattva practices.
The bodhicitta is like a palace, for it provides a secure dwelling for the cultivation of samādhi.
The bodhicitta is like a garden, for therein one sports and enjoys the bliss of the Dharma. The bodhicitta is like a home, for it brings peace and security to all beings.
Because it is that which gives birth, the bodhicitta is the place of refuge, for it benefits all worlds.
Because it is the basis for the practices of all bodhisattvas, the bodhicitta is the foundation.
Because it instructs and guides all bodhisattvas, the bodhicitta is like a compassionate father. Because it causes them to grow, the bodhicitta is like a compassionate mother.
Because it is for the sake of all bodhisattvas, the bodhicitta is like a wet nurse, for it nurtures and raises all bodhisattvas.
The bodhicitta is like a virtuous friend, for it brings benefit and fulfillment to all bodhisattvas.
The bodhicitta is like a sovereign ruler, for it surpasses all those of the two vehicles. The bodhicitta is like...
The Bodhicitta is like a sovereign king, for it attains mastery over all aspirations.
The Bodhicitta is like the great ocean, for all virtues enter into it. The Bodhicitta is like Mount Sumeru, for its mind is impartial toward all sentient beings.
The Bodhicitta is like the Iron Ring Mountains (Cakravāḍa), for it sustains and upholds all worlds.
The mind is like the Snowy Mountains, for it nurtures all medicinal herbs of wisdom.
The bodhicitta is like the Fragrant Mountain, for it gives rise to the fragrance of all meritorious qualities.
The bodhicitta is like space, for its sublime virtues are vast and boundless. The bodhicitta is like a lotus flower, for it is unstained by anything in the world.
Because of the Dharma: the bodhicitta is like a well-trained intelligent elephant, for its mind is well-disciplined and not fierce or unruly.
The bodhicitta is like a noble and good horse, for it is far removed from all evil natures.
The bodhicitta is like a charioteer, for it protects all the teachings of the Mahāyāna. The bodhicitta is like excellent medicine, for it can cure...
Because it is the remedy for all the diseases of affliction, the bodhicitta is like a pitfall, for it causes all unwholesome dharmas to fall into it.
The bodhicitta is like a vajra, for it is able to pierce through all dharmas.
The bodhicitta is like a casket of incense, for it can store the fragrance of all merits. The bodhicitta is like...
The wondrous flower, for it is that which all the world delights to behold. The bodhicitta is like white sandalwood, for it removes the heat of all desires and brings about refreshing coolness.
The bodhicitta is like black agarwood, for it perfumes the entire dharma-realm, pervading it everywhere.
The bodhicitta is like the sovereign medicine Suvīra, for it can destroy the disease of all afflictions. The bodhicitta...
The bodhicitta is like the *vighuṣma* medicine, for it can extract all the arrows of affliction.
The bodhicitta is like Śakra, for it is the most honored among all lords. The bodhicitta is like Vaiśravaṇa.
Because it can sever all suffering of poverty, the bodhicitta is like the goddess Guṇakāśikā;
because it is adorned with all merits, the bodhicitta is like an ornament that adorns all bodhisattvas.
The bodhicitta is like the fire at the end of an eon, for it can incinerate all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛta*).
The bodhicitta is like the rootless medicinal herb, for it nurtures and develops all the qualities of a Buddha (*buddhadharma*).
The bodhicitta is like the dragon’s jewel, for it can neutralize the poison of all afflictions (*kleśa*). The bodhicitta is like the water-purifying gem, for it can clarify...
Because it cuts through all turbidities of affliction, the bodhicitta is like a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*), for it can provide for all who are impoverished.
The bodhicitta is like a vase of merit (*bhadraghaṭa*), for it satisfies the minds of all sentient beings.
The bodhicitta is like a wish-fulfilling tree (*kalpavṛkṣa*), for it can rain down all manner of ornaments. The bodhicitta is like a *haṃsa*...

The feather garment (*kṣaumapaṭa*), because it is untainted by all the defilements of birth and death. The bodhicitta is like white cotton thread, because its nature has been pure from the very beginning.
The bodhicitta is like a sharp plow, because it can cultivate the fields of all sentient beings.
The bodhicitta is like Nārāyaṇa, because it can destroy the enemy of all views of self (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*). The bodhicitta...
The mind is like a swift arrow, for it can shatter all sufferings. The bodhicitta is like a sharp spear, for it can pierce the armor of all afflictions.
The bodhicitta is like sturdy armor, for it can secure all minds that accord with reality. The bodhicitta is like a sharp sword, for it can sever all afflictions.
Because it is the head [of all virtues], the bodhicitta is like a sharp sword, for it can sever the armor of all pride.
The bodhicitta is like the banner of a valiant general, for it can subdue all the armies of Māra.
The bodhicitta is like a sharp saw, for it can cut through the tree of ignorance. The bodhicitta is like a sharp axe, for it can fell...
Because it is the root of all trees of suffering, the bodhicitta is like a weapon, for it can ward off all hardships and misfortunes.
The bodhicitta is like a skillful hand, for it protects and upholds the body of all perfections (pāramitās).
The bodhicitta is like excellent feet, for it establishes all roots of merit. The bodhicitta is like...
The medicinal eye-salve, because it eliminates all cataracts of ignorance. The bodhicitta is like a pair of tongs, because it can extract the thorns of the view of a self-identity.
The bodhicitta is like a bed, because it pacifies and removes all the weariness and suffering of birth and death.
The bodhicitta is like a virtuous friend, because it can untie all the bonds of birth and death. The bodhicitta...
The mind is like precious wealth, for it can eliminate all causes of poverty.
The bodhicitta is like a great guide, for it well knows the path of the bodhisattva’s definitive departure.
The bodhicitta is like a hidden treasure, for it yields a wealth of merit without exhaustion. The bodhicitta is like a gushing spring, for it produces the water of wisdom without end.
Because it is exhaustive. The bodhicitta is like a clear mirror, for it universally manifests the images of all dharma-gates.
The bodhicitta is like a lotus flower, for it is unstained by any defilement of sin.
The bodhicitta is like a great river, for it flows and draws forth all dharmas of deliverance and gathering. The bodhicitta is like a great nāga king, for it can rain down...
Because it rains down all sublime dharmas, the bodhicitta is like the life-faculty (*jīvitendriya*), for it sustains the body of a bodhisattva’s great compassion.
The bodhicitta is like nectar (*amṛta*), for it enables one to abide in the realm of immortality.
The bodhicitta is like a great net, for it universally gathers in all sentient beings. The bodhicitta is like...
The lasso, because it gathers in all those who are to be converted. The bodhicitta is like a hook and bait, because it draws out those dwelling within the abyss of existence.
The bodhicitta is like the agada medicine, because it can bring about illness-free and eternal peace.
The bodhicitta is like an antidote to poison, because it can completely eliminate the poison of craving and attachment. The bodhicitta...
The bodhicitta is like a well-recited mantra, for it can eliminate the poison of all perversions.

The bodhicitta is like a swift wind, for it can sweep away the mists of all hindrances. The bodhicitta is like a great island of jewels, for it gives birth to all the jewels of the factors of enlightenment (*bodhipakṣa*).
The bodhicitta is like a noble lineage of seeds, for it gives birth to all that is pure.
Because it purifies all phenomena, the bodhicitta is like a dwelling, for it is the locus upon which all virtuous qualities depend.
The bodhicitta is like a marketplace, for it is the place where Bodhisattvas, like merchants, conduct their trade.
The bodhicitta is like an elixir for refining gold, for it can purify the stains of all afflictions. The bodhicitta is like excellent honey, for it is perfectly...
Because it fulfills the flavor of all merits, the bodhicitta is like a correct path;
because it causes all bodhisattvas to enter the city of wisdom, the bodhicitta is like a fine vessel;
because it can sustain all pure and white dharmas, the bodhicitta is like a timely rain; because it can extinguish the dust of all afflictions, the bodhicitta is...
It is the dwelling place, for it is the abode where all bodhisattvas reside. The bodhicitta is the life-force, for it does not grasp at the fruit of liberation of the śrāvakas.
The bodhicitta is like pure lapis lazuli, for its intrinsic nature is luminous and stainless.
The bodhicitta is like the sapphire, for it transcends the worldly wisdom of the two vehicles. The bodhicitta...
The awakening mind is like the drum that strikes the watches of the night, for it awakens all sentient beings from the sleep of afflictions.
The awakening mind is like pure water, for its nature is inherently clear and stainless, free from turbidity.
The awakening mind is like Jambu-river gold, for it outshines all conditioned virtues. The awakening mind is like the king of great mountains, for it rises above all...
Because it is for the sake of the world, the bodhicitta is that to which one returns;
because it does not reject any who come to it. The bodhicitta is beneficial, as it can eliminate all afflictions.
The bodhicitta is a sublime jewel, as it can cause all minds to rejoice. The bodhicitta is like a great assembly of giving, for it fills...
Because it fulfills the hearts of all sentient beings, the bodhicitta is most honored and supreme; for no other sentient being’s mind can equal it.
The bodhicitta is like a hidden treasure, for it can encompass all the qualities of a Buddha.
The bodhicitta is like Indra’s net, for it can subdue the asuras of the afflictions. The bodhicitta...
Like the wind of Varuṇa, it is able to move all that is to be transformed.
The bodhicitta is like the fire of Indra, for it can burn away all afflictions and habitual tendencies.
The bodhicitta is like a stūpa of the Buddha, for it should be venerated by all the world. Noble son, the bodhicitta accomplishes such immeasurable merits.
Virtue. To state the essentials: one should know that it is entirely equal to all the qualities of the Buddha-dharma. Why is this?
Because all bodhisattva practices are born from the bodhicitta, and the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time are born from the bodhicitta.
Therefore, son of good family, if there is anyone who generates the resolve for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*...
One who maintains the mind has already produced immeasurable merit and is universally able to encompass the path to omniscience.
Good son, it is like a person who obtains the medicine of fearlessness and is freed from five terrors. What are these five? Namely:
fire cannot burn them; poison cannot affect them; blades cannot wound them; water cannot sweep them away; and smoke cannot suffocate them.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this. Having obtained the medicine of the bodhicitta of omniscience, they are not burned by the fire of greed, not struck by the poison of anger, not wounded by the sword of delusion, and not swept away by the currents of existence. The smoke of discursive thought and observation cannot pollute or harm them.
Good son, it is as if there were a person who, having obtained the medicine of liberation, would never encounter untimely calamities. So it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
The Bodhisattva is also like this. Having obtained the medicinal drug of the wisdom of liberation through the bodhicitta, they are forever free from all the calamities of birth and death.
Good son, it is as if there were a person who holds the mahā-aṅgada medicine; upon smelling its scent, venomous snakes immediately flee far away.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this; holding the great aṅgada medicine of the bodhicitta, [all afflictions depart].
All afflictions and evil poisonous snakes, upon smelling its fragrance, are entirely dispersed and extinguished.
Good son, it is like a person who holds the "Invincible Medicine" (Ajeya-bhaiṣajya); no enemy whatsoever can overcome them. The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this:
holding the "Invincible Medicine" of the bodhicitta, they are able to subdue all the armies of Māra. Well said!
"Son of good family, it is just as if there were a person who, by holding the *vighuṣṭa* medicine, could cause poisonous arrows to fall away of their own accord.
In the same way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva, by holding the *vighuṣṭa* medicine of the bodhicitta, causes the arrows of greed, hatred, delusion, and all false views to fall away of their own accord.
Son of good family, it is just as if there were a person who, by holding the *sudarśana* medicine..."

In the same way, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva likewise possesses the medicinal king of the well-seen *bodhicitta*, which completely eliminates all diseases of the afflictions (*kleśa*). Good son, it is like a medicinal tree named Saṃdhana;
if one takes its bark and applies it to a wound, the wound is immediately healed, yet the bark of that tree [continues to grow] as before.

Even if one were to take [its fruit] throughout successive lifetimes, it could never be exhausted. It is just so with the tree of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) that grows from the bodhicitta of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.

If there are those who see it and give rise to faith, the wounds of their afflictions (*kleśa*) and karma will all be eliminated, yet the tree of omniscience suffers no loss whatsoever. Good son, it is like a medicinal tree named "Rootless" (*amūla*).

By its power, it causes all the trees of Jambudvīpa to grow. In the same way, the Bodhicitta-tree of the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva likewise causes all the wholesome dharmas of those in training (śaikṣa), those beyond training (aśaikṣa), and all bodhisattvas to grow.
Good son, it is like a medicine named Ālambā; if it is applied to the body...
Both body and mind become fully capable; it is just so with the bodhicitta-āraṇava medicine obtained by a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, which causes their body and mind to increase in wholesome dharmas.

Good son, it is like a person who obtains the medicine of the power of mindfulness, whereby they remember and do not forget whatever they hear. So it is with the bodhisattva-mahāsattva who obtains the bodhicitta.
The power of mindfulness is a sublime medicine; it enables one to hear and retain all Buddha-dharmas without ever forgetting them.
Good son, it is like a medicine named Great Lotus (*mahāpadma*); whoever consumes it dwells for the duration of an eon.
It is the same for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva who consumes the Great Lotus medicine of the bodhicitta: throughout incalculable eons, they attain mastery over their lifespan.
Good son, it is like a person who possesses a medicinal drug that renders one invisible; neither humans nor non-humans can see them.
In the same way, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva possesses the wondrous invisibility-elixir of the bodhicitta, none of the māras can see them.
"Good son, it is like the jewel in the ocean called 'Universal Gatherer of All Treasures.
If this jewel remains, even if the fires at the end of an eon were to burn and consume the world, there is no possibility that these oceans could be diminished by so much as a single drop.
The jewel of the bodhicitta of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is likewise; when it dwells within the great ocean of the Bodhisattva’s vows, if one constantly recollects it..."
Maintain it so that you do not let it fall away or be lost. It is simply impossible for anything to destroy even a single root of goodness in a bodhisattva;
